01-12.title: Haiti Earthquake
01-12.description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck near Port-au-Prince, devastating the capital and surrounding areas. An estimated 220,000 people were killed and over 300,000 injured.

01-26.title: Gujarat (Bhuj) Earthquake
01-26.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Bhuj in Kutch district on India's Republic Day, killing about 20,000 people and injuring more than 160,000 according to official figures. It was India's deadliest earthquake in half a century, destroying or damaging roughly a million buildings across Gujarat.

02-14.title: Pulwama attack
02-14.description: A suicide bomber rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into a convoy of the Central Reserve Police Force on the Srinagar-Jammu highway near Pulwama on 14 February 2019. Forty CRPF personnel were killed and dozens wounded in the deadliest attack on Indian security forces in Kashmir in decades. The Pakistan-based militant group Jaish-e-Mohammed claimed responsibility, and the attack triggered a major military escalation between India and Pakistan that included an Indian airstrike at Balakot and an aerial engagement between the two air forces.

02-14.title: Parkland School Shooting
02-14.description: A gunman opened fire at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School, killing 17 people and injuring 17 others. The shooting sparked a nationwide student-led movement for gun control.

02-14.title: Sunjiawan coal mine explosion
02-14.description: A gas explosion at the state-owned Sunjiawan coal mine in Fuxin, Liaoning Province, killed 214 miners and injured 30. The blast occurred about 240 metres underground while 574 miners were working the shaft, making it China's deadliest mining disaster in 15 years.

03-11.title: Jaffar Express hijacking
03-11.description: On March 11, 2025, Balochistan Liberation Army militants stopped the Jaffar Express near Sibi in Balochistan, Pakistan, hijacking roughly 400 passengers inside a railway tunnel and executing many during a standoff that lasted into the next day; at least 64 people were killed, including 33 militants and 31 civilians and security personnel, before security forces killed the remaining attackers and freed 354 hostages.

03-11.title: Tohoku earthquake, tsunami and Fukushima disaster
03-11.description: A magnitude 9.0 earthquake struck off the Pacific coast of Japan on March 11, 2011, generating a massive tsunami that inundated the northeastern coastline. Waves up to 40 metres high destroyed entire towns in Iwate, Miyagi and Fukushima prefectures, and the tsunami caused a nuclear meltdown at the Fukushima Daiichi power plant. Japan's National Police Agency final figures record 19,759 deaths and 2,553 missing, with most victims drowned by the tsunami; the majority of the deceased were over 60 years old.

03-11.title: Winnenden School Shooting
03-11.description: On March 11, 2009, 17-year-old former student Tim Kretschmer opened fire at the Albertville-Realschule secondary school in Winnenden, Germany, killing 9 students and 3 teachers. After fleeing, he killed a passerby and two more people at a car dealership in nearby Wendlingen before being shot dead, for a total of 16 dead including the gunman. It was Germany's deadliest school shooting since the 2002 Erfurt massacre.

03-11.title: Madrid Train Bombings
03-11.description: Coordinated bombings on four commuter trains during morning rush hour killed 193 people and wounded approximately 2,000. The deadliest terrorist attack in Spanish history.

03-11.title: Barakova coal mine explosion
03-11.description: A methane gas explosion at the Barakova coal mine killed 80 miners. Ukraine's worst mining disaster since independence.

03-15.title: Christchurch Mosque Shootings
03-15.description: A gunman attacked two mosques during Friday prayers, killing 51 people and injuring 40. The attack was live-streamed. New Zealand subsequently banned most semi-automatic weapons.

03-15.title: Syrian uprising and government crackdown
03-15.description: Pro-democracy protests inspired by the Arab Spring began in the city of Daraa in mid-March 2011 and spread across Syria, where they were met with a violent government crackdown involving live fire, tanks, mass arrests and torture. The unrest progressively militarized into an armed insurgency as army defectors formed the Free Syrian Army in July. By December 13, 2011, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay reported that more than 5,000 people, including over 300 children, had been killed in the uprising.

03-24.title: Russian Invasion of Ukraine — Start of Full-Scale War
03-24.description: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the largest conventional military attack in Europe since World War II. Tens of thousands of civilians and soldiers have been killed, and millions displaced.

04-15.title: Sudan civil war begins
04-15.description: Fighting erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces paramilitary group in Khartoum and other cities, escalating into a nationwide civil war. The conflict spread to Darfur and Kordofan, where reports documented ethnically targeted violence, and displaced over 7 million people within Sudan by the end of the year. Conflict monitoring group ACLED estimated that more than 12,000 people were killed in Sudan during 2023, and the UN declared the country's humanitarian situation among the world's worst.

04-15.title: Boston Marathon Bombing
04-15.description: Two pressure-cooker bombs exploded near the finish line of the Boston Marathon, killing 3 people and injuring 264. An ensuing manhunt paralyzed the Boston area for days.

04-15.title: Air China Flight 129 crash
04-15.description: Air China Flight 129, a Boeing 767 flying from Beijing to Busan, crashed into a hillside while approaching Gimhae Airport in heavy weather during a go-around. All 129 people on board were killed.

04-24.title: Rana Plaza factory collapse
04-24.description: On April 24, 2013, the eight-story Rana Plaza commercial building in Savar, near Dhaka, Bangladesh, collapsed, killing 1,134 people and injuring about 2,500 in the deadliest garment-factory disaster in history. Thousands of garment workers had been ordered to return to work despite visible cracks in the building the day before; the collapse prompted international scrutiny and reform agreements within the apparel industry's supply chain.

05-12.title: Kabul maternity hospital attack
05-12.description: On 12 May 2020, three gunmen wearing police uniforms stormed the MSF-supported maternity ward of Atatürk Children's Hospital in Kabul's predominantly Hazara Dashte Barchi neighborhood. The attackers killed 24 people, including 16 mothers, two small children and a midwife, and wounded 16 others before being killed by Afghan and Norwegian special forces. No group claimed the hospital attack; the Afghan government blamed the Taliban, while the United States later assessed that Islamic State Khorasan was responsible.

05-12.title: Nepal earthquake aftershock
05-12.description: A magnitude 7.3 aftershock struck Nepal east of Kathmandu less than three weeks after the Gorkha earthquake, killing at least 218 people, most of them in the Sindhupalchok and Dolakha districts, and injuring more than 3,500. The quake triggered fresh avalanches and building collapses in a country where millions were still living in temporary shelter.

05-12.title: Wenchuan earthquake (Sichuan earthquake)
05-12.description: A magnitude 7.9 (Mw, USGS) / 8.0 (Ms, CEA) earthquake struck Wenchuan County in Sichuan Province at 14:28 local time on 12 May 2008, collapsing schools, factories, and villages across mountainous western Sichuan and damaging areas over 500,000 square kilometers. China's State Council Information Office confirmed 69,227 dead, 17,923 missing, and about 374,000 injured, for a combined total of roughly 87,000 dead or missing; over 15 million people were evacuated and 5 million left homeless. It was China's most destructive earthquake since 1949.

05-12.title: Znamenskoye truck bombing
05-12.description: Suicide bombers drove an explosives-laden truck into the government administration compound in Znamenskoye, northern Chechnya, destroying the local FSB headquarters and killing about 59 people, including children. It was one of the deadliest attacks of the Chechen conflict, later claimed by rebel commander Shamil Basayev.

05-12.title: Riyadh compound bombings
05-12.description: Al-Qaeda suicide bombers attacked three foreign residential compounds in Riyadh with car bombs, killing 35 people including nine Americans and wounding more than 160. The attacks marked the beginning of a militant campaign inside Saudi Arabia.

05-24.title: Uvalde School Shooting
05-24.description: A gunman killed 19 children and 2 teachers at Robb Elementary School. Police waited over an hour before entering the classroom. The deadliest school shooting in Texas history.

06-12.title: Air India Flight 171 crash
06-12.description: On June 12, 2025, Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner bound for London, crashed into the student hostels of B. J. Medical College in Ahmedabad about 32 seconds after takeoff and 1.7 km from the airport; 241 of the 242 people on board and 19 people on the ground were killed, in the first fatal accident involving a Boeing 787.

06-12.title: Orlando Pulse nightclub shooting
06-12.description: A gunman armed with a semiautomatic rifle and pistol opened fire at the Pulse nightclub in Orlando, Florida, during its weekly Latin night, killing 49 people and wounding 53 others before police killed him after a three-hour hostage standoff. The attack was the deadliest mass shooting by a single gunman in U.S. history at the time. The shooter, Omar Mateen, pledged allegiance to Islamic State during the attack.

06-12.title: Camp Speicher Massacre
06-12.description: On 12 June 2014, days after capturing the city of Tikrit, fighters of the Islamic State group captured and systematically executed hundreds of unarmed Iraqi Air Force cadets from Camp Speicher military base. Iraqi authorities put the death toll at about 1,700, while human rights investigators documented at least several hundred victims in mass graves. The United Nations described the massacre as a war crime and possible crime against humanity.

07-31.title: IRGC claims retaliatory strike on US base in Kuwait amid Iran war
07-31.description: On July 31, 2026, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it had targeted a US base in Kuwait in retaliation for American strikes on Iran, after an earlier Iranian attack on a building in Kuwait housing a Chinese company had killed one person the previous day. The strikes were part of the sharp escalation of the 2026 Iran war following the resumption of US bombardment of IRGC targets in Iran on July 29; no further casualty figures for the Kuwait attack had been released at the time of reporting.

07-31.title: Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh
07-31.description: Ismail Haniyeh, political leader of Hamas, was killed in Tehran by a projectile strike on his residence during the Israel–Hamas war, disrupting ceasefire negotiations.

07-31.title: Kaohsiung Gas Explosions
07-31.description: A series of underground gas explosions ripped through streets in Kaohsiung, killing 32 people and injuring over 300. The blasts were caused by leaking propylene gas in sewer systems.

07-31.title: Flash floods and landslides in Dien Bien Province
07-31.description: Flash floods and landslides struck Dien Bien Province in the early hours of 1 August local time, killing at least 10 people and injuring seven. The disaster damaged homes and roads in Tia Dinh and Xa Dung communes and isolated several villages; heavy rain also flooded parts of Son La Province.

07-31.title: Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv
07-31.description: Russian forces launched a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv shortly after midnight on 1 August local time, killing at least nine people and injuring more than 20, including children. Fires broke out across four districts and rescue operations continued through the night.

07-31.title: Terrorist attack on labourers in Kulgam
07-31.description: Unidentified terrorists opened fire on two labourers from Chhattisgarh at a brick kiln in Kulgam district, killing one and injuring the other. Authorities said the attack targeted non-local workers.

07-31.title: Calabar flood and landslide crisis
07-31.description: Weeks of torrential rain in July 2026 caused flooding and landslides across Calabar, killing at least 10 people, including a baby swept away by floodwater and a father buried in mud. The rains destroyed homes, triggered landslides that killed families, and cut off access roads; the toll was cumulative through the end of July.

07-31.title: Apartment building fire kills four in Changsha
07-31.description: A fire broke out at 03:54 local time on 1 August at a high-rise residential building in the Poly Lugu Linyu compound, Yuelu District, Changsha, killing four people and injuring two. Firefighters rescued six people from the building, but four later died of their injuries in hospital.

07-07.title: Dallas police ambush
07-07.description: During a protest in downtown Dallas over the police shootings of Alton Sterling in Louisiana and Philando Castile in Minnesota, a lone gunman opened fire on responding officers, killing five officers and wounding nine others plus two civilians. The attacker, Micah Johnson, was killed by an explosive delivered by a police robot after a lengthy standoff, in the deadliest single attack on U.S. law enforcement since September 11, 2001.

07-07.title: Krasnodar Krai flash floods
07-07.description: Overnight on 6-7 July 2012, torrential rain triggered flash floods in the Krasnodar region of southern Russia. The flood wave hit the town of Krymsk around 2 a.m. while most residents slept, killing 171 people, the great majority in Krymsk, with additional deaths in Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk.

07-07.title: Indian embassy bombing in Kabul
07-07.description: A suicide car bomber rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the gates of the Indian embassy in Kabul on the morning of 7 July 2008, killing 58 people and wounding about 140, most of them Afghan civilians queuing for visas. Among the dead were four Indian embassy staff, including the defence attaché and press counsellor, six Afghan police officers, and reportedly eight schoolchildren. The attack, blamed on elements of the Afghan Taliban and Pakistan-based militant networks, was one of the deadliest in Kabul during the war.

07-07.title: London bombings (7/7)
07-07.description: Four coordinated suicide bombings struck three London Underground trains and a double-decker bus at Tavistock Square during the morning rush hour, killing 52 commuters and injuring more than 770. It was the deadliest terrorist attack on British soil since the 1988 Lockerbie bombing.

07-22.title: Munich Olympia shopping mall shooting
07-22.description: An 18-year-old gunman opened fire at the Olympia-Einkaufszentrum shopping mall and a nearby McDonald's in Munich, killing nine people and wounding 35 before killing himself with a gunshot to the head. The attacker, David Sonboly, had right-wing extremist sympathies and had been treated for mental illness; it was Germany's deadliest shooting in decades. Police initially treated the incident as a possible terror attack but concluded it was not Islamist-related.

07-22.title: Norway terror attacks (Oslo bombing and Utoya massacre)
07-22.description: On July 22, 2011, a car bomb exploded outside government buildings in Oslo, killing 8 people, and roughly two hours later a gunman opened fire at a summer camp on Utoya island run by the governing Labour Party's youth wing, killing 69 people, most of them teenagers. The perpetrator, Anders Behring Breivik, was arrested on the island and later convicted and sentenced to 21 years in an extended prison sentence. With 77 dead, it was the deadliest attack in Norway since World War II.

08-04.title: Beirut Port Explosion
08-04.description: A massive explosion at the Port of Beirut, caused by improperly stored ammonium nitrate, devastated large parts of the city. At least 218 people were killed and over 7,000 injured.

08-04.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Moscow region kills five
08-04.description: A Ukrainian drone strike on an industrial zone in Novoselki near Chekhov, outside Moscow, started fires at an industrial site and killed five people, wounding at least six others, Moscow Region Governor Andrei Vorobyov said. The attack was part of an escalation of long-range drone strikes exchanged between Russia and Ukraine.

08-04.title: Russian guided bombs kill three in Sumy
08-04.description: Russian forces struck Sumy with six guided aerial bombs between 2:08 and 2:17 a.m., hitting civilian infrastructure. One bomb struck a residential area, killing three civilians - two girls aged 5 and 10 and a 76-year-old woman - and injuring four others, according to the Sumy City Council.

08-04.title: Serviceman kills four in shooting near Sevastopol
08-04.description: A Russian serviceman opened fire on fellow soldiers and civilians in the village of Khmelnitskoye near Sevastopol, killing four people - one soldier and three civilians aged 59, 64 and 71 - and wounding four others before being detained, Sevastopol Governor Mikhail Razvozhayev said.

08-04.title: CRPF officer shooting in Assam kills four
08-04.description: A CRPF officer shot two colleagues dead and seriously wounded another at the 34th Battalion camp in Katimari, Nagaon, before killing himself; the wounded personnel member later died in hospital, bringing the death toll to four, police said.

08-04.title: Russian drone strike on Mykolaiv kills elderly woman
08-04.description: Russian drones attacked the southern port city of Mykolaiv overnight, killing an 89-year-old woman and injuring seven people, including two children. Two private houses were destroyed and several other buildings were damaged.

08-04.title: Israeli fire kills two in Gaza
08-04.description: Two more Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire in Gaza over 24 hours, with ten others injured, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, bringing the death toll since October 7, 2023 to 73,377. Some victims remained trapped under rubble beyond the reach of rescue crews.

08-04.title: Lightning strike kills footballer in Thailand
08-04.description: A 24-year-old Thai footballer, Safwan Awae of Yala FC, was killed and nine to twelve others injured when lightning struck the pitch during a lower-league match at Santiphap Stadium in southern Thailand.

08-06.title: Ethiopia floods (Dire Dawa and Omo Valley)
08-06.description: Unusually intense seasonal rains in August 2006 caused two major flood disasters in Ethiopia: a flash flood of the Dechatu River in the city of Dire Dawa on August 6 killed 256 people with about 250 missing, and flooding of the Omo River in the remote South Omo Valley on August 13 killed 364 people and submerged five villages. Combined flood deaths across the country in 2006 reached about 640, with roughly 118,000 people affected and tens of thousands displaced.
sources: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)

08-06.title: Russian drone attacks across Ukraine kill six
08-06.description: At least six people were killed in Russian drone attacks on Thursday: three in Balakliia in the Kharkiv region and three in residential areas of the Sumy region, with dozens injured across the affected regions, including 13 in Sumy city after a series of guided bombs. Six more people were injured in the Kherson region when a drone struck a van.

08-06.title: Israeli airstrike on Beit Lahia kills one
08-06.description: One Palestinian died of wounds from an earlier attack and five others were injured over 24 hours, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, bringing the death toll since October 7, 2023 to 73,382.

08-06.title: Storm deaths in northern Philippines reach at least 26
08-06.description: Heavy rains from tropical depressions Luis and Maymay and the enhanced southwest monsoon killed at least 26 people in the northern Philippines by August 12, including a police officer, according to the Philippine National Police. Landslides killed people in Benguet, Rizal and Batangas, including 10 in Baguio City when a rain-drenched mountainside collapsed on three houses; other victims died by drowning, falling trees, lightning and electrocution. More than 2.27 million people were affected, with school closures and evacuation centers across the north.

08-06.title: Rain-triggered house collapse kills six in Pratapgarh, India
08-06.description: A roughly 100-year-old house collapsed in Mahuli Bazaar in Pratapgarh district during heavy rain at about 2 a.m., killing six members of one family - a couple, two of their sons, a daughter-in-law and a two-year-old grandson, plus a 10-month-old infant - while they slept. One family member survived and raised the alarm; rescue teams pulled the victims from the rubble.

08-06.title: ATF agents kill two men during Nashville firearms operation
08-06.description: Federal ATF agents fatally shot two men during a federal firearms enforcement action at the Thompson Lane Self Storage facility in South Nashville on August 6. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation identified the dead as 32-year-old James Salinas and 16-year-old Denzel Molina; agents opened fire after one man pointed a gun at them, and a second man was shot when he pointed a gun at agents.

08-09.title: Voepass Flight 2283 Crash
08-09.description: On August 9, 2024, Voepass Flight 2283, an ATR 72-500 turboprop bound for Guarulhos, crashed into a residential area in Vinhedo, São Paulo state, Brazil, shortly after takeoff. All 62 people aboard — 58 passengers and 4 crew — were killed; flight recorders indicated ice buildup, and the crash was Brazil's deadliest aviation disaster since 2007.

08-09.title: Saada school bus airstrike
08-09.description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a school bus at a crowded market in Dahyan, Saada province, northern Yemen, while the bus was carrying children on a field trip during the Yemeni civil war. At least 51 people were killed and 79 wounded, with children accounting for roughly 40 of the dead, as reported by the International Committee of the Red Cross and UNICEF. The attack drew international condemnation and contributed to calls for an end to the conflict.

08-09.title: Sbarro Pizzeria Bombing
08-09.description: A Palestinian suicide bomber detonated a nail-packed bomb at the Sbarro pizzeria in central Jerusalem, killing 15 civilians, including several children, and wounding about 130. Hamas claimed responsibility for the attack, the deadliest in Jerusalem during the first year of the Second Intifada.

08-09.title: Russian missile strike on Kharkiv apartment block kills two
08-09.description: Russian missiles struck a high-rise apartment block in Kharkiv's Saltivskyi district on Sunday morning, August 9, killing two people, two men aged 50 and 66, and injuring more than a dozen others, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov.

08-09.title: Ukrainian drone strikes kill five in Russia's Belgorod region
08-09.description: Ukrainian drone strikes on Sunday killed five people and injured two dozen others, including a 4-year-old boy, in Russia's border region of Belgorod, according to the regional administration. The strikes damaged apartment blocks, private houses and administrative buildings.

08-09.title: Israeli strikes kill three Palestinians in Gaza
08-09.description: Israeli strikes across the Gaza Strip killed three Palestinians and wounded nine others on August 9, targeting civilian neighborhoods, displacement camps and areas previously designated as safe, amid ongoing violations of the ceasefire agreement. Gaza's Health Ministry put the cumulative death toll at 73,386.

08-09.title: Habagat floods and landslides kill three in Batangas, Philippines
08-09.description: Widespread flooding and multiple landslides triggered by the southwest monsoon (habagat) killed three people and left one fisherman missing in Batangas province. One victim, 69-year-old construction worker Teodoro Latumbo, died when a landslide buried his barracks in Barangay Calumala, Santa Teresita, late Saturday night.

08-09.title: Houthi strikes on Mokha kill at least seven in Yemen
08-09.description: Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks on the western port city of Mokha on Sunday killed at least seven people - three civilians and four military personnel, according to medical sources - and wounded about 15 others, some critically. The Houthis launched a fresh round of strikes hours later.

08-09.title: Two tribal elders shot dead in South Waziristan, Pakistan
08-09.location: Toi Khulla, Lower South Waziristan, Pakistan
08-09.description: Unidentified armed men shot dead two tribal elders, Haji Gul and Malik Badshah, both members of the Suleman Khel tribe, in the Zarmilan area of Toi Khulla tehsil in Lower South Waziristan on Sunday, police said. The two men sustained multiple bullet wounds and died at the scene.

08-09.title: Sofa factory fire in Riyadh kills 16 Bangladeshi workers
08-09.description: A fire broke out on Sunday at a sofa manufacturing factory in the Musa Sanaiya industrial area of Riyadh, killing at least 16 Bangladeshi migrant workers, according to Bangladesh's Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry. Ten of the victims were from the Naogaon district and others from Natore and Rajshahi.

08-09.title: Landslide on rain-soaked hillside in Baguio kills 10
08-09.description: A rain-drenched mountainside collapsed onto three houses in Baguio City late Sunday night, August 9, killing at least 10 people in Barangay Guisad Surong, including at least four minors; three others and a dog were rescued and two people remained missing as of Monday night, according to the Baguio City Public Information Office. The landslide was part of a nine-day downpour that left at least 26 dead across the northern Philippines, and rescue work was done manually because of continuing rain and fear of further landslides.

09-11.title: Mecca crane collapse
09-11.description: A construction crane toppled into the courtyard of the Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) in Mecca during Friday prayers, amid a severe windstorm with gusts of up to 100 km/h, killing 111 people and injuring 394. The crane belonged to the company expanding the mosque; the official investigation attributed the collapse to the strong winds and the crane's positioning, and the manufacturer said it had not been secured for the conditions.

09-11.title: Ali Enterprises factory fire
09-11.description: On the night of 11 September 2012, a fire swept through the Ali Enterprises garment factory in Baldia Town, Karachi, killing 289 workers, with more than 600 injured. Locked and barred exit doors and unsecured windows trapped workers on the upper floors; most victims suffocated. Some later official reports revised the toll to roughly 255-260.

09-11.title: September 11 Attacks
09-11.location: New York, Washington DC, Pennsylvania, United States
09-11.description: Al-Qaeda hijackers flew commercial airliners into the World Trade Center towers and the Pentagon. A fourth plane crashed in Pennsylvania after passengers fought back. 2,977 people were killed.

10-01.title: Las Vegas Route 91 Harvest festival shooting
10-01.description: On the night of 1 October 2017, a gunman opened fire with multiple rifles fitted with bump stocks from a hotel room on the 32nd floor of the Mandalay Bay resort into a crowd of about 22,000 attending the Route 91 Harvest country music festival on the Las Vegas Strip. The attack killed 60 people, including two victims who died of their injuries in 2019 and 2020, and wounded more than 850 others before the shooter killed himself; it remains the deadliest mass shooting in modern US history. No clear motive was established.

10-01.title: Nigeria floods — 2012
10-01.description: From July to October 2012, the worst flooding in Nigeria in four decades submerged large areas of the country, peaking in October. The National Emergency Management Agency reported 363 deaths and over 2.1 million people displaced, with 30 of Nigeria's 36 states affected; Kogi and Benue were the hardest hit, and more than 150,000 hectares of farmland were destroyed.

10-01.title: Bali bombings
10-01.description: Three suicide bombers attacked restaurants in Kuta Square and on Jimbaran beach in Bali, Indonesia, killing 20 victims and wounding more than 100. The attacks, attributed to Jemaah Islamiyah, killed a total of 23 people including the three bombers.

10-01.title: Srinagar Legislative Assembly Attack
10-01.description: Jaish-e-Mohammed militants rammed a car bomb into the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly complex in Srinagar and stormed the building, killing 38 people and wounding about 60 during a gun battle lasting several hours. No legislators were in the building at the time of the attack.

10-07.title: Israel–Hamas war
10-07.description: On October 7, 2023, Hamas-led armed groups broke out of Gaza in an attack on southern Israel, killing about 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and taking around 250 hostages; Israel responded with airstrikes and a ground invasion of the Gaza Strip. By the end of 2023, the Gaza Health Ministry reported more than 22,000 Palestinians killed and over 57,000 wounded, with much of northern Gaza destroyed and most of the population displaced. The war remained ongoing through 2024 and beyond, with UN assessments describing near-famine conditions in Gaza.

10-07.title: Herat earthquakes
10-07.description: A magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck Herat province in western Afghanistan on October 7, followed by strong aftershocks over subsequent days, leveling villages of largely mud-brick homes in the Zindajan district. Initial official counts reported more than 1,000 people killed, with later official tolls citing around 1,480 dead and over 2,100 injured, before aid agencies stopped updating casualty figures. The disaster compounded Afghanistan's severe economic and humanitarian crises, with most survivors needing winter shelter.

10-07.title: US-Led Invasion of Afghanistan
10-07.description: The United States and allied forces launched Operation Enduring Freedom with airstrikes against the Taliban regime on October 7, 2001, in response to the September 11 attacks. Estimates of Afghan civilian deaths from bombing in the first three months ranged from about 1,000 to over 3,000, with thousands more believed to have died from the disruption of food aid deliveries.

11-13.title: Paris Attacks
11-13.description: Coordinated attacks across Paris — suicide bombings at the Stade de France, mass shootings at restaurants, and a hostage siege at the Bataclan theatre. 130 people were killed and over 400 injured.

12-14.title: Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting
12-14.description: On 14 December 2012, a gunman killed 20 children aged six to seven and 6 adult staff members at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, Connecticut, after fatally shooting his mother at home, then killed himself — 28 total deaths including the shooter. It was the deadliest mass shooting at a US elementary school and prompted a national debate on gun control.

12-26.title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
12-26.description: A magnitude 9.1-9.3 undersea earthquake off the coast of northern Sumatra triggered a series of tsunamis that struck coastlines in 14 countries across the Indian Ocean, including Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India and Thailand. At least 227,898 people were killed or left missing and presumed dead, and about 1.7 million were displaced, making it the deadliest tsunami in recorded history.

12-26.title: Bam earthquake
12-26.description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake destroyed the ancient city of Bam in southeastern Iran, killing about 26,271 people and injuring roughly 30,000. More than 85% of the city's buildings collapsed, and the quake was Iran's deadliest disaster in decades.

02-05.title: Novye Aldi massacre
02-05.description: Russian OMON police conducted a house-to-house purge of the Novye Aldi suburb of Grozny, summarily executing at least 62 civilians. The European Court of Human Rights later ruled Russia responsible.

02-21.title: Kaduna religious riots
02-21.description: Clashes between Christian and Muslim communities broke out after Kaduna State announced the adoption of Sharia law. A state commission recorded 1,295 deaths; Human Rights Watch estimated 2,000 to 5,000 total.

02-22.title: Christchurch earthquake
02-22.description: A magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck near Christchurch, New Zealand's second-largest city, on February 22, 2011, at shallow depth. It killed 185 people and injured more than 7,000, with most fatalities caused by the collapse of the CTV building and other structures in the central business district. The quake destroyed much of the city centre, damaged around 100,000 buildings, and caused an estimated NZ$40 billion in economic losses. It was the deadliest natural disaster in New Zealand since 1931.

02-22.title: Al-Askari shrine bombing triggers sectarian violence
02-22.description: Bombers dressed as security personnel detonated explosives inside the al-Askari shrine in Samarra on February 22, 2006, destroying the golden dome of one of Shia Islam's holiest sites. The blast itself killed no one, but it triggered waves of retaliatory sectarian killings across Iraq, with more than 1,000 people dead within days and hundreds of mosques attacked; leaked U.S. military documents later indicated the death toll exceeded 3,000, and the bombing is widely regarded as having ignited Iraq's civil war.

02-22.title: Iraq sectarian civil war (deadliest year of the conflict)
02-22.description: Sectarian violence between Shia and Sunni communities escalated sharply after the February 22 bombing of the al-Askari shrine, plunging Iraq into civil war conditions characterized by car bombings, executions, death squads and forced displacement. The Iraq Body Count project recorded about 29,000 violent civilian deaths in 2006, making it the deadliest year of the war since 2003, with the United Nations reporting similar monthly tolls; more than 400,000 people were displaced within Iraq during the year.
sources: United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq (UNAMI)

02-22.title: Zarand earthquake
02-22.description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck near Zarand in Kerman Province, Iran, levelling several mud-brick mountain villages and killing 612 people. An estimated 80,000 people were affected and more than 900 were injured.

02-22.title: Mozambique floods and Cyclone Eline
02-22.description: Cyclone Eline made landfall unleashing the worst floods in Mozambique's recorded history. Approximately 700 people died and up to 2 million were displaced.

03-01.title: Abiemnom massacre
03-01.description: On 1 March 2026, several hundred armed youths from Unity State crossed into Abiemnom County in South Sudan's Ruweng Administrative Area and attacked the town for about three hours, killing 169 people — 79 government soldiers and 90 civilians — and wounding 68. More than 1,000 residents took shelter in the UNMISS compound during the attack; officials attributed it to rebel-linked militias, though attribution remained disputed.

03-01.title: Kunming Railway Station Attack
03-01.description: On 1 March 2014, eight knife-wielding attackers stormed the Kunming Railway Station in Yunnan province, China, stabbing passengers in a coordinated assault. Thirty-one people were killed and more than 140 injured before police shot four of the attackers dead. Chinese authorities attributed the attack to Uyghur separatists from Xinjiang.

03-01.title: Ethiopia drought and food crisis
03-01.description: After years of failed rains, a severe drought gripped southeastern Ethiopia with 8 million facing severe food shortages. Malnutrition-related deaths ran into the low thousands before international relief averted a repeat of the 1984-85 famine.

03-20.title: Peru floods and mudslides
03-20.description: Torrential rains linked to a coastal El Niño event from January through April 2017 caused catastrophic flooding and mudslides across Peru's coastal regions, overwhelming rivers in Lima and the northern departments of Piura, Lambayeque and La Libertad. The Peruvian government reported 162 deaths, with more than 270,000 people left homeless and about one million affected; the EM-DAT international disaster database records a toll of 177. Landslides buried villages and the flooding destroyed bridges, highways and thousands of homes, isolating communities for weeks.

03-20.title: US-led invasion of Iraq
03-20.description: A US-led coalition invaded Iraq on March 20, 2003, and toppled the government of Saddam Hussein within roughly three weeks. Iraq Body Count estimated that between 5,000 and 7,000 Iraqi civilians were killed during the invasion phase, with higher figures proposed by some academic studies.

03-20.title: Chattisinghpora massacre
03-20.description: Armed gunmen rounded up Sikh men and boys in the village of Chattisinghpora and shot them. The attack came on the eve of US President Bill Clinton's visit to India.

05-13.title: Soma Coal Mine Disaster
05-13.description: An underground coal mine in Soma, Manisa Province, Turkey, caught fire and filled with toxic gas on 13 May 2014 after a power failure and fire in a transformer. The electrical outage stranded hundreds of miners underground, and 301 miners died, making it the worst mining disaster in Turkish history. The accident prompted widespread criticism of workplace safety rules and charges against mine operator officials.

05-13.title: Jaipur bombings
05-13.description: Eight synchronized bombs exploded within about 15 minutes across the crowded Walled City markets of Jaipur, Rajasthan, on the evening of 13 May 2008, including near the Hawa Mahal landmark, killing 63 people and wounding more than 200. The devices included ammonium-nitrate and RDX bombs hidden on bicycles, and a previously unknown group, the Indian Mujahideen, claimed responsibility; Bangladesh-based militants were also suspected. Four men were later convicted over the attacks, though all were acquitted by the Rajasthan High Court in 2023.

05-13.title: Enschede fireworks disaster
05-13.description: A fire at a fireworks depot escalated into massive explosions, killing 23 people including four firefighters. The blasts destroyed around 400 homes.

05-23.title: Poso sectarian riots
05-23.description: The third and deadliest phase of the Poso riots between Christian and Muslim communities. An estimated 300 people were killed.

08-08.title: Maui wildfire
08-08.description: A wind-driven wildfire, fueled by dry conditions and hurricane-force winds from a passing offshore storm, swept through the historic town of Lahaina on the island of Maui, Hawaii, destroying more than 2,200 structures and much of the town. At least 101 people were confirmed dead, making it the deadliest U.S. wildfire in more than a century, and hundreds remained unaccounted for. The fire's rapid spread raised criticism of emergency alert failures and utility power-line conditions.

08-08.title: Typhoon Morakot
08-08.description: Typhoon Morakot, the deadliest typhoon to hit Taiwan in about 50 years, made landfall on August 7-8, 2009, dumping record rainfall of up to 3 meters in the southern mountains. A massive mudslide buried the village of Xiaolin in Kaohsiung County, killing an estimated 400-500 residents. More than 670 people were confirmed dead in Taiwan, with additional deaths in China and the northern Philippines, for a regional total of roughly 700-800 lives lost.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

08-08.title: Pushkin Square bombing
08-08.description: A bomb exploded in a crowded underground passageway beneath Pushkin Square during rush hour, killing 13 people. Linked to Chechen separatists.

08-08.title: Russian drone and missile attack on Kyiv region kills three, including child
08-08.description: Russia attacked Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight on August 8, killing three people, including a child, in strikes on the Brovary district east of Kyiv. Three more people were injured, including another child, and the attack damaged a residential building, cars and outbuildings.

08-08.title: IS-linked militants kill at least 13 in eastern Congo village attack
08-08.location: Banana École, Mambasa, Ituri, DR Congo
08-08.description: Militants affiliated with the Islamic State group attacked the village of Banana École, a suburb of the territorial capital of Mambasa in eastern DR Congo near the border with Uganda, early Saturday, killing at least 13 people and burning and looting homes, a local civil society group said.

08-08.title: Helicopter crash in Rio de Janeiro kills four
08-08.location: Alto da Boa Vista, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
08-08.description: A Robinson 44 helicopter crashed in a forested area near Vista Chinesa in the Tijuca National Park in Rio de Janeiro on Saturday morning, killing all four people on board, firefighters said.

08-08.title: Explosive drone attack on police substation kills officer in northern Colombia
08-08.description: A non-commissioned police officer died after a drone loaded with explosives attacked the San Roque police substation in Curumaní, Cesar department, on the first day of President Abelardo de la Espriella's term. The attack came alongside a separate explosion that damaged the Mondomo tollgate on the Pan-American Highway in Cauca, injuring two guards.

08-22.title: Azizabad airstrike
08-22.description: US-led coalition forces called in air strikes, including from an AC-130 gunship, on the village of Azizabad in Shindand district, Herat Province, on 22 August 2008, during an operation against a suspected Taliban commander. The Afghan government and the UN (UNAMA) said about 90 civilians were killed, including 60 children and 15 women, based on witness accounts and video evidence; the US military initially denied civilian deaths before a second inquiry acknowledged 33 civilians killed. The incident, which President Hamid Karzai condemned, became a flashpoint over civilian casualties and led Afghanistan to pay compensation to victims' families.

08-22.title: Typhoon Bilis
08-22.description: Super Typhoon Bilis, the strongest typhoon on record to strike Taiwan at the time, made landfall with winds over 200 km/h. It killed 71 people across Taiwan and mainland China.

09-10.title: Derna dam collapses and floods
09-10.description: Mediterranean Storm Daniel brought extreme rainfall to northeastern Libya, causing two upstream dams to fail on the night of September 10 and releasing a wall of water through the coastal city of Derna, which swept away entire neighborhoods into the sea. Libya's official death toll reached more than 4,000 people, with initial estimates that included thousands of missing running far higher, and tens of thousands were left homeless. The disaster was aggravated by years of civil conflict that had left the dams unrepaired.

09-10.title: Mekong Delta floods
09-10.description: The worst flooding in the Mekong Delta in decades inundated more than 825,000 homes and affected over 5 million people. 482 people died, most of them children.

09-13.title: Jakarta Stock Exchange bombing
09-13.description: A car bomb exploded in the underground car park of the Jakarta Stock Exchange building, killing 15 people. Three Indonesian soldiers were later convicted.

09-15.title: Typhoon Mangkhut
09-15.description: Typhoon Mangkhut, the strongest storm of the year, made landfall in northern Luzon, Philippines, on September 15, 2018, with sustained winds of 205 km/h. The typhoon triggered landslides in mining and farming areas, destroyed over 400,000 homes, and killed at least 134 people in the Philippines, with additional deaths reported in Hong Kong and southern China. Storm surges and flooding affected millions across the region.

09-15.title: Bangladesh floods
09-15.description: The worst floods in more than 20 years hit southwestern Bangladesh, drowning over 2 million people across border districts. 130-150 people died from drowning, snakebites, and disease.

09-28.title: Sulawesi earthquake and tsunami
09-28.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, triggering a tsunami up to six meters high that hit Palu Bay, along with widespread soil liquefaction that swallowed entire neighborhoods. The disaster destroyed tens of thousands of buildings in Palu, Donggala, and Sigi and displaced over 200,000 people. Indonesia's disaster agency (BNPB) confirmed 4,340 deaths, more than 10,000 injured, and hundreds missing.

09-28.title: Start of the Second Intifada
09-28.description: The Second Intifada began after Israeli opposition leader Ariel Sharon visited the Temple Mount compound. By end of 2000, roughly 300 people had been killed.

10-12.title: Typhoon Hagibis
10-12.description: Typhoon Hagibis, one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in decades, made landfall on the Izu Peninsula near Tokyo on 12 October 2019, bringing record rainfall that caused more than 70 rivers to overflow and widespread landslides. Around 100 people were killed, more than 350 were injured and thousands of homes were flooded, with several prefectures including Nagano, Fukushima and Miyagi among the worst affected. The storm disrupted transport, power and the 2019 Rugby World Cup, and the government described the scale of damage as unprecedented.

10-12.title: Bali bombings
10-12.description: Three bombs exploded in Kuta and Denpasar on Bali, including a large car bomb outside the Sari Club nightclub, in an attack linked to Jemaah Islamiyah. The bombings killed 202 people, mostly foreign tourists, and injured more than 200.

10-12.title: USS Cole bombing
10-12.description: Al-Qaeda suicide bombers rammed an explosive-laden boat into the USS Cole as it refuelled. Seventeen American sailors were killed and 39 wounded.

12-25.title: Luoyang Dongdu commercial building fire
12-25.description: A fire started by illegal welding spread toxic smoke through the Dongdu commercial building into a packed dance hall. All 309 victims died of smoke inhalation.

12-30.title: Aden airport attack
12-30.description: On 30 December 2020, explosions and gunfire hit Aden International Airport just as a plane carrying members of Yemen's newly formed unity government, including the prime minister and the Saudi ambassador, was landing from Riyadh. The attack killed 28 people and wounded 107, though none of the cabinet passengers were hurt. A UN investigation later found the Houthi movement responsible for the attack, which came as the Saudi-brokered power-sharing government returned to the interim capital.

12-30.title: Rizal Day bombings
12-30.description: Coordinated bombings struck five locations across Metro Manila on a national holiday, killing 22 people. The deadliest blast hit a crowded LRT train.

09-01.title: Nigeria floods
09-01.description: Heavy rains from July 2022 produced Nigeria's worst flooding in a decade, peaking in September and October after the release of water from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon. Nigeria's National Emergency Management Agency reported more than 603 deaths and over 2,400 injuries, with at least 1.4 million people displaced. The floods destroyed more than 200,000 homes and inundated farmland across 33 of Nigeria's 36 states, worsening food insecurity.

09-01.title: Hurricane Dorian
09-01.location: Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama, Bahamas
09-01.description: Hurricane Dorian, a Category 5 storm with sustained winds of 185 mph, devastated the northern Bahamas when it made landfall on 1 September 2019, stalling over the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama for more than a day. The storm killed 84 people across all affected areas, including 74 in the Bahamas, where hundreds of people were initially reported missing and whole settlements were flattened by the storm surge. It was the strongest hurricane on record to hit the Bahamas and caused tens of thousands of people to be displaced or left homeless.

09-01.title: Beslan school siege
09-01.description: Armed Chechen separatist militants seized School Number One in Beslan on the first day of the academic year, holding more than 1,000 hostages, mostly children, in the school gymnasium for three days. The siege ended when Russian security forces stormed the school; 334 people were killed, including 186 children.

09-18.title: Benisheik massacre
09-18.description: On September 18, 2013, Boko Haram militants attacked Benisheik in Borno State, northeastern Nigeria, shooting and setting fire to vehicles along the highway and raiding the town, killing about 161 people, including travelers, police officers, and soldiers (some reports cited at least 143). It was among the deadliest single attacks by the insurgency in 2013, and the group claimed responsibility.

09-18.title: Sikkim earthquake
09-18.description: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck on September 18, 2011 near the Nepal-Sikkim border in northeastern India, with the epicentre in the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area. At least 111 people were killed, including 97 in India (mostly in Sikkim), 7 in China's Tibet region, 6 in Nepal and 1 in Bhutan, and hundreds were injured. The quake, felt across northern India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Tibet, triggered landslides and rockfalls that cut off remote areas and damaged roughly 43,000 houses in Sikkim.

09-18.title: Hurricane Jeanne flooding in Haiti
09-18.description: Torrential rains from Tropical Storm Jeanne triggered catastrophic flash flooding and mudslides in Haiti, most severely in the coastal city of Gonaives, which was left largely submerged. The Haitian government's final tally recorded 3,006 deaths, including 2,826 in Gonaives, with about 200,000 people affected.

09-18.title: 2001 Anthrax Attacks
09-18.description: Letters containing weaponized anthrax spores were mailed to news media offices and two US senators, killing five people and infecting 17 others between September and November 2001, and forcing about 35,000 people onto antibiotics. The FBI concluded in 2010 that biodefense researcher Bruce Ivins acted alone, a finding later questioned in part by the National Academies of Sciences.

02-24.title: Russian invasion of Ukraine
02-24.description: On 24 February 2022, Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the largest armed conflict in Europe since World War II. The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights documented at least 6,919 civilian deaths in Ukraine during 2022, with the true toll believed to be considerably higher, and both militaries sustained tens of thousands of casualties. The war displaced millions of people, destroyed entire cities, and no ceasefire was reached by the end of the year.

02-24.title: Al Hoceima earthquake
02-24.description: A magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck near the Mediterranean port city of Al Hoceima in northern Morocco, destroying about 2,500 homes and leaving more than 15,000 people homeless. The final death toll was 628, with 926 people injured.

02-24.title: Bogoro massacre
02-24.location: Bogoro, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo
02-24.description: Fighters of the FNI and FRPI militias, many of them child soldiers under age 15, attacked the village of Bogoro in Ituri Province, killing at least 200 civilians with machetes, guns, and fire. Two rebel commanders were later convicted by the International Criminal Court for the attack.

10-23.title: Siege of Marawi ends
10-23.description: The five-month armed confrontation between Philippine security forces and the Maute and Abu Sayyaf groups loyal to the Islamic State over the city of Marawi, which began on 23 May 2017, ended on 23 October 2017 when the military announced full recapture of the city. The urban battle killed an estimated 1,233 people, including 978 militants, 168 government forces and 87 civilians, and left most of Marawi, the Philippines' only predominantly Muslim city, in ruins; hundreds of thousands of residents were displaced and reconstruction cost billions. It was the longest urban battle fought by the Philippine military since World War II.

10-23.title: Van earthquake
10-23.description: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck eastern Turkey near the city of Van on October 23, 2011, collapsing poorly constructed masonry and adobe buildings, particularly in the town of Ercis. It killed 604 people, injured about 4,152, and left roughly 60,000 people homeless, with 11,232 buildings damaged. A magnitude 5.7 aftershock on November 9 killed about 40 additional people, bringing the earthquake sequence's combined toll to approximately 644.
sources: AFAD (Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency of Turkey)

10-23.title: Niigata Chuetsu earthquake
10-23.description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck the Chuetsu region of Niigata Prefecture, triggering landslides and destroying about 3,100 homes. The earthquake and its aftershocks killed 68 people and injured nearly 5,000, forcing over 100,000 residents to evacuate.

10-23.title: Moscow theater siege (Nord-Ost)
10-23.description: Chechen militants seized the Dubrovka theater in Moscow on October 23, taking more than 900 hostages. Russian security forces pumped an incapacitating gas into the building on October 26; at least 130 hostages died, most of them from the gas.

03-02.title: Ashura bombings in Karbala and Baghdad
03-02.description: Coordinated suicide bombings, car bombs and small-arms attacks struck Shia worshippers commemorating Ashura at shrines in Karbala and Baghdad, killing at least 182 people and wounding more than 550. It was one of the deadliest attacks in Iraq since the fall of Saddam Hussein.

11-28.title: Koshebe massacre
11-28.description: On 28 November 2020, gunmen believed to be Boko Haram fighters attacked farmers harvesting rice fields near the village of Koshebe in Borno State, northeastern Nigeria. The United Nations reported that as many as 110 civilians and peasant farmers were killed, six were wounded and about 15 women were kidnapped. The attack, which followed a dispute with farmers who had disarmed a Boko Haram gunman the previous day, was among the deadliest attacks on civilians in Nigeria during 2020.

11-28.title: Kano Central Mosque Attack
11-28.description: Suicide bombers attacked the Central Mosque of Kano in northern Nigeria on 28 November 2014 during Friday prayers. The first bomb exploded during the imam's sermon, and gunmen opened fire on worshippers fleeing the blast, killing around 120 people. The Boko Haram insurgency was widely held responsible for the attack on the mosque of the Emir of Kano.

11-28.title: Chenjiashan coal mine gas explosion
11-28.description: A gas explosion at the Chenjiashan coal mine in Tongchuan, Shaanxi Province, trapped 166 miners, all of whom were confirmed dead, making it China's worst mining accident in 44 years. High temperatures and repeated underground blasts hampered recovery efforts for weeks.

10-20.title: Haiti cholera outbreak
10-20.description: A cholera epidemic, the largest in recent history, broke out in the Artibonite region of Haiti in October 2010, 10 months after the January earthquake, and spread nationwide within weeks. The World Health Organization and U.S. CDC recorded about 820,000 cases and 9,789 deaths through the epidemic's successive waves ending in 2019, with experts estimating the true toll was higher. Scientific studies traced the outbreak's origin to the introduction of cholera-contaminated waste from a U.N. peacekeepers' camp, and the United Nations acknowledged a role in the outbreak in 2016.
sources: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

10-20.title: Daping coal mine gas explosion
10-20.description: A gas explosion at the Daping coal mine in Xinmi, Henan Province, killed all 148 miners trapped underground, making it China's deadliest mine accident of 2004. The blast pushed hot, toxic fumes through the shaft and could be heard several kilometers away.

10-20.title: Typhoon Tokage
10-20.description: Typhoon Tokage, the record tenth typhoon to strike Japan in 2004, crossed Shikoku and Honshu with torrential rain that triggered more than 700 landslides. It killed 95 people and left three missing, making it Japan's deadliest typhoon since 1979.

08-24.title: Central Italy earthquake (Amatrice)
08-24.description: A magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck central Italy at 3:36 a.m., leveling the hill towns of Amatrice, Accumoli, and Arquata del Tronto in the Apennines. Two hundred ninety-nine people were killed, including 234 in Amatrice, and about 388 were injured; most deaths occurred when old stone and unreinforced masonry buildings collapsed on sleeping residents. The quake also caused major damage in Norcia and triggered thousands of aftershocks.

08-24.title: San Fernando migrant massacre
08-24.description: Mexican marines discovered the bodies of 72 Central and South American migrants, 58 men and 14 women, bound, blindfolded, and shot dead inside a grain barn on a ranch near San Fernando, Tamaulipas, on August 24, 2010. The sole survivor, an Ecuadorean who escaped by feigning death, told investigators that members of the Los Zetas drug cartel killed the migrants after they refused to be forcibly recruited to work for the gang. The massacre was the largest single mass killing of the Mexican drug war at the time and drew international condemnation, with U.N. human rights chief Navi Pillay demanding an end to impunity.

08-24.title: Greek forest fires
08-24.description: Widespread forest fires in Greece, most severely in the Peloponnese, burned from late August 2007 and killed 85 people across the country. Flames raced through villages, and many victims were trapped in their homes or while fleeing by car.

08-24.title: Russian passenger plane bombings
08-24.description: Explosives were detonated aboard two Russian domestic passenger flights that departed Moscow's Domodedovo Airport minutes apart on the evening of August 24, downing both aircraft over Tula and Rostov oblasts and killing all 90 people on board. Investigators found traces of RDX explosives, and two Chechen female suicide bombers were identified as the perpetrators.

02-27.title: Balyun airstrikes on Turkish troops
02-27.description: On 27 February 2020, during the Idlib offensive in northwestern Syria, an airstrike attributed to the Syrian and Russian air forces hit a convoy of a Turkish mechanized infantry battalion near Balyun. Turkey reported 34 soldiers killed (33-34 depending on the official source) and more than 30 wounded, making it the deadliest attack on Turkish forces in Syria. Turkey responded by launching Operation Spring Shield, which ended in a Russia-Turkey ceasefire on 5 March 2020.

02-27.title: Chile earthquake and tsunami
02-27.description: A magnitude 8.8 earthquake, one of the strongest ever recorded, struck off the coast of central Chile on February 27, 2010, generating a tsunami with waves up to 24 meters that destroyed coastal towns such as Dichato and Constitución. Authorities confirmed 525 deaths and 25 missing, about 800,000 people displaced, and roughly 370,000 homes damaged. The quake triggered over 1,000 landslides and a nationwide blackout affecting 93 percent of the population; the death toll was comparatively low due to Chile's stringent building codes adopted after the 1960 Valdivia earthquake.

02-27.title: SuperFerry 14 bombing
02-27.description: A bomb planted aboard the SuperFerry 14 exploded in Manila Bay about an hour after departure, setting the ferry ablaze and killing 116 people. The Abu Sayyaf group claimed responsibility, and the attack remains the deadliest terrorist attack at sea.

02-27.title: Godhra train burning
02-27.description: A mob set fire to the Sabarmati Express at Godhra station in Gujarat, killing 59 passengers, most of them Hindu pilgrims returning from Ayodhya. The attack triggered weeks of retaliatory communal violence across the state.

08-12.title: Tianjin warehouse explosions
08-12.description: A series of explosions at a hazardous-chemicals warehouse in the Binhai New Area of Tianjin, involving roughly 800 tonnes of ammonium nitrate and stored nitrocellulose, destroyed nearby buildings and killed 173 people, including 104 firefighters, injuring about 800. An official investigation attributed the first blast to the overheating and auto-ignition of dry nitrocellulose and noted that the depot was sited close to residential areas.

08-12.title: Typhoon Rananim
08-12.description: Typhoon Rananim, the strongest typhoon to hit the Chinese mainland since 1956, made landfall in Zhejiang Province, collapsing thousands of homes and triggering floods and landslides. At least 164 people were killed and 24 reported missing in Zhejiang, with nearly 13 million people affected.

08-12.title: Russian drone strikes on Kherson kill two
08-12.description: Russian strike drones killed two people in Kherson overnight on August 12, including a woman struck inside her home, and wounded others in the Tsentralnyi district, according to regional authorities and military administration head Oleksandr Prokudin.

08-12.title: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia region kill one
08-12.description: Russia carried out more than 1,000 strikes on Zaporizhzhia and the surrounding region over the day, killing one person and wounding at least eight, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said. An overnight drone attack destroyed the Epicentr shopping center in the city, sparking a large fire and power outages, and damaged residential buildings.

08-12.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Novorossiysk kills three
08-12.description: A massive Ukrainian drone attack on the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk killed three people — including an eight-year-old child — and injured about 24, damaging roughly 60 residential buildings and forcing major grain terminals in the city to halt operations, according to Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev. Russia said air defenses shot down 502 Ukrainian drones overnight, and Ukraine said the operation targeted the Novorossiysk naval base with drones, missiles and unmanned naval systems.

08-12.title: Ukrainian attacks on Belgorod region kill two civilians
08-12.description: Ukrainian forces attacked Russia's Belgorod region more than 170 times over 24 hours, killing two civilians in the Belgorodsky and Graivoronsky districts and injuring three others, acting Governor Alexander Shuvayev said. RIA Novosti later reported three dead and seven people seeking medical help.

08-12.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea kills civilian
08-12.description: A civilian was killed in the village of Novosyolovskoye in the Razdolnensky district of Crimea in an overnight Ukrainian drone attack, regional head Sergey Aksyonov said.

08-12.title: Landslide on Mumbai chawl kills seven
08-12.description: A hillside collapsed onto the Gaushiya Chawl row tenement in Chirag Nagar, Kurla West, Mumbai, at about 3:48 a.m. on August 12 after heavy rain, killing at least seven people — including three children — and injuring four others, with more feared trapped. The youngest victim was a two-year-old.

08-12.title: Israeli fire kills one in Gaza
08-12.description: An Israeli airstrike on Beit Lahia in the northern Gaza Strip killed one Palestinian and wounded five others, the first reported airstrike in about a week, with the Israeli military saying it targeted a Hamas cell commander. Gaza's Health Ministry put the death toll since October 7, 2023 at 73,388 and the number of wounded at 174,259.

08-12.title: Military Apache helicopter crash near Salado kills two
08-12.description: An AH-64 Apache attack helicopter from Fort Hood crashed into a field south of Salado, Texas, around 1:35 p.m. local time, killing both pilots on board and igniting a grass fire that forced nearby residents to flee.

08-12.title: Severe storms and tornadoes kill three in US Midwest
08-12.description: Severe storms swept across the US Midwest, spawning tornadoes near Chicago and producing damaging winds and flash flooding. At least three people died, two in Indiana including a four-year-old killed by a fallen tree, and one in Roseville, Ohio, where emergency crews could not reach the victim; hundreds of thousands of customers lost power.

08-12.title: Landslide in Rolpa district kills ten
08-12.description: A landslide triggered by continuous rain swept away nine houses, two cowsheds, a shop and a church in the Kotalbara area of Thabang Rural Municipality in Nepal's western Rolpa district on the night of August 12, 2026, killing 10 people and leaving two missing. Five bodies were recovered at the site and five more were found in neighbouring Pyuthan district, police said.

08-12.title: Ferry fire off Bali kills one
08-12.description: A passenger ferry travelling from Bali to Lombok caught fire in the early hours, killing a 19-year-old Indonesian woman. Authorities said 211 people were rescued and five passengers remained missing as search efforts continued.

11-07.title: Pétion-Ville school collapse (Collège La Promesse Évangélique)
11-07.description: The three-story Collège La Promesse Évangélique school collapsed around 10:00 a.m. on 7 November 2008 while classes were in session in the Nerette neighbourhood of Pétion-Ville, a suburb of Port-au-Prince, burying hundreds of the roughly 500-700 students and teachers. Rescue workers recovered at least 90 bodies, with final tolls reported between 90 and 97 dead and more than 150 injured, most of them children. The school's owner was detained over allegations of unauthorized structural additions; the building was found not to have met construction standards.

11-07.title: Second Battle of Fallujah
11-07.description: US, British and Iraqi forces launched Operation Phantom Fury to recapture the insurgent-held city, in the bloodiest battle of the Iraq War up to that point. More than 1,000 people were killed overall, including roughly 1,200-1,500 insurgents, 107 coalition troops, and an estimated 581-670 civilians per Iraq Body Count (about 800 per the Red Cross), and most of the city was destroyed.
sources: International Committee of the Red Cross

04-22.title: Kabul voter registration center bombing
04-22.description: A suicide bomber attacked a voter registration center in the Dasht-e-Barchi district of western Kabul, a predominantly Shia Hazara area, during Afghanistan's parliamentary election registration process. The blast killed at least 57 people and wounded more than 100, mostly civilians queued to obtain voter cards. The Islamic State Khorasan Province claimed responsibility for the attack, one of a series targeting the 2018 election process.

04-22.title: Ryongchon train explosion
04-22.description: Two freight wagons loaded with ammonium nitrate exploded at Ryongchon railway station near the Chinese border, flattening the town center and destroying nearly 1,800 homes. The officially confirmed death toll was 161, including 76 schoolchildren, with about 1,300 people injured.

07-30.title: Russia launches massive missile and drone strike on Ukraine
07-30.location: Kyiv, Lviv and Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine
07-30.description: In the early hours of July 30, 2026, Russia launched one of its largest combined strikes of the war, firing dozens of ballistic and cruise missiles and hundreds of drones (President Zelensky cited over 70 missiles and 280 drones) at cities across Ukraine, with damage reported from east to west in Kyiv, Lviv and Kryvyi Rih. At least 10 civilians, including children, were killed and more than 50 injured, including six people killed by a ballistic missile strike on Kryvyi Rih and a family of six killed in a village hit by a suspected North Korean missile; NATO scrambled jets in response and a stray Russian cruise missile briefly entered Polish airspace.

07-30.title: Avalanche on Broad Peak leaves climbers missing, four confirmed dead
07-30.description: An avalanche swept ten climbers from the 8,051-metre Broad Peak in the Karakoram on July 30, 2026, leaving them reported missing, among them celebrated Nepalese mountaineer Nirmal Purja and Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy. Rescue teams recovered the bodies of four of the climbers by July 31, while helicopters continued to search for the remaining six in one of the deadliest mountaineering accidents on the eight-thousander in recent years.

07-30.title: Wayanad Landslides
07-30.description: On July 30, 2024, torrential monsoon rainfall triggered catastrophic landslides in the Wayanad district of Kerala, India, burying the villages of Chooralmala and Mundakkai under mud and debris. At least 231 people were killed and more than 130 injured, with hundreds of homes destroyed and bodies recovered along the Chaliyar River for weeks afterward.

07-30.title: Darfur genocide (2004 killings)
07-30.description: The armed conflict in Darfur, in which the Sudanese government and allied Janjaweed militias systematically attacked civilian villages, killed tens of thousands of people and displaced more than a million during 2004. United Nations and WHO estimates of deaths in 2004 ranged from about 30,000 to 71,000, mostly from violence, starvation and disease.

07-30.title: Coal mine explosion in Balochistan
07-30.description: A methane gas explosion ripped through a coal mine in Balochistan province on 30 July, killing at least 34 miners. Rescue officials recovered 32 bodies and said two workers remained trapped in an inaccessible section of the mine.

08-31.title: Al-Aaimmah bridge stampede
08-31.description: A stampede on the Al-Aaimmah bridge in Baghdad during a Shia pilgrimage killed at least 965 people, mostly women and children crushed or drowned in the Tigris River after rumours of a suicide bomber sparked panic. The stampede followed mortar fire near the Kadhimiya shrine that had already killed pilgrims.

08-31.title: Rizhskaya metro station bombing
08-31.description: A female suicide bomber detonated an explosive device near the Rizhskaya metro station in Moscow, killing 10 people and wounding more than 50. The attack, linked to Chechen separatist militants, came one week after the bombing of two Russian passenger planes.

08-31.title: Typhoon Rusa
08-31.description: Typhoon Rusa, the strongest typhoon to strike South Korea in more than four decades, made landfall near Goheung on August 31, 2002. It killed 238 people across South Korea, Japan and North Korea and caused about $4.2 billion in damage.

04-04.title: Battle for Tripoli (Western Libya offensive)
04-04.description: On 4 April 2019, forces of the Libyan National Army under Khalifa Haftar launched an offensive to capture Tripoli from the UN-backed Government of National Accord, setting off nearly 14 months of fighting in the capital's southern suburbs. By the end of 2019 the United Nations reported that more than 1,000 people had been killed and about 146,000 displaced, with civilian infrastructure including hospitals and residential areas hit by airstrikes and shelling. The campaign continued into 2020, when a ceasefire and UN-brokered political talks brought a halt to the offensive.

04-04.title: Khan Sheikhoun chemical attack
04-04.description: On 4 April 2017 an airstrike released sarin gas on the rebel-held town of Khan Sheikhoun in Idlib province. At least 89 people were killed and more than 500 injured, including many women and children, with victims showing classic nerve-agent symptoms; medical workers filmed victims convulsing and foaming at the mouth. The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism concluded the Syrian air force dropped the sarin, a finding echoed by the UN Commission of Inquiry, the United States, France and the UK. The attack prompted a US Tomahawk missile strike on Syria's Shayrat air base days later.

04-04.title: Thane building collapse
04-04.description: On April 4, 2013, an illegally constructed seven-story residential building under construction collapsed in Mumbra, in Thane district near Mumbai, India, killing 74 people and injuring more than 60, many of them construction workers and their families sleeping at the site. The building had been erected with substandard materials on unapproved land, and its collapse was among India's deadliest building failures in years.

04-04.title: First Battle of Fallujah
04-04.description: US Marines besieged Fallujah in response to the killing of four American private security contractors, in the first major battle of the Iraq insurgency. Approximately 800 Iraqis were killed, including an estimated 572-616 civilians per Iraq Body Count, more than 300 of them women and children.

11-30.title: Super Typhoon Durian and Mayon mudflows
11-30.description: Super Typhoon Durian struck the Bicol region of the Philippines on November 30, 2006, and its torrential rainfall triggered massive mudflows of loose volcanic debris on the slopes of Mayon Volcano, burying villages such as Padang, Busay and Daraga under metres of mud and boulders. At least 1,400 people died in the Philippines, with hundreds more missing, and dozens more were killed when the weakened storm crossed Vietnam; the disaster affected about 3.5 million people and left roughly 120,000 homeless.
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)

11-30.title: Philippines typhoon series and Quezon floods
11-30.description: A series of four typhoons and tropical storms, including Tropical Depression Winnie and Typhoon Nanmadol, brought torrential rain to the Philippines in late November and early December, triggering massive floods and landslides in Quezon Province. The storms killed 1,060 people and left 566 missing, according to the World Health Organization, with most deaths caused by Winnie.

01-05.title: Iraq insurgency attacks — 2012
01-05.description: Violence surged across Iraq in 2012 as Sunni insurgent groups intensified attacks, particularly bombings against Shiite civilians. Iraq Body Count documented 4,622 violent civilian deaths from about 2,100 incidents, the first year-over-year rise since 2009, with major coordinated bombings in January, February, March, and June each killing 50-90 people in a single day.

01-05.title: Tel Aviv Central Bus Station double suicide bombing
01-05.description: Two Palestinian suicide bombers detonated explosives about 600 feet apart near the old central bus station in Tel Aviv during the evening rush hour, killing 23 civilians and wounding more than 100, most of them foreign workers. The al-Aqsa Martyrs Brigade claimed responsibility.

02-18.title: Samjhauta Express bombing
02-18.description: Two bombs hidden in luggage exploded aboard the Samjhauta Express passenger train near Panipat, Haryana, India, around midnight on February 18, 2007, killing 68 people, mostly Pakistani citizens. The blasts occurred in coaches carrying passengers between India and Pakistan, and a resulting fire intensified the toll.

02-18.title: Daegu subway fire
02-18.description: An arsonist set flammable liquid ablaze aboard a train at Jungangno Station, and the fire spread to a second train pulling into the station, killing 192 people and injuring more than 140. Most victims died of asphyxiation after the second train's doors were sealed when power was cut.

02-19.title: Sudan famine confirmed in North Darfur camps
02-19.description: In February 2025, the United Nations confirmed famine conditions in at least five areas of Sudan, including the Zamzam, Abu Shouk and Al Salam displacement camps in North Darfur and two locations in the Western Nuba Mountains. The Sudan Doctors Union estimated in January 2025 that about 522,000 children had died from malnutrition since the civil war began, amid widespread aid access restrictions imposed by the warring parties.

02-19.title: Hanau far-right shootings
02-19.description: On the evening of 19 February 2020, 43-year-old Tobias Rathjen attacked two shisha bars and a kiosk in Hanau, Germany, killing nine people and wounding others, deliberately targeting people of immigrant backgrounds. He then returned home, where he killed his mother and himself. German authorities classified the attack as a far-right terrorist act motivated by racism, xenophobia and conspiracy beliefs, after finding a manifesto written by the perpetrator.

02-19.title: Pasta de Conchos coal mine explosion
02-19.description: A methane gas explosion at the Pasta de Conchos coal mine near Sabinas, Coahuila on February 19, 2006 killed 65 miners. Rescue operations were called off weeks later without recovering the bodies of 63 of the dead, and the disaster prompted criticism of mine safety enforcement and workers' rights in Mexico's coal industry.
sources: Mexican Labour and Social Welfare Ministry

02-19.title: Iran Ilyushin Il-76 military plane crash
02-19.description: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards Ilyushin Il-76 military transport crashed into Mount Sirach in heavy snow and high winds while descending to land near Kerman, killing all 275 people aboard, mostly Guards personnel returning from leave. Investigators attributed the crash to controlled flight into terrain during the descent.

02-20.title: South Sudan famine declared
02-20.description: On 20 February 2017 the United Nations formally declared famine in parts of South Sudan's Unity State (Leer and Mayendit counties), the first famine declared anywhere since 2011. The UN estimated that 100,000 people were in famine conditions, with roughly 4.9 million people needing emergency food assistance and a further one million on the brink of famine. Armed conflict and a collapsed economy prevented aid access; famine-related excess deaths in 2017 were estimated in the tens of thousands (best estimate ~20,000), with UNICEF reporting severe acute malnutrition rates far above emergency thresholds. The famine officially subsided in mid-2017 but hunger conditions persisted across the country.

02-20.title: The Station nightclub fire
02-20.location: West Warwick, Rhode Island, United States
02-20.description: Pyrotechnics ignited flammable polyurethane soundproofing foam during a concert at The Station nightclub, engulfing the building within minutes and killing 100 people. More than 200 others were injured, making it one of the deadliest nightclub fires in US history.

02-26.title: Outbreak of the Darfur conflict
02-26.description: Rebel groups attacked a government air base in North Darfur, triggering a counterinsurgency campaign by the Sudanese government and allied Janjaweed militias that killed an estimated 3,000 civilians and displaced more than 600,000 people by the end of 2003. The conflict escalated into a sustained campaign of attacks on civilian villages.

05-16.title: Casablanca bombings
05-16.description: Thirteen suicide bombers attacked Jewish, Spanish, and Italian targets across Casablanca, killing 45 people, including 12 bombers, and wounding more than 100. The attacks were the deadliest in Moroccan history and prompted a large-scale crackdown on Islamist networks.

05-21.title: Boumerdès earthquake
05-21.description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck offshore near Zemmouri in Boumerdès Province, northern Algeria, killing about 2,266 people and injuring more than 10,000. It was the strongest earthquake to hit Algeria since 1980 and left roughly 200,000 people homeless.

07-01.title: Irapuato rehabilitation center massacre
07-01.description: On 1 July 2020, at least three armed men entered the clandestine drug rehabilitation center 'Buscando el Camino a mi Recuperación' in Irapuato, Guanajuato, Mexico, and opened fire, killing 27 people and wounding several others.
