The massacre was linked to the territorial war between the Santa Rosa de Lima and Jalisco New Generation cartels; prosecutors later charged a suspect with aggravated homicide of 27 victims. It was one of a series of attacks on rehabilitation centers in Guanajuato during 2020.

07-01.title: Majiya fuel tanker explosion
07-01.description: In early July 2019, a fuel tanker that had overturned near the village of Majiya in Jigawa State exploded, killing at least 48 people, many of whom had gathered to collect leaking fuel, and leaving dozens more hospitalised with severe burns. Local officials said most of the dead were burnt beyond recognition and the explosion also destroyed nearby properties. The incident highlighted the recurring danger of fuel collection at tanker crash sites across Nigeria, where fuel shortages have driven people to scoop up spilled petrol.

07-01.title: India monsoon floods
07-01.description: The 2019 southwest monsoon caused severe and prolonged flooding across much of India between June and October, with more than 1,600 people killed in rain-related incidents according to reports citing official data. Bihar was among the hardest-hit states, along with Maharashtra, Kerala, Karnataka and Assam, and heavy flooding in the south coincided with torrential rain in Maharashtra's coastal districts. More than a million people were displaced, crops were destroyed and the floods followed unusually heavy August rainfall that came within weeks of drought in parts of the country.

07-01.title: Yemen famine and cholera crisis
07-01.description: The war-ravaged country faced the world's worst humanitarian crisis in 2018: UN agencies reported 8.4 million people one step away from famine and over 22 million in need of assistance, while a massive cholera outbreak killed at least 2,315 people out of more than 1.1 million suspected cases recorded since the epidemic began in 2017. Port restrictions, collapsed health infrastructure, and food insecurity compounded the crisis, with the UN warning that parts of the country could slip into famine.

07-01.title: Niger food crisis
07-01.description: Severe drought and a locust infestation triggered a food crisis in Niger affecting 3.6 million people, with UNICEF reporting 32,000 severely malnourished children under five facing death without treatment. A final death toll was never established; UN officials said thousands of children had already died, with overall mortality estimates ranging from several thousand to tens of thousands.

07-01.title: Yangtze and Huaihe river floods
07-01.description: Seasonal floods along the Huaihe and Yangtze river basins in central and eastern China inundated large areas of Anhui, Jiangsu, and Henan provinces during the summer, killing about 1,551 people and affecting more than 100 million. It was the worst flooding in China since the 1998 Yangtze floods.

07-01.title: Uberlingen mid-air collision
07-01.description: A Bashkirian Airlines Tupolev Tu-154 carrying 69 people, including many children en route to a Spanish holiday, collided with a DHL cargo Boeing 757 over southern Germany. All 71 people on both aircraft died.

07-08.title: Gaza War (Operation Protective Edge)
07-08.description: Israel and Hamas fought a 50-day conflict in the Gaza Strip from 8 July to 26 August 2014. United Nations figures recorded 2,251 Palestinian deaths, including 1,462 civilians and 540 children, alongside 66 Israeli soldiers, six Israeli civilians and one foreign national. More than 11,000 people were injured and hundreds of thousands displaced by airstrikes, rocket fire and ground operations.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

07-08.title: Sudan Airways Flight 139 crash
07-08.description: A Sudan Airways Boeing 737 crashed into terrain near Port Sudan shortly after takeoff following an engine failure, killing 116 of the 117 people on board. The crew missed the runway on the emergency approach in poor visibility.

07-18.title: Second siege of Monrovia
07-18.description: LURD rebels besieged the Liberian capital Monrovia from June to August 2003, shelling civilian neighborhoods, churches, and schools and killing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 civilians. The siege ended when President Charles Taylor went into exile and international peacekeepers arrived.
sources: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights

08-01.title: Sudan Famine and Humanitarian Crisis
08-01.description: In August 2024, the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) confirmed famine conditions in Zamzam displacement camp near El Fasher, North Darfur — the first famine declaration anywhere in the world since 2011 — amid the civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. Independent monitors recorded more than 61,000 people killed in the conflict since April 2023, humanitarian agencies reported child malnutrition deaths in the camp, and the UN said more than 25 million people across Sudan were facing acute food insecurity.

08-01.title: European heat wave
08-01.description: An extreme heat wave across Western and Central Europe, peaking in the first half of August, caused an estimated 70,000 excess deaths, including about 15,000 in France. Temperatures exceeded 40 degrees Celsius for consecutive days, and most victims were elderly people living without air conditioning.
sources: French Institute for Public Health Surveillance (InVS)

08-01.title: Bombing at Moscow restaurant kills three
08-01.description: An improvised explosive device detonated on Saturday evening near a restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in central Moscow, killing three people and injuring 21. Russia's National Anti-Terrorism Committee said a woman carrying the device was killed in the blast; a security guard who had stopped her from entering the restaurant and a restaurant visitor were the other two fatalities.

08-01.title: Plane crash near Nazca kills 13
08-01.description: A small plane crashed in farmland about 6 km from the city of Nazca in Peru's southern Ica region on Saturday, killing all 13 on board — 11 tourists plus the pilot and co-pilot. Local media reported that seven Italians, two Germans and two Spaniards were among the dead; the flight was on a tour route over the Nazca Lines.

08-01.title: Shooting at In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls
08-01.description: A gunman opened fire in the area of an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho, shortly before 2:30 p.m. local time on Saturday, killing at least three people and wounding two. Officials said the gunman was no longer considered a threat, and the investigation remained active.

08-01.title: Israeli strikes kill at least seven in Gaza
08-01.description: Israeli airstrikes and shelling across the Gaza Strip killed at least seven Palestinians on Saturday, according to Gaza's civil defence, and strikes near Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital destroyed two warehouses storing medical supplies and damaged the outpatient clinic. The attacks came a day after Hamas said it agreed to the next stage of a US-backed ceasefire plan.

08-01.title: Seven armed robbers killed in Kabul police operation
08-01.description: Seven armed robbers were killed in an exchange of fire with Afghan police in Police District 8 of Kabul on Saturday night, and 16 people were arrested on suspicion of armed robbery, the Taliban-run police said. The group was accused of earlier storming a residence in the Beni Hisar area and fatally shooting two members of a family.

08-01.title: Assam flood death toll reaches 82
08-01.description: The death toll in ongoing monsoon floods in India's northeastern state of Assam rose to 82 on Saturday, with two people still missing. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the floods hit 2,251 villages and affected more than 1.1 million people; Sivasagar district reported the highest toll with 42 deaths, followed by Charaideo with 21 and Jorhat with 9.

08-01.title: Russian missile barrage on Kyiv kills ten
08-01.description: In a heavy ballistic missile attack early on Saturday, Russia struck Kyiv and the surrounding region, killing 10 people and wounding more than 30. It was the second major attack on the capital that week; President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had run out of Patriot interceptor missiles.

08-19.title: Baghdad Ministry Bombings
08-19.description: On August 19, 2009, coordinated truck bombings hit the Iraqi Foreign Ministry and Finance Ministry in Baghdad, along with other explosions, killing at least 95 people and wounding about 563 according to Iraqi Interior Ministry officials. The attacks, blamed on al-Qaeda-linked militants and Baathist elements, were the bloodiest day in Baghdad since February 2008 and the worst since US troops withdrew from Iraqi cities at the end of June 2009.

08-19.title: Les Issers police academy suicide bombing
08-19.description: A suicide bomber rammed an explosives-filled car into a line of young applicants waiting outside a gendarmerie training academy in Les Issers, about 60 km east of Algiers, on 19 August 2008, killing at least 43 people and wounding about 45. The dead included 42 civilians, mostly men aged 18-20 queuing for entrance exams, and one gendarme. It was the deadliest attack in Algeria in years, with al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb suspected, though no group immediately claimed responsibility.

08-19.title: Abidjan toxic waste dumping (Probo Koala)
08-19.description: Around August 19, 2006, the tanker Probo Koala, chartered by the Dutch commodities firm Trafigura, discharged about 500 tonnes of chemical waste containing sulphur compounds and petroleum slops at roughly 17 open-air sites around Abidjan, Ivory Coast. The dumping caused at least 17 deaths and led an estimated 100,000 people to seek hospital treatment for nausea, respiratory difficulties, skin lesions and other symptoms; the resulting scandal caused the Ivorian government to resign, and a UN investigation found prima facie evidence linking the waste to the deaths and illnesses.

08-19.title: Canal Hotel (UN Baghdad headquarters) bombing
08-19.description: A suicide truck bomb destroyed the Canal Hotel, the UN headquarters in Baghdad, killing 22 people, including the UN special representative Sergio Vieira de Mello and other UN staff. It remains one of the deadliest attacks ever directed at the United Nations.

08-25.title: Rohingya clearance operations, Myanmar
08-25.description: Following attacks on security posts on 25 August 2017, Myanmar's military launched 'clearance operations' in Rakhine State that combined mass killings, arson of villages, rape and mass displacement of the Rohingya Muslim population. Médecins Sans Frontières estimated at least 6,700 Rohingya, including 730 children, were killed in the first month alone, most by gunshots or burned in their homes, with later research suggesting 24,000 or more killed over the longer campaign. Over 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh, and UN investigators later concluded the military's acts constituted genocide and crimes against humanity.

08-25.title: Mumbai twin bomb blasts
08-25.description: Twin car bombs exploded at the Gateway of India and the Zaveri Bazaar jewellery market during the lunch hour, killing 52 people and injuring more than 200. Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba was suspected, and three people were later convicted for the attack.

08-29.title: Hurricane Katrina
08-29.description: Hurricane Katrina made landfall on the US Gulf Coast, breached New Orleans' levee system and flooded about 80% of the city, causing 1,833 confirmed deaths across the affected states. It remains the costliest hurricane in US history, with damage estimated at $81 billion.

08-29.title: Imam Ali Mosque bombing in Najaf
08-29.description: A car bomb exploded outside the Imam Ali Mosque in Najaf as worshippers left Friday prayers, killing Ayatollah Mohammed Baqir al-Hakim and about 95 people and wounding more than 200. It was one of the deadliest attacks in Iraq since the fall of Baghdad.

11-15.title: Cyclone Sidr
11-15.description: Cyclone Sidr struck Bangladesh on November 15, 2007, with sustained winds of about 215 km/h and a storm surge exceeding five meters in places. The official death toll was 3,447, with some estimates as high as 15,000; the districts of Barguna and Patuakhali were hardest hit.

11-15.title: Istanbul bombings
11-15.description: Al-Qaeda truck bombers attacked two synagogues in Istanbul on November 15 and the British Consulate and HSBC headquarters on November 20, killing 57 people and wounding more than 700. They were the deadliest terrorist attacks in Turkish history.

11-15.title: Podi Coal Mine Explosion
11-15.description: A gas explosion at the Podi coal mine in Shanxi Province killed 33 miners, part of a series of five blasts that killed 99 miners in the province within two weeks in November 2001. The mine had been ordered to fix safety problems after an earlier accident, and its owner was arrested, with China's government subsequently suspending small mines nationwide for safety checks.

02-28.title: Tempe passenger train collision
02-28.description: A passenger train carrying more than 350 people collided head-on with a freight train on the same track near Tempe in central Greece, causing several carriages to catch fire and derail. Fifty-seven people were killed, including many university students returning from a carnival holiday, and dozens were injured. The crash, Greece's deadliest rail disaster, was attributed to human error in signaling, prompting nationwide protests over the state of the country's railway network.

02-28.title: Hilla suicide car bombing
02-28.description: A suicide car bomb exploded beside a queue of police recruits waiting outside a health clinic in Hilla, Iraq, killing 125 people and wounding about 130, many of them civilians shopping in a nearby market. It was the deadliest single attack in Iraq since the 2003 invasion at the time.

02-28.title: 2002 Gujarat riots
02-28.description: Weeks of communal rioting followed the Godhra train burning, with violence concentrated in Ahmedabad and other Gujarat cities. The official death toll was about 1,000, while independent estimates range up to 2,000, most of them Muslims.

03-21.title: China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735 crash
03-21.description: China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735, a Boeing 737-800 flying from Kunming to Guangzhou, crashed into mountainous terrain near Wuzhou, Guangxi, on 21 March 2022 after an unexplained rapid descent from cruising altitude. All 132 people on board, 123 passengers and 9 crew, were killed, making it China's deadliest aviation disaster in decades. The preliminary investigation identified no mechanical failure or crew error, and the cause remained undetermined by the end of 2022.

03-21.title: Battle of Mogadishu (2007)
03-21.description: In March-April 2007, Ethiopian and Somali government forces launched a major offensive against Islamist insurgents in Mogadishu, prompting heavy urban fighting that killed approximately 1,200 civilians in the capital. The year as a whole was the deadliest of the insurgency, with estimates of more than 6,000 people killed in Mogadishu in 2007.

03-21.title: Red Lake High School shooting
03-21.description: A 16-year-old student killed his grandfather and his grandfather's partner, then drove to Red Lake Senior High School on the Red Lake Indian Reservation and killed a security guard, a teacher and five students before killing himself. Ten people died in total, making it the deadliest US school shooting since Columbine.

03-28.title: Myanmar earthquake (magnitude 7.7)
03-28.description: On March 28, 2025, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Sagaing and Mandalay in Myanmar along the Sagaing Fault, collapsing buildings and infrastructure and also killing 18 people in Bangkok, Thailand. Myanmar's military government reported about 3,770 dead, while independent Myanmar media estimates exceeded 5,000, and the true toll was widely considered higher.

03-28.title: Nias-Simeulue earthquake
03-28.description: A magnitude 8.6 earthquake struck off the west coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, causing heavy destruction on Nias Island and killing an estimated 1,300 people, with hundreds killed on Simeulue and the Banyak islands. A small tsunami and widespread building collapses added to the casualties.

04-25.title: Nepal earthquake (Gorkha)
04-25.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the Gorkha district of central Nepal, about 80 km northwest of Kathmandu, triggering avalanches on Mount Everest and landslides across the Himalayas. The Nepal government confirmed 8,857 deaths in Nepal, with at least 107 more in India, China and Bangladesh, for a combined toll of roughly 8,960; more than 21,000 people were injured and over 600,000 buildings were destroyed or damaged. It was Nepal's deadliest earthquake in over 80 years.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)

04-25.title: Amagasaki train derailment
04-25.description: A JR West commuter train derailed on a curve and crashed into an apartment building in Amagasaki, Hyogo Prefecture, killing 107 people and injuring more than 550. The train entered the curve at about 116 km/h against a 70 km/h limit, Japan's worst rail accident in decades.

07-23.title: Kabul twin bombing of Hazara demonstration
07-23.description: Two suicide bombers detonated at a demonstration of the Hazara community's Enlightenment Movement at Dehmazang Square in Kabul, where thousands had gathered to protest the rerouting of the TUTAP power transmission line away from Hazara-dominated areas. At least 97 people were killed and 260 wounded, making it the deadliest attack in Kabul since 2001 at the time. Islamic State's Khorasan branch claimed responsibility, its first major assault on the Afghan capital.

07-23.title: Sharm el-Sheikh bombings
07-23.description: Three bombs exploded in the Red Sea resort town of Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, including two car bombs that hit the Old Market and a hotel in Naama Bay, killing 88 people and wounding about 200. Most of the dead were Egyptians, and it was Egypt's deadliest terrorist attack at the time.

07-26.title: Ahmedabad serial bombings
07-26.description: Between 21 and 22 bombs exploded across Ahmedabad, Gujarat, over about 90 minutes on 26 July 2008, hitting 14 locations including markets, buses, and two hospitals where victims of the first blasts were being treated. The attacks killed 56 people and injured about 240-260, according to official government records, and were carried out by the Indian Mujahideen. In 2022 a special court convicted 49 of 78 accused, sentencing 38 to death.

07-26.title: Mumbai floods
07-26.description: A record 944 mm of rain fell on Mumbai in 24 hours, flooding the city and much of Maharashtra state, halting rail, road and air transport and killing approximately 1,094 people. The flood was among the heaviest in the region's recorded history.

07-26.title: Gansu flash flood at Weiyuan scenic area
07-26.description: A flash flood struck a scenic area in Weiyuan County, Dingxi City, on the afternoon of 26 July 2026, killing 25 people and injuring 23. China's national disaster commission said it would oversee an investigation into the disaster and urged Gansu Province to strengthen disaster prevention, mitigation and relief capacity.

10-05.title: Hurricane Stan
10-05.description: Hurricane Stan triggered torrential rain and catastrophic mudslides across Guatemala, El Salvador and southern Mexico, burying entire villages including Panabaj near Lake Atitlan, where about 1,400 residents were declared missing and presumed dead. More than 1,600 people were killed across the region, most of them in Guatemala.

10-08.title: Kunduz mosque bombing
10-08.description: A suicide bomber attacked a Shia mosque in Kunduz during Friday prayers, killing about 100 worshippers and wounding dozens more. The Islamic State affiliate in Khorasan (ISIS-K) claimed responsibility, and the attack was among the deadliest in Afghanistan following the Taliban takeover in August, targeting the country's Shia Hazara minority.

10-08.title: Sanaa funeral hall airstrike
10-08.description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike struck a large funeral hall in Sanaa's Sabeen district during a mourning ceremony for the father of Houthi-appointed Interior Minister Jalal al-Rowaishan. At least 155 people were killed and more than 525 wounded, including senior Houthi figures. The attack drew international condemnation, the United States said it would reassess support for the coalition, and the coalition later acknowledged an error in conducting the strike.

10-08.title: Yemen wedding party airstrike
10-08.description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a wedding party in a village near the Red Sea port of Mokha in Taiz governorate, Yemen, killing at least 131 people, including many women and children, and wounding hundreds. Yemeni officials and residents reported the toll, and Human Rights Watch documented the attack; the coalition later acknowledged the strike and said it had been a mistake.

10-08.title: Kashmir earthquake
10-08.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck near Muzaffarabad in Pakistani-administered Kashmir, collapsing tens of thousands of poorly built homes and schools and killing an estimated 75,000 people in Pakistan and more than 1,300 in India, with regional estimates reaching 87,000. About 3.5 million people were left homeless.

10-29.title: Valencia Flash Floods (DANA)
10-29.description: On October 29, 2024, a cut-off low pressure system (DANA) brought torrential rain to eastern Spain, causing flash floods that swept through the province of Valencia and killed at least 232 people, with dozens more reported missing. The floods destroyed homes and vehicles across dozens of municipalities and displaced thousands, prompting one of Spain's largest peacetime rescue operations.

10-29.title: Seoul Halloween crowd crush (Itaewon)
10-29.description: During Halloween celebrations on 29 October 2022, a crowd crush in a narrow sloping alley in Seoul's Itaewon district killed 159 people, mostly in their twenties and thirties, and injured about 196 more. The crush occurred when a crowd of thousands packed into the alleyway became compressed as people surged from above. Government and police investigations subsequently found serious failings in crowd management and emergency response.

10-29.title: Mogadishu car bombings
10-29.description: On 29 October 2022, two car bombs exploded within minutes of each other near the Ministry of Education in Mogadishu, Somalia, during heavy traffic at the K-5 junction. At least 121 people were killed and more than 300 injured, including many women and children. The al-Qaeda-linked group al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for one of the deadliest attacks in Somalia's recent history.

10-29.title: Lion Air Flight 610 crash
10-29.description: Lion Air Flight 610, a Boeing 737 MAX 8, crashed into the Java Sea 13 minutes after taking off from Jakarta en route to Pangkal Pinang, killing all 189 people on board. The aircraft had experienced airspeed and sensor problems on its previous flight. The crash was the first fatal accident involving the Boeing 737 MAX and led to investigations into the aircraft's Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System, which later factored into the worldwide grounding of the model.

10-29.title: Balochistan earthquake
10-29.description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck the remote Ziarat and Pishin districts of Balochistan Province in southwestern Pakistan on 29 October 2008, flattening mud-brick villages and triggering landslides. The government's final toll was 215 confirmed dead with several hundred injured (official counts rose from 115 to 236 as reports came in), and about 120,000 people were left homeless in freezing mountain conditions. The UN appealed for emergency shelter after an initial government appeal failed to secure funds.

10-29.title: Delhi serial bombings
10-29.description: Three bombs exploded within half an hour at Paharganj market, on a DTC bus in Govindpuri and at Sarojini Nagar market in New Delhi, killing at least 67 people and injuring more than 200. The blasts occurred days before the Diwali festival.

11-09.title: Mai Kadra massacre
11-09.description: On 9-10 November 2020, in the first days of the Tigray War, hundreds of Amhara civilians were killed in house-to-house raids in the town of Mai Kadra near the Sudanese border. Estimates of the death toll ranged from hundreds to more than 1,100, with a Reuters investigation confirming at least 767 deaths; Amnesty International reported that hundreds were killed, likely by local Tigrayan security forces, police and militias aligned with the TPLF. The massacre was the first documented mass atrocity of the Tigray conflict.

11-09.title: Amman hotel bombings
11-09.description: Three suicide bombers attacked the lobbies of the Grand Hyatt, Radisson SAS and Days Inn hotels in Amman, Jordan, killing 60 people and injuring more than 100, including victims at a wedding reception in the Radisson. Al-Qaeda in Iraq claimed responsibility for the attacks.

11-27.title: Nevsky Express Bombing
11-27.description: On the night of November 27, 2009, a bomb equivalent to roughly 7 kg of TNT derailed the Nevsky Express train traveling from Moscow to St. Petersburg near Bologoye, killing 28 people and injuring about 90. Russian authorities declared the derailment a terrorist attack, blaming militants from the North Caucasus. It was the second bombing on the line, following an explosion in August 2007 that injured dozens.

11-27.title: Dongfeng coal mine explosion
11-27.description: A coal dust explosion at the Dongfeng coal mine in Qitaihe, Heilongjiang Province, killed 171 miners, making it one of China's deadliest mine disasters of 2005. The blast occurred in a year of repeated major mining accidents in China.

01-01.title: New Orleans Bourbon Street truck attack
01-01.description: On January 1, 2025, Shamsud-Din Jabbar drove a pickup truck into crowds celebrating New Year on Bourbon Street, then opened fire, killing 14 people and injuring dozens before being fatally shot by police. The FBI classified the attack as a terrorist act inspired by the Islamic State, to which Jabbar pledged allegiance in videos posted before the attack.

01-01.title: Noto Peninsula Earthquake
01-01.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck the Noto Peninsula in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, on January 1, 2024, triggering tsunami warnings, building collapses, and a major fire in Wajima. The disaster killed 241 people, injured more than 1,300, and destroyed or damaged tens of thousands of homes, with Wajima and Suzu among the hardest-hit towns.

01-01.title: Horn of Africa drought and hunger crisis
01-01.description: Failed rainy seasons through 2022 produced the worst drought in four decades across the Horn of Africa, affecting Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya. A joint WHO-UNICEF-FAO analysis estimated approximately 43,000 excess deaths in Somalia in 2022 alone, about half of them children under five. More than 20 million people across the region faced acute food insecurity, with famine-level hunger reported in parts of Somalia.

01-01.title: Jakarta flood disaster
01-01.description: Record rainfall of nearly 400 mm on New Year's Eve overflowed the Ciliwung and Cisadane rivers, flooding large parts of Jakarta and surrounding areas in the early hours of 1 January 2020. Officials reported 66 deaths, the highest toll from flooding in the city since 2007, with about 60,000 people displaced and more than 397,000 evacuated to higher ground at the peak. Water levels reached 30 to 200 cm across many districts and up to four metres in parts of East Jakarta.

01-01.title: Afghanistan conflict — 2012
01-01.description: UNAMA documented 2,769 civilian deaths and 4,821 injuries in Afghanistan during 2012, making it the first year of decline since UN casualty tracking began, though the toll remained among the highest of the war; several thousand Afghan security forces, international troops (about 400 coalition deaths) and insurgents were also killed. 2012 saw a record spike in insider 'green-on-blue' attacks on coalition personnel.

01-01.title: Kenya post-election violence
01-01.description: After the disputed 27 December 2007 presidential election, in which Mwai Kibaki was declared winner over Raila Odinga, weeks of ethnic and political violence engulfed Kenya in January-February 2008, concentrated in Nairobi, the Rift Valley, Western, and Nyanza provinces. Attacks involved machetes, arson, and police gunfire, killing an estimated 1,100-1,500 people (official inquiries later counted about 1,133-1,220 deaths), displacing some 300,000-600,000 people, and triggering a UN-brokered power-sharing agreement in February 2008.

01-01.title: Iraq War (2007)
01-01.description: 2007 was the second-deadliest year of the Iraq War. Iraq Body Count documented 26,112 violent civilian deaths during the year, driven by sectarian violence, vehicle bombings, and the U.S. troop surge launched in February 2007. Approximately 900 U.S. service members were also killed, making 2007 the deadliest year for coalition forces.

01-01.title: Darfur conflict (ongoing genocide and humanitarian crisis)
01-01.description: Armed conflict between government-aligned Janjaweed militias and rebel groups continued across Darfur throughout 2006, marked by attacks on civilians, mass displacement and a severe humanitarian crisis. A September 2006 study published in the journal Science estimated at least 200,000 deaths since the conflict began in 2003, with estimates up to 300,000-400,000 cited by the UN Secretary-General and other organizations, most deaths resulting from violence, disease and starvation. The Darfur Peace Agreement signed in May 2006 failed to end the fighting, and more than two million people remained displaced.

01-13.title: El Salvador Earthquake
01-13.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck off the Pacific coast of El Salvador, killing 944 people and injuring more than 4,700, with a massive landslide in Santa Tecla burying hundreds. The quake displaced more than one million people and destroyed or damaged over 100,000 homes.

02-13.title: Texas winter storm Uri
02-13.description: An unusually severe winter storm, Uri, brought record cold and snow across Texas, causing the state's power grid to fail and leaving millions without electricity, heat, or water for days during subfreezing temperatures. At least 246 people died, most from hypothermia, while carbon monoxide poisoning from generators and house fires also claimed lives.

02-13.title: Second El Salvador Earthquake
02-13.description: A magnitude 6.6 aftershock earthquake struck near San Salvador one month after the January quake, killing 315 people and injuring more than 3,000. Thousands of people in and around the capital were left homeless.

06-01.title: Southern Africa food crisis
06-01.description: A regional drought, compounded by failed harvests and high HIV/AIDS prevalence, created a severe food crisis across Malawi, Zimbabwe, Zambia and neighboring countries, leaving more than 10 million people in need of emergency food aid. The WHO projected up to 300,000 excess deaths from hunger and related disease in the worst-affected countries.

06-01.title: Nepalese Royal Palace Massacre
06-01.description: Crown Prince Dipendra shot and killed nine members of Nepal's royal family, including King Birendra and Queen Aishwarya, at the Narayanhity Royal Palace before shooting himself. Dipendra died of his wounds on June 4, and his uncle Gyanendra assumed the throne, with an official inquiry attributing the killings to Dipendra.

06-01.title: Dolphinarium Discotheque Bombing
06-01.description: A Hamas suicide bomber detonated an explosive device outside the Dolphinarium discotheque in Tel Aviv, killing 21 people, most of them teenagers, and wounding about 120. It was one of the deadliest attacks of the Second Intifada.

06-21.title: Afghanistan Drought and Famine Crisis
06-21.description: Afghanistan's third consecutive year of severe drought brought the country to the brink of famine, with FAO and WFP reporting that about 5.5 million people faced severe food shortages by mid-2001. World Bank and UN officials warned of famine conditions and reported thousands of deaths from starvation and exposure, though the total death toll was never precisely counted.

06-23.title: Southern Peru Earthquake
06-23.description: A magnitude 8.4 earthquake struck off the coast of southern Peru, killing roughly 100 people and injuring more than 1,300, with most deaths in the Arequipa region. The quake triggered a tsunami that killed about two dozen people in the Camaná area and damaged or destroyed thousands of buildings, including historic structures in Arequipa.

07-04.title: Highland Park parade shooting
07-04.description: During the 4 July Independence Day parade in Highland Park, Illinois, a gunman opened fire from a rooftop on the crowd below, killing seven people and wounding 48 others. The 21-year-old attacker had legally purchased the rifle used in the shooting. He was charged with 117 felony counts, including 21 counts of first-degree murder.

07-04.title: Typhoon Utor (Feria)
07-04.description: Typhoon Utor struck northern Luzon in early July 2001, killing at least 168 people in the Philippines and dozens more in southern China, with most fatalities caused by landslides and flooding around Baguio City. Nearly one million people across about 20 provinces were affected, and tens of thousands of homes were destroyed.

07-24.title: Angara Airlines Flight 2311 crash
07-24.description: On July 24, 2025, Angara Airlines Flight 2311, an Antonov An-24 turboprop, crashed roughly 16 km from Tynda airport in Amur Oblast, Russia, while landing in poor weather; all 42 passengers and 6 crew members on board died.

07-24.title: Air Algérie Flight 5017 Crash
07-24.description: Air Algérie Flight 5017, an MD-83 flying from Ouagadougou to Algiers, crashed in the Gossi region of Mali on 24 July 2014 about an hour after takeoff. All 110 passengers and six crew members were killed, making it the deadliest accident in the airline's history. French investigators attributed the crash to ice accretion that triggered an aerodynamic stall.

07-24.title: Colombo Airport Attack
07-24.description: LTTE suicide commandos attacked Bandaranaike International Airport and the adjoining air force base near Colombo, killing at least 18 people and destroying or damaging 11-13 aircraft, including several SriLankan Airlines jets. The attack caused an estimated $350 million in losses to the national carrier alone.

09-09.title: Zamboanga City siege
09-09.description: From September 9 to 28, 2013, members of a faction of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) seized coastal districts of Zamboanga City in the Philippines, holding dozens of residents hostage in a three-week standoff that ended in military operations. More than 200 people were killed, mostly MNLF fighters along with 20 soldiers, 5 policemen, and 13 civilians, and over 119,000 residents were displaced.

09-09.title: Assassination of Ahmad Shah Massoud
09-09.description: Two al-Qaeda operatives posing as journalists detonated a bomb hidden in a camera while interviewing Ahmad Shah Massoud, the military leader of the Afghan Northern Alliance, killing him and one other person. The assassination came two days before the September 11 attacks and removed the alliance's most effective commander ahead of the US invasion.

11-25.title: Qala-i-Jangi Fortress Uprising
11-25.description: Taliban and al-Qaeda prisoners revolted at the Qala-i-Jangi fortress near Mazar-i-Sharif, triggering a six-day battle in which up to 400 prisoners, about 73 Northern Alliance fighters, and CIA officer Johnny Spann — the first American killed in combat in the war — died. Only 86 of the more than 400 prisoners survived, including American Taliban fighter John Walker Lindh.

12-01.title: Chennai floods
12-01.description: Torrential northeast-monsoon rains, among the heaviest recorded in a century, flooded Chennai and surrounding districts of Tamil Nadu in late November and December 2015, killing more than 500 people, with at least 422 deaths officially recorded in Tamil Nadu alone. Much of the city remained submerged for weeks, and transport, power and communications were disrupted across a region home to tens of millions of people; neighboring Andhra Pradesh was also affected.

12-01.title: Ben Yehuda Street Bombings
12-01.description: Two Palestinian suicide bombers detonated explosives on Ben Yehuda Street in central Jerusalem, killing 11 civilians, mostly teenagers, and wounding about 180, with a car bomb exploding nearby about 20 minutes later. Hamas claimed responsibility for the attacks.

12-02.title: San Bernardino shooting
12-02.description: A married couple, Syed Rizwan Farook and Tashfeen Malik, opened fire with assault rifles at a holiday gathering of county employees at the Inland Regional Center in San Bernardino, California, killing 14 people and seriously wounding 22. The attackers, who had pledged allegiance to the Islamic State, died in a shootout with police hours later.

12-02.title: Haifa Bus 16 Bombing
12-02.description: A Hamas suicide bomber detonated a nail-studded explosives belt aboard bus 16 in Haifa, killing 15 people and wounding about 40. The attack came about 12 hours after the Ben Yehuda Street bombings and was one of the deadliest attacks of the Second Intifada.

12-13.title: Indian Parliament Attack
12-13.description: Five gunmen from the Pakistan-based groups Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed attacked the Indian Parliament complex in New Delhi, killing nine security personnel and a gardener before being shot dead. The attack brought India and Pakistan to the brink of war, with both sides mobilizing troops along the border.

01-17.title: Gul Plaza shopping mall fire
01-17.description: On 17 January 2026, a fire broke out at the Gul Plaza shopping mall in Karachi, Pakistan, killing at least 79 people and injuring more than 20. The blaze engulfed the multi-storey commercial building, and many victims died trapped in shops and offices; it was among the deadliest building fires in Pakistan's recent history.

01-17.title: Mount Nyiragongo eruption
01-17.location: Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
01-17.description: Mount Nyiragongo erupted on January 17, 2002, sending lava flows through the city of Goma and forcing hundreds of thousands of residents to flee into Rwanda. Estimates of the death toll range from about 45 to 147, with more than 12,000 homes destroyed and roughly 100,000 people displaced.

03-25.title: Kemerovo shopping mall fire
03-25.description: A fire broke out at the Winter Cherry shopping and entertainment complex in Kemerovo, Siberia, Russia, trapping shoppers in the cinema and children's play areas. The blaze killed 60 people, 41 of them children, and injured dozens. Investigators found that fire alarms and exits were malfunctioning or locked, and security guards had failed to guide visitors out; more than 20 officials and private security personnel were later charged in connection with the disaster.

03-25.title: Capitol Hill massacre in Seattle
03-25.description: A gunman, Kyle Huff, opened fire on a house party in the Capitol Hill neighborhood of Seattle on March 25, 2006, killing six people and wounding several others; a seventh victim died in hospital the next day. Huff then killed himself with a shotgun as police officers arrived, and police later found a rifle in his car and notes indicating he had planned the attack.

03-25.title: Nahrin earthquake
03-25.description: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck the Nahrin district of Baghlan Province, collapsing thousands of mud-brick homes in remote villages. Afghan authorities and the UN estimated about 1,800 people killed and up to 4,000 injured.

03-27.title: Lahore Easter park bombing
03-27.description: A suicide bomber detonated in the crowded Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park in Lahore on Easter Sunday, targeting Christian families gathered for the holiday. Seventy-five people were killed, including at least 29 children, and more than 300 were wounded. Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, a faction of the Pakistani Taliban, claimed responsibility for the attack.

03-27.title: Tal Afar truck bombings
03-27.description: Twin truck bombs exploded in Shia residential neighborhoods of Tal Afar, Iraq, on March 27, 2007, killing 152 people and wounding more than 340. The bombs detonated within minutes of each other, collapsing buildings and burying families.

03-27.title: Park Hotel Passover massacre
03-27.description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked the Park Hotel in Netanya during the Passover seder, killing 30 people and wounding about 140. It was one of the deadliest attacks of the Second Intifada and a trigger for Operation Defensive Shield.

05-02.title: Cyclone Nargis strikes Myanmar
05-02.description: Category 4 Cyclone Nargis made landfall over the Ayeyarwady (Irrawaddy) Delta on 2-3 May 2008 with winds of about 215 km/h and a 3.6-meter storm surge, devastating coastal townships including Labutta and Bogale. Myanmar's government reported 84,537 confirmed dead and 53,836 missing, a combined toll of roughly 138,000, with nearly 20,000 injured and an estimated 2.4 million people affected. The Post-Nargis Joint Assessment by the Myanmar government, ASEAN, and the UN confirmed the scale of the catastrophe, which was the deadliest cyclone worldwide since the 1970 Bhola cyclone.

05-02.title: Bojaya massacre
05-02.description: During a battle between FARC and right-wing paramilitaries in Bellavista, a gas-cylinder mortar fired by FARC struck the town church where about 300 civilians had taken refuge. The attack killed 119 people, including roughly 45 children, in the deadliest single incident of Colombia's civil war.

05-25.title: Houla massacre
05-25.description: On 25 May 2012, during the Syrian civil war, at least 108 people were killed in the Houla area, including 49 children and 34 women. UN observers determined that most victims were summarily executed in two separate incidents rather than killed by artillery fire; international reaction led to the expulsion of Syrian diplomats from several countries.

05-25.title: Cyclone Aila
05-25.description: Cyclone Aila, a severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal, made landfall on May 25, 2009, near the Bangladesh-India border, bringing storm surges of up to 6 meters. Final official tallies recorded about 339 deaths across the region, including roughly 190 in Bangladesh and 140 in eastern India's West Bengal state, with hundreds of thousands left homeless and millions affected by flooding and breached embankments.
sources: University of Colorado Natural Hazards Center

05-25.title: China Airlines Flight 611 disaster
05-25.description: China Airlines Flight 611, a Boeing 747 traveling from Taipei to Hong Kong, broke up in mid-air about 20 minutes after takeoff and crashed into the Taiwan Strait. All 225 passengers and crew were killed.

06-18.title: Jerusalem bus 32A bombing
06-18.description: A Palestinian suicide bomber detonated a device aboard Egged bus 32A in Jerusalem during the morning rush hour, killing 19 people and wounding more than 70. It was the deadliest bus bombing in Jerusalem during the Second Intifada.

06-22.title: Afghanistan earthquake (Khost and Paktika)
06-22.description: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck rural districts of Khost and Paktika provinces in southeastern Afghanistan on 22 June 2022, toppling mud-brick homes and triggering landslides. The UN confirmed at least 1,036 deaths and nearly 3,000 injuries, while Afghan authorities reported 1,150 killed, including more than 200 children. The disaster compounded an ongoing humanitarian crisis, leaving many survivors without shelter in a country already affected by severe drought and economic collapse.

06-22.title: Bou'in-Zahra earthquake
06-22.description: A magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck near Bou'in-Zahra in northwestern Iran, destroying virtually all of the region's single-story masonry houses. At least 261 people were killed and about 1,500 injured.

07-27.title: Sknyliv air show disaster
07-27.description: A Ukrainian Air Force Su-27 fighter crashed into a crowd during an aerobatics display at Sknyliv airfield near Lviv. The crash killed 85 people and injured more than 100 spectators.

08-13.title: Central European floods
08-13.description: Days of record rainfall in August 2002 caused catastrophic flooding along the Elbe, Danube and Vltava rivers, inundating Dresden, Prague and other cities. About 110 people died across central Europe and Russia, with damages exceeding $15 billion.

08-13.title: Russian drone and missile attack on Zaporizhzhia kills five
08-13.description: Russian forces launched a combined drone and missile attack on Zaporizhzhia in the early hours, damaging buildings and industrial facilities and causing fires and power outages. Five people were killed and at least 20 were injured, according to the head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, Ivan Fedorov.

08-13.title: Russian drone strike on passenger train in Odesa region kills two
08-13.description: A jet-powered drone struck the locomotive of a passenger train carrying 340 passengers in Ukraine's southern Odesa region, killing the train driver and his assistant. Passengers were unharmed and evacuated to Odesa, according to Ukrainian authorities.

08-13.title: Armed man fatally shot by police at Auckland shopping centre
08-13.description: An armed man fleeing from police was shot and killed at Sylvia Park Shopping Centre in Auckland on Thursday afternoon. Police said the man had stolen an air rifle from a gun shop in Penrose; he was confronted under an overpass and pronounced dead at the scene despite first aid.

08-13.title: Explosion at Port of Rotterdam kills one
08-13.description: An explosion at the Port of Rotterdam in the Netherlands killed at least one person and injured several others on August 13, 2026. Dutch regional broadcaster Rijnmond reported the blast occurred at around 11:30 a.m. local time; Rotterdam police said the cause remained under investigation and emergency services scaled up their response.

08-13.title: Multi-vehicle crash near Accra kills at least 11
08-13.description: A multi-vehicle collision on the Accra-Kumasi highway at Ofankor Barrier in Ghana's capital killed at least 11 people and injured 13 others in the early hours of August 13, 2026, according to the Ghana National Fire Service. The service said it received a distress call at about 4:00 a.m. local time regarding the collision.

08-13.title: Explosion during ordnance disposal in Sevastopol kills five
08-13.description: Five people were killed on August 13, 2026, during the clearance and disposal of explosive ordnance following a Ukrainian UAV attack on Sevastopol, Russian media reported. Four of the dead were pyrotechnicians of the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations (EMERCOM) and one was a security guard.

08-13.title: Israeli strikes kill two Palestinians in Gaza
08-13.description: Israeli airstrikes killed two Palestinians in Gaza on August 13, 2026, the first fatalities in more than a week. Gaza City Police Chief Jamal Mahmoud Abu Kamil, 43, was killed when an airstrike targeted his vehicle on Rashid Street southwest of Gaza City, and Hudhaifa Kawara was killed in an Israeli attack in the al-Amal neighborhood of Khan Younis.

08-13.title: Landslide and water seepage in Chamoli tunnel kills seven workers
08-13.description: A landslide with water seepage inside an under-construction tunnel of the Vishnugad-Pipalkoti hydroelectric project in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, killed seven workers and injured 14 others on August 13, 2026. Rescue teams pulled trapped workers from the tunnel at Pipal Koti as water and debris poured in.

08-13.title: Record rainfall floods eastern Japan, killing nine
08-13.description: Record rainfall from a stalled weather system flooded large parts of Chiba Prefecture east of Tokyo starting August 13, killing nine people and leaving one man missing, with more than a thousand homes inundated and hundreds of residents in evacuation shelters. Rivers overflowed, roads were blocked and thousands of households lost power across the prefecture.

08-13.title: Explosion at Fujian shipyard kills firefighter
08-13.description: A fire broke out on a ship at the Huahai shipbuilding plant in Gantang township, Fu'an, Fujian Province, on the afternoon of August 13, 2026, and an explosion occurred about an hour into firefighting operations. Twelve people were injured, including 10 firefighters, and one firefighter, Chi Kejie, 23, was confirmed dead despite medical efforts, according to the city's fire and rescue bureau.

08-13.title: Fire at Greater Noida wood-cutting shop kills one worker
08-13.location: Shahberi, Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India
08-13.description: A massive fire broke out late at night at a CNC wood-cutting shop in the Shahberi furniture market of Greater Noida West, Uttar Pradesh, killing one young man, Altamas, from suffocation and leaving another, Aman, in serious condition. A short circuit was suspected as the cause; firefighters rescued the two trapped workers and police registered the case.

08-13.title: Car crash into truck in Nagpur kills two students
08-13.description: Two students were killed and one injured when their car crashed into a parked truck in Nagpur, Maharashtra, on the way to a friend's birthday party. CCTV footage of the crash circulated widely on social media.

08-13.title: Bomb blast kills defected naval officer in Sevastopol
08-13.description: Robert Shageyev, a former Ukrainian naval officer who commanded the submarine Zaporizhzhia and defected to Russia during the 2014 annexation of Crimea, was killed by an explosive device in Sevastopol on August 13, 2026, in what regional governor Mikhail Razvozhayev called a targeted assassination plot. Russia's Federal Security Service confirmed the death of the military official and detained a Russian woman suspected of carrying out the attack on instructions from Ukrainian intelligence agencies.

08-13.title: Suspected murder-suicide shooting on Staten Island kills two
08-13.location: Staten Island, New York, United States
08-13.description: A man and a woman were found shot to death in a suspected murder-suicide at a home on Garth Court in Staten Island, New York, on August 13, 2026. Police responded to a domestic incident at the residence, where both were declared dead.

08-13.title: Firecracker factory explosion near Sivakasi kills two workers
08-13.description: At least two workers were killed in a massive explosion and fire at a firecracker factory near Sivakasi in Virudhunagar district, Tamil Nadu. The blast occurred while a newly purchased machine used to mix chemicals was being tested; firefighters battled the blaze and authorities launched an inquiry into safety failures at the plant.

09-26.title: Iguala Mass Kidnapping of 43 Students
09-26.description: On 26 September 2014, municipal police in Iguala, Guerrero, Mexico, confronted students from the Ayotzinapa Rural Teachers' College who had commandeered buses to travel to a protest. Six people were killed and 43 students were abducted and have never been found; investigators concluded police handed them to a drug cartel, which killed them and burned most of the remains. The case triggered a national political crisis in Mexico.

09-26.title: Typhoon Ketsana (Ondoy)
09-26.description: Tropical storm Ketsana (Ondoy) struck the Philippines on September 26, 2009, bringing the heaviest rainfall to Metro Manila in more than four decades — about a month's rain in under 12 hours — and causing catastrophic flash flooding. The consolidated regional death toll reached roughly 900, including 671 in the Philippines, 179 in Vietnam, and dozens more in Cambodia and Laos. Hundreds of thousands were displaced across Southeast Asia.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

09-26.title: MV Le Joola capsizing
09-26.description: The Senegalese ferry MV Le Joola, severely overloaded with an estimated 1,900 people aboard, capsized in a storm off the coast of The Gambia en route to Dakar. Only 64 survivors were rescued, making it one of the deadliest peacetime maritime disasters in history.

10-02.title: Beltway sniper attacks
10-02.description: Over three weeks in October 2002, John Allen Muhammad and Lee Boyd Malvo killed 10 people and wounded 3 in seemingly random shootings across the Washington, D.C., region. The pair killed a total of 17 people during the broader multi-state crime spree.

12-27.title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead) begins
12-27.description: Israel launched Operation Cast Lead on 27 December 2008 with air strikes on Hamas targets in the Gaza Strip, including a missile attack on the Gaza City police headquarters that alone killed about 40 people, followed by a ground invasion on 3 January 2009. Over the 22-day offensive, at least 1,387 Palestinians were killed, including roughly 773 civilians and 320 children, with over 5,000 wounded, according to Palestinian and human-rights organizations; 13 Israelis were also killed. A UN investigation found the offensive used disproportionate force and caused widespread destruction of homes, schools, and hospitals.

12-27.title: Assassination of Benazir Bhutto
12-27.description: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated at a campaign rally in Rawalpindi on December 27, 2007, when a suicide attacker detonated a bomb after opening fire. At least 24 people were killed, including Bhutto, who died shortly afterward at Rawalpindi General Hospital.

12-27.title: Grozny government headquarters bombing
12-27.description: Chechen suicide bombers drove explosive-laden vehicles into the pro-Russian Chechen government headquarters in Grozny. The blast killed 83 people and injured 210 in one of the deadliest attacks of the Second Chechen War.

02-17.title: Kandahar dog-fighting show suicide bombing
02-17.description: A suicide bomber detonated explosives in a crowd of several hundred people watching a dog-fighting competition near Kandahar on 17 February 2008, in an attack believed aimed at a local anti-Taliban auxiliary police commander, Abdul Hakim Jan, who was killed with his guards. The blast killed more than 100 people and wounded about 100 others, making it the deadliest single bombing in Afghanistan since 2001; Kandahar's governor confirmed the toll exceeded 100 as wounded victims died. No group claimed responsibility, though the Taliban denied involvement.

02-17.title: Southern Leyte mudslide buries Guinsaugon village
02-17.description: A rain-triggered mudslide buried the village of Guinsaugon in Saint Bernard, Southern Leyte province on February 17, 2006, following more than a week of heavy rain. The debris slide, reportedly tens of metres deep, covered the entire village including an elementary school holding about 250 pupils; the official death toll reached 1,126 from a population of about 1,857, with only about 57 survivors recovered.

03-19.title: Ulyanovskaya mine disaster
03-19.description: A methane and coal dust explosion at the Ulyanovskaya coal mine in the Kemerovo region of Siberia on March 19, 2006 killed 110 of the 203 miners on shift, one of the worst mining disasters in post-Soviet Russia. An official investigation found the mine's methane monitoring and alarm system had been deliberately disabled before the blast.

03-31.title: Borujerd (Silakhor) earthquake
03-31.description: An earthquake of magnitude 6.1 struck the Silakhor plain region of Lorestan province in western Iran on March 31, 2006, early in the morning, centered near the village of Darb-e Astaneh. The quake killed about 70 people, injured more than 1,200 and damaged or destroyed buildings in roughly 330 villages, with the worst destruction in Borujerd and Dorud.
sources: International Institute of Earthquake Engineering and Seismology (IIEES)

05-27.title: Yogyakarta earthquake
05-27.description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck the Yogyakarta region of central Java on May 27, 2006, at shallow depth along the Opak River fault. The quake killed 5,749 people, injured about 38,500 and destroyed or damaged several hundred thousand buildings, displacing an estimated 600,000 residents, and was the deadliest earthquake of 2006.

07-11.title: Kampala World Cup bombings
07-11.description: Three suicide bombs exploded in Kampala on July 11, 2010, while crowds watched the FIFA World Cup final, killing 74 people and injuring over 70. Two devices were detonated at the Kyadondo Rugby Club and one at the Ethiopian Village restaurant. The Somali militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility, stating the attacks were retaliation for Uganda's participation in the African Union peacekeeping mission in Somalia (AMISOM), marking the first major Al-Shabaab attack outside Somalia.

07-11.title: Mumbai train bombings
07-11.description: Seven bombs hidden in pressure cookers exploded on crowded Western Line suburban commuter trains in Mumbai during evening rush hour on July 11, 2006. The coordinated attacks killed 209 people and injured more than 700, making them among the deadliest terrorist attacks in India's history; the Indian government blamed the Pakistan-based group Lashkar-e-Taiba.

07-12.title: 2006 Lebanon War (33-day conflict)
07-12.description: A 33-day war between Israel and the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah began on July 12, 2006 after Hezbollah captured two Israeli soldiers in a cross-border raid. Israeli airstrikes, naval bombardment and ground operations killed about 1,190 people in Lebanon, most of them civilians, according to the Lebanese government and Human Rights Watch, and displaced about one million people; Hezbollah rocket fire killed about 160 people in Israel, mostly soldiers.

07-14.title: Western European floods
07-14.description: Unprecedented rainfall caused devastating flash floods in western Germany, particularly the Ahr and Erft valleys, and eastern Belgium along the Vesdre river. Around 240 people died, roughly 189 of them in Germany, with dozens more killed in Belgium and other neighboring countries. Thousands lost homes, and scientists linked the extreme rainfall to climate change.

07-14.title: Nice Bastille Day truck attack
07-14.description: A 19-tonne cargo truck driven by Mohamed Lahouaiej-Bouhlel plowed through crowds celebrating Bastille Day on the Promenade des Anglais in Nice for nearly two kilometers before police shot the driver dead. Eighty-six people, including many children, were killed and 458 wounded. Islamic State claimed responsibility for the attack, one of the deadliest in modern French history.

07-14.title: Typhoon Bilis floods and landslides in China
07-14.description: Tropical Storm Bilis made landfall on China's southeastern coast on July 14, 2006, and its torrential rains over six southern provinces triggered severe flash floods, reservoir breaches and mudslides. The final official death toll was 843 people with more than 200 missing, making Bilis China's deadliest storm in a decade; nearly three million people were displaced or evacuated.

07-15.title: 2022 European heatwaves
07-15.description: Consecutive heatwaves through summer 2022 brought record temperatures across Europe, including 40.3 degrees Celsius in the United Kingdom, 47 degrees Celsius in Portugal, and widespread wildfires from Spain to France. A peer-reviewed study by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health estimated 61,672 heat-related deaths across Europe between 30 May and 4 September 2022, a toll that a later analysis revised upward to over 70,000. Excess deaths fell most heavily on the elderly in France, Spain, Germany and Italy.
sources: Barcelona Institute for Global Health (Nature Medicine)

07-15.title: Attempted coup in Turkey
07-15.description: A faction of the Turkish armed forces attempted to overthrow the government on the night of July 15, bombing the parliament building in Ankara, seizing bridges and key infrastructure in Istanbul, and announcing military control of the country. The government, aided by large pro-democracy street protests, regained control within about 24 hours. Estimates of the dead range from 270 to 350, with roughly 300 people killed including about 180 civilians, and more than 2,100 wounded.

07-15.title: Typhoon Rammasun
07-15.description: Typhoon Rammasun, the strongest typhoon to hit the Philippines in decades, made landfall on Luzon in mid-July 2014 before crossing southern China and northern Vietnam. Around 190 people were killed across the three countries, more than a hundred of them in the Philippines, and hundreds of thousands of homes were damaged or destroyed. It was among the deadliest typhoons of the year.

07-15.title: North Korea floods and food crisis
07-15.description: Torrential rains and three major storms in mid-July 2006 caused severe flooding and landslides across North Korea, particularly in South Pyongan, North Hwanghae and Kangwon provinces, destroying about 31,000 houses and inundating tens of thousands of hectares of farmland. Official reports indicated about 600 people dead or missing, while a UN assessment recorded far lower figures and unverified claims reached thousands; the loss of an estimated 100,000 tonnes of food raised fears of famine, and the government rejected most international relief offers.
sources: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)

07-17.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 Shootdown
07-17.description: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 was shot down over eastern Ukraine on 17 July 2014, killing all 298 passengers and crew, including 80 children. The Dutch-led Joint Investigation Team concluded the Boeing 777 was struck by a Russian-made Buk surface-to-air missile fired from territory controlled by pro-Russian separatists. A Dutch court later convicted three men for their roles in the downing.

07-17.title: Pangandaran earthquake and tsunami
07-17.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck south of the Indonesian island of Java on July 17, 2006, generating a tsunami that struck more than 300 kilometres of coastline centred on Pangandaran in West Java. The waves killed about 668 people, left nearly 300 missing, injured about 9,000 and destroyed thousands of buildings, fishing boats and tourist facilities along the southern Java coast.

08-10.title: Typhoon Saomai strikes China
08-10.description: Typhoon Saomai, the strongest typhoon to make landfall on mainland China in 50 years, struck Zhejiang province on August 10, 2006, with maximum sustained winds of about 216 km/h. The storm and its associated rains killed about 460 people in Zhejiang and Fujian provinces, destroyed or damaged hundreds of thousands of houses and coastal dikes, and forced the evacuation of more than a million residents.

08-10.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk kills 13
08-10.description: A large-scale Ukrainian drone attack on industrial and civilian targets in the Russian city of Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan killed at least 13 people, including a child, and injured 39 others, authorities said. It was one of the deadliest Ukrainian strikes inside Russia in the war.

08-10.title: Russian artillery strike on Buhaivka village in Kharkiv region kills five
08-10.location: Buhaivka, Chuhuiv district, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine
08-10.description: Russian forces carried out a massive artillery strike on the residential area of the village of Buhaivka in the Chuhuiv district of Kharkiv Oblast on August 10, killing five people and destroying several houses, according to regional authorities and the prosecutor's office.

08-10.title: Palestinian girl dies of wounds from Israeli fire in Gaza
08-10.location: Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, Gaza Strip, Palestine
08-10.description: Thirteen-year-old Sabah Naim Abdullah al-Hashash died on August 10 from a head wound sustained two days earlier when she was shot by Israeli forces in the Al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip, amid continuing ceasefire violations.

08-10.title: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake in western Colombia kills at least 273
08-10.location: Western Colombia (Choco; Cali, Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo)
08-10.description: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday morning, August 10, killing at least 273 people by August 14, with about 500 still missing and thousands injured, as buildings collapsed across Cali, Pereira, Manizales and Quibdo. The epicenter was in San Jose del Palmar in Choco, about 400 kilometers west of Bogota; Colombia's Geological Service called it the strongest quake recorded in the country this century, and President Abelardo de la Espriella declared an emergency and three days of national mourning to expedite recovery funding.

08-10.title: Ukrainian drone hits Donetsk gas station, killing truck driver
08-10.description: A Ukrainian drone attack on a gas station complex in the Proletarsky district of Donetsk killed a 45-year-old truck driver and wounded a station employee, according to Denis Pushilin, head of the Donetsk People's Republic.

08-10.title: Two custodians killed in shooting at Chicago elementary school
08-10.description: Two school custodians, a 63-year-old man and a 48-year-old woman, were found shot to death inside Mark Twain Elementary School in Chicago's Garfield Ridge neighborhood on Monday afternoon, August 10. Each had a single gunshot wound to the head; police were investigating at least one of the deaths as a homicide, and the circumstances were not immediately clear.

09-08.title: Marrakesh–Safi earthquake
09-08.description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck the High Atlas Mountains south of Marrakesh, Morocco, in the early hours of September 8, devastating remote mountain villages whose largely earthen buildings collapsed. At least 2,960 people were killed and more than 5,600 injured, making it Morocco's deadliest earthquake since 1960. Thousands of survivors were left in temporary camps through the winter.

09-08.title: Malegaon bombings
09-08.description: Three bombs exploded on the evening of September 8, 2006 in the town of Malegaon, Maharashtra, targeting Muslims gathered for the Shab-e-Barat festival: the devices were placed near a mosque, in a cemetery and in a busy market. The blasts killed 37 people and injured more than 100; a curfew was imposed and several suspects were later arrested and convicted in connection with the attacks.

11-23.title: Maguindanao Massacre
11-23.description: On November 23, 2009, a convoy carrying relatives of gubernatorial candidate Esmael Mangudadatu and journalists covering his candidacy filing was stopped by about 100 armed men linked to the ruling Ampatuan clan in Maguindanao province. The 58 people abducted were taken to a hilltop, shot, and buried in shallow graves. Thirty-two of the dead were journalists — the deadliest single event for journalists ever documented by the Committee to Protect Journalists.

11-23.title: Sadr City bombings
11-23.description: A coordinated attack of multiple car bombs and mortar rounds struck the Shia neighbourhood of Sadr City in Baghdad on November 23, 2006, at the height of Iraq's sectarian civil war. At least 215 people were killed and about 250 wounded, making it one of the deadliest single attacks of the conflict up to that point; the Iraqi government imposed a curfew on Baghdad in response.

01-08.title: Tucson mass shooting targeting Rep. Gabrielle Giffords
01-08.description: On January 8, 2011, Jared Lee Loughner opened fire at a constituent event held by U.S. Representative Gabrielle Giffords in a Safeway parking lot in Tucson, Arizona. Six people were killed, including federal judge John Roll and nine-year-old Christina Taylor Green, and 13 others were wounded, including Giffords, who was shot in the head and survived. Loughner was subdued by bystanders and arrested at the scene; he pleaded guilty to 19 federal charges in 2012 and was sentenced to life in prison without parole.

01-24.title: West Bandung landslide
01-24.location: West Bandung Regency, West Java, Indonesia
01-24.description: On 24 January 2026, heavy rainfall triggered a major landslide in West Bandung Regency, West Java, Indonesia, that buried the village of Pasir Langu and killed at least 74 people, with others missing. Rescue operations in the mud-covered area continued for days as dozens of homes were destroyed.

01-24.title: Domodedovo International Airport suicide bombing
01-24.description: On January 24, 2011, a suicide bomber detonated a shrapnel-packed device in the international arrivals hall of Domodedovo Airport, Moscow's busiest airport, killing 37 people and injuring more than 170. The bomber, Magomed Yevloyev, a 20-year-old from Ingushetia, was linked to the Caucasus Emirate insurgent network led by Doku Umarov, who claimed responsibility. Victims included citizens of Russia, Britain, Germany, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and other countries. In 2013, four accomplices were sentenced to prison terms, including three life sentences.

01-25.title: Brumadinho dam disaster
01-25.description: A tailings dam at Vale's Feijão iron-ore mine collapsed on 25 January 2019, releasing a wave of mining waste that buried the mine's cafeteria, administrative buildings and nearby rural homes. The disaster killed 270 people, including 259 confirmed dead and 11 missing who were later declared dead, most of them mine workers and employees eating lunch at the time. It was one of the deadliest industrial accidents in Brazilian history and prompted investigations into dam safety standards at mining companies.

01-25.title: Egyptian Revolution of 2011
01-25.description: Mass protests against the rule of President Hosni Mubarak began across Egypt on January 25, 2011, and continued for 18 days until Mubarak's resignation on February 11. Security forces used live ammunition, tear gas and beatings against demonstrators, primarily in Cairo's Tahrir Square and other cities. Egypt's official fact-finding commission reported that 846 people were killed and 6,467 injured during the uprising, which it determined involved unlawful police use of lethal force against protesters.

02-15.title: Petropolis floods and mudslides
02-15.description: On 15 February 2022, intense rainfall dumped more than 250 millimetres of water in a few hours on the mountainous Brazilian city of Petropolis, triggering flash floods and hundreds of mudslides. At least 231 people were killed and more than 1,000 displaced, making it the deadliest disaster in the city's history. The slides buried entire neighbourhoods, and many victims were killed inside cars and homes.

02-15.title: Libyan civil war and NATO intervention
02-15.description: Anti-government protests erupted in Benghazi on February 15, 2011, and escalated into a nationwide armed rebellion against the rule of Muammar Gaddafi. A UN-mandated NATO bombing campaign began in March, and fighting continued until the fall of Tripoli in August and Gaddafi's capture and killing on October 20, 2011. Estimates of the conflict's death toll range from about 20,000 to 30,000; a 2013 statistical study published by The New York Times estimated approximately 25,000 killed during the eight-month conflict, including thousands of civilians.

04-16.title: Ecuador earthquake (M7.8)
04-16.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck off Ecuador's northern Pacific coast at a depth of about 20 kilometers, devastating coastal towns including Pedernales, Manta, and Portoviejo in Manabí Province, which accounted for more than three-quarters of casualties. At least 676 people were killed, about 27,700 were injured, and tens of thousands of buildings were destroyed or damaged, making it Ecuador's worst natural disaster since 1949.

04-16.title: Kumamoto earthquakes
04-16.description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture on the island of Kyushu on April 16, following a magnitude 6.2 foreshock two days earlier. At least 50 people were killed directly by the quakes, with more than 270 deaths attributed to the disaster once earthquake-related causes were counted, and 2,809 were injured. The quakes triggered landslides and damaged tens of thousands of structures across Kumamoto and Oita prefectures.

04-16.title: Sewol Ferry Sinking
04-16.description: The South Korean ferry Sewol capsized and sank off the coast of Jindo on 16 April 2014 while carrying 476 people, most of them Danwon High School students on a field trip. The vessel listed sharply and sank within hours; 304 people died, including 250 students, while 172 survived. Overloading, improperly secured cargo and crew failures were blamed, leading to criminal convictions of the captain, crew and operator.

04-16.title: Nigeria post-election violence
04-16.description: Following the April 16, 2011 presidential election, in which incumbent Goodluck Jonathan defeated northern candidate Muhammadu Buhari, riots and sectarian violence broke out across at least 12 northern states, including Kaduna, Kano, Bauchi and Borno. Human Rights Watch documented that more than 800 people were killed over roughly three days, with churches, mosques, homes and shops burned and more than 65,000 people displaced. Security forces were also documented as having unlawfully killed unarmed residents in several incidents.

04-16.title: Virginia Tech shooting
04-16.description: On April 16, 2007, a student gunman killed 32 people and wounded 17 in two separate attacks at Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University in Blacksburg, Virginia, before killing himself. It was the deadliest school shooting in U.S. history at the time.

04-27.title: Afghanistan flash floods
04-27.description: In late April 2025, heavy rains triggered flash floods across northern Afghanistan, with the worst destruction in Baghlan Province, where entire villages were swept away; at least 150 people were killed across the affected provinces per BBC reporting, while the World Food Programme estimated more than 300 dead and hundreds more injured.

04-27.title: 2011 Super Outbreak tornadoes
04-27.description: Between April 25 and 28, 2011, a record outbreak of 360 tornadoes struck 21 US states from Texas to New York, with 216 tornadoes touching down on April 27 alone. The outbreak killed 324 people across six states, including 238 in Alabama, and injured more than 3,100; four tornadoes were rated EF5. The deadliest tornado, the Hackleburg-Phil Campbell EF5 in Alabama and Tennessee, killed 72 people. It was the deadliest US tornado outbreak since 1936, with damages exceeding US$10 billion.

05-22.title: Qinyuan coal mine explosion
05-22.description: On 22 May 2026, an explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Qinyuan County, Shanxi Province, China, killed at least 82 miners, the worst coal-mining blast in China in more than a decade. The blast in one of China's major coal-producing regions prompted a state investigation into safety practices.

05-22.title: Manchester Arena bombing
05-22.description: A suicide bomber detonated a homemade shrapnel-laden device in the foyer of Manchester Arena as thousands of mostly young fans were leaving an Ariana Grande concert on 22 May 2017. The blast killed 22 people, including a number of children and teenagers, and injured more than 1,000. The attacker, Salman Abedi, died in the explosion; the Islamic State claimed responsibility, and British authorities judged it a terrorist attack carried out by a local cell with support from his brother.

05-22.title: Joplin tornado
05-22.description: On the evening of May 22, 2011, a violent EF5 tornado, the first to strike Missouri since 1957, carved a path roughly one mile wide and 22 miles long directly through the city of Joplin. It killed 158 people directly (with several additional indirect deaths), injured more than 1,000, destroyed over 4,000 homes and severely damaged St. John's Regional Medical Center. It was the deadliest single US tornado since 1947 and the costliest on record at the time, with damage estimated at US$2.8 billion.

05-22.title: Air India Express Flight 812 crash
05-22.description: Air India Express Flight 812, a Boeing 737-800 flying from Dubai to Mangalore, overshot the runway while landing on May 22, 2010, plunged down a gorge, and caught fire, killing 158 of the 166 people on board, in the deadliest aviation accident in India's history. The aircraft broke into pieces before sliding down the embankment into a valley near the end of the tabletop runway at Mangalore International Airport. India's Directorate General of Civil Aviation investigation cited pilot error in landing short of the designated touchdown zone.
sources: Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), India

07-13.title: Mastung election rally bombing
07-13.description: A suicide bomber detonated an explosive vest at an election rally of Awami National Party candidate Siraj Raisani in Mastung, Balochistan province, days before Pakistan's general election. The attack killed 131 people and wounded over 100, including Raisani himself. The Islamic State Khorasan Province claimed responsibility, and it was the deadliest attack in Pakistan in several years, following a separate bombing the same day in Peshawar that killed over 20 people.

07-13.title: Mumbai triple bombings
07-13.description: On July 13, 2011, three improvised explosive devices hidden on a parked motorcycle, in a tiffin box and on an electric pole exploded within 11 minutes at crowded commercial locations in Mumbai: Zaveri Bazaar, Opera House and Dadar. The blasts killed 26 people and injured more than 130 during evening rush hour. No group claimed responsibility initially; investigations linked the attack to the Indian Mujahideen network, and authorities later named co-founder Yasin Bhatkal as the alleged mastermind.

07-20.title: Henan floods
07-20.description: Torrential rain described as a once-in-a-millennium event inundated Zhengzhou and surrounding areas of Henan province, flooding subway lines, underpasses, and neighborhoods. At least 398 people died across Henan, including 302 in Zhengzhou, where dozens drowned inside subway cars. More than one million residents were evacuated.

07-20.title: Syrian civil war — 2012 escalation
07-20.description: The Syrian civil war escalated dramatically in 2012, from protests to full-scale urban warfare including the Battle of Aleppo from July. Monitors estimated about 50,000 people were killed during the year alone (SOHR's year-by-year count was 52,916, including 22,663 civilians), and the UN reported more than 60,000 cumulative deaths since March 2011 by early 2013; massacres such as Houla and Daraya and indiscriminate shelling of civilian areas accounted for a large share of casualties.

07-20.title: Aurora theater shooting
07-20.description: On 20 July 2012, during a midnight premiere screening of 'The Dark Knight Rises' at a Cinemark theater in Aurora, Colorado, a gunman opened fire, killing 12 people and wounding 70 others (58 by gunfire). The shooter, James Holmes, was convicted and sentenced to 12 consecutive life terms. It was the deadliest mass shooting in the US at that time.

07-20.title: Horn of Africa famine in Somalia
07-20.description: The UN declared famine in July 2011 in parts of southern Somalia following the Horn of Africa's worst drought in 60 years, as failed harvests, food price spikes, and the al-Shabaab insurgency's block on aid deliveries combined with underfunded relief efforts.
