A joint FAO/FEWS NET study published in May 2013 estimated that approximately 258,000 people died from famine and severe food insecurity in Somalia between October 2010 and April 2012, including about 133,000 children under five, with peak death rates of 30,000 per month between May and August 2011. The famine was declared over in February 2012.

07-25.title: 2011 Thailand floods
07-25.description: Torrential monsoon rains from late July 2011 triggered the worst flooding in Thailand in more than half a century, affecting 65 of the country's 77 provinces and about 13.6 million people over more than five months. Official figures recorded 815 deaths and three missing. Floodwaters inundated Bangkok's outskirts and submerged large parts of the central plains, destroying millions of acres of crops and crippling the country's industrial estates, including hard-disk drive and automobile factories, with total economic damages estimated at around US$45 billion.
sources: Thai Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

08-14.title: Haiti earthquake
08-14.description: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck near Petit-Trou-de-Nippes in southwestern Haiti, killing at least 2,207 people and injuring about 12,000. The quake destroyed homes, churches, and hospitals in the southern cities of Les Cayes and Jérémie, displacing hundreds of thousands of people, with Tropical Depression Grace adding rain and mudslides days later.

08-14.title: Freetown mudslide and floods, Sierra Leone
08-14.description: After days of torrential rain, a hillside above the Babadorie River valley collapsed on 14 August 2017, sending a wall of mud and debris through the Regent district on the outskirts of Freetown, burying homes and residents as they slept. The final official death toll declared 1,141 dead or missing, with more than 3,000 people displaced and hundreds of children orphaned, according to the World Bank's damage and loss assessment. Deforestation and unregulated hillside construction were cited by authorities as factors amplifying the disaster.

08-14.title: Rabaa massacre
08-14.description: On August 14, 2013, Egyptian security forces violently dispersed sit-in camps of supporters of deposed President Mohamed Morsi at Rabaa al-Adawiya and al-Nahda squares in Cairo. At least 817 people and more than 1,000 by some counts were killed (Human Rights Watch documented 904-1,000+, while the government reported 638), including four journalists; HRW called it one of the largest single-day killings of demonstrators in recent history.

08-14.title: 2011 Pakistan monsoon floods
08-14.description: Heavy monsoon rains from mid-August to mid-September 2011 caused severe flooding across southern Pakistan, with the province of Sindh the hardest hit, followed by Balochistan. The official damage assessment recorded 520 deaths (497 in Sindh and 23 in Balochistan), about 9.6 million people affected, and more than 1.5 million homes damaged. The floods destroyed over a million acres of crops and livestock, compounding the effects of the record 2010 floods, and forced roughly 744,000 people to be displaced.

08-14.title: Qahtaniya Yazidi community bombings
08-14.description: Four suicide truck bombers attacked the Yazidi towns of Qahtaniya and Jazira in Nineveh Province, Iraq, on August 14, 2007, killing 796 people and wounding more than 1,500. The coordinated blasts, which destroyed entire residential blocks, remain the deadliest car bomb attack of the Iraq War.

08-14.title: Russian double drone strike on Sumy region kills woman and nine-year-old boy
08-14.description: Russian forces launched a double strike with jet-powered UAVs on a private home in the Buryn community of Ukraine's Sumy region early on August 14, 2026, killing a 29-year-old woman and her nine-year-old son and wounding four others, including the boy's father and grandmother who were hospitalized with severe burns. The attack caused extensive damage and sparked a fire, according to the Sumy Regional Military Administration.

08-14.title: Russian glide bomb hits apartment block in Donetsk region, killing one
08-14.description: A Russian glide bomb demolished six floors of a 10-story apartment block in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region on August 14, 2026, killing one person and wounding at least 16 others, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Reports from Kramatorsk described 17 wounded in the glide bomb attack.

08-14.title: Helicopter crash in Sehmatal, Saxony kills pilot
08-14.description: A helicopter crashed and burned in a forest near Sehmatal in the Erzgebirge, Saxony, at about 9:55 a.m. on August 14, 2026, killing the pilot. Workers pulled the pilot from the aircraft but he died at the crash site. The helicopter had been in use for lime-spreading in the forest; criminal police and the German Federal Bureau of Aircraft Accident Investigation began investigating the cause.

08-14.title: Series of shootings in Michigan kills six including gunman
08-14.description: A 39-year-old gunman, Chad Hickman, killed five people and then himself in a series of shootings across Michigan on August 14, 2026. Police responding to a home in Missaukee County found three people dead and another critically injured; a fourth victim was found at another home during a large-scale manhunt, and Hickman's body and another dead person were found in woods near Whitlock Lake in Caldwell Township. A motive was not immediately known.

08-14.title: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake off Indonesia kills at least 53
08-14.location: Nagekeo District, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
08-14.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Mbay Village in Nagekeo District, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, at 5:58 a.m. local time on August 15 (21:58 UTC August 14). The death toll rose to at least 53 as rescuers dug through rubble and landslide debris, with thousands of displaced people spending nights outdoors fearing aftershocks. Buildings toppled in Maumere and elsewhere, and Indonesia's BMKG issued a Level II tsunami warning after the tremor triggered minor tsunami waves across several coastal areas.

08-14.title: Coal mine explosion in Cucunuba kills six miners
08-14.description: Six miners died in a coal mine explosion in Cucunuba, Cundinamarca. The Cundinamarca governor said the mine had no permit to operate; bodies of the trapped workers were recovered after rescue efforts. The mine had been reported as operating despite being suspended by the authorities.

08-14.title: Toxic gas leak at Sitakunda shipbreaking yard kills nine workers
08-14.description: At least nine workers died and ten others were taken seriously ill after inhaling toxic gas that leaked while they were carrying out housekeeping work aboard a ship at Ferdous Steel Shipbreaking Yard in Sitakunda, Chattogram, on the morning of August 14. Hydrogen sulphide was detected inside the ship; the death toll rose from eight to nine as one more worker died in hospital.

08-14.title: RSF attack on Um Arada near El Obeid kills at least 18 civilians
08-14.description: Rapid Support Forces attacked Um Arada, about 20 km southwest of El Obeid, capital of North Kordofan, killing at least 18 people and wounding 17 others, according to local sources and Sudanese media. The incursion also affected two other localities; about 300 families fled to El Obeid. A Sudanese rights group said more than 14 civilians were killed.

08-14.title: Mudslide in Changxing, Zhejiang kills one and leaves three missing
08-14.description: A mudslide triggered by short-duration heavy rain and rising water struck Heping Town's Tanlongqiao Village in Changxing County, Zhejiang, at about 6:30 a.m. on August 14, collapsing one house. By 2:30 p.m. the same day one person had died and three were missing, with rescue operations under way. China's Ministry of Water Resources upgraded a yellow flood warning for Jiangsu, Shanghai, Zhejiang and Anhui as heavy rain continued.

11-10.title: Shizong coal mine gas outburst
11-10.description: On the morning of November 10, 2011, a methane gas outburst struck the Sizhuang coal mine in Shizong County, Yunnan Province, China, trapping 43 miners working underground. Rescue teams recovered 35 bodies, with 8 miners never found; the official toll is 43 trapped miners. The privately operated mine had its safety production license revoked in 2010 and had been ordered to stop production, and China's work safety administration said safety monitoring was very poor. Four mine bosses and four local officials were detained, and the accident was the deadliest in Yunnan in 15 years.

12-16.title: Super Typhoon Rai
12-16.description: Super Typhoon Rai, locally named Odette, struck the central and southern Philippines as one of the strongest typhoons on record for December, devastating the islands of Bohol, Siargao, and Dinagat with extreme winds and storm surge. More than 405 people were killed, about 8 million were affected, and over a million homes were damaged or destroyed.

12-16.title: Army Public School Attack, Peshawar
12-16.description: On 16 December 2014, nine gunmen from the Pakistani Taliban (Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan) stormed the Army Public School in Peshawar, going classroom to classroom and firing on students. The siege lasted about eight hours and killed 141 people, including 132 schoolchildren, with around 150 injured. It was one of the deadliest terrorist attacks in Pakistan's history and prompted a nationwide military crackdown on militant groups.

12-16.title: Typhoon Washi (Sendong) flash floods
12-16.location: Cagayan de Oro and Iligan, Philippines
12-16.description: Tropical Storm Washi (locally named Sendong) made landfall on Mindanao on the night of December 16-17, 2011, dumping up to 20 cm of rain in 24 hours and triggering flash floods that swept away thousands of sleeping residents in the riverside cities of Cagayan de Oro and Iligan. The Philippines' NDRRMC final count recorded 1,268 fatalities, 181 missing and 6,071 injured, with nearly 700,000 people affected and more than 11,000 homes destroyed. It was the deadliest tropical cyclone to hit Mindanao in recorded history.

12-23.title: Damascus twin suicide bombings
12-23.description: On December 23, 2011, two suicide car bombers detonated devices within minutes of each other outside heavily guarded security compounds in the Kfar Sousa district of Damascus, one targeting the General Security Directorate and the second the nearby military intelligence building. At least 44 people were killed and 166 wounded, most of them civilians. It was the first suicide bombing since Syria's uprising began in March 2011; the government blamed al-Qaeda-linked 'terrorists', while opposition figures accused the regime of staging the attack, and no group claimed responsibility.

03-26.title: ROKS Cheonan sinking
03-26.location: Baengnyeong Island, Yellow Sea, South Korea
03-26.description: The South Korean corvette ROKS Cheonan broke in two and sank in the Yellow Sea near Baengnyeong Island on March 26, 2010, killing 46 of its 104 crew members. An international investigation team concluded the ship was split by a torpedo launched from a North Korean submarine; North Korea denied involvement. South Korea and the United States attributed the attack to North Korea and responded with joint military exercises, marking a major escalation of tensions on the Korean Peninsula in 2010.

03-29.title: Moscow Metro suicide bombings
03-29.description: Two female suicide bombers detonated explosives on the Moscow Metro on the morning of March 29, 2010, during rush hour, first at Lubyanka station near the FSB headquarters and then at Park Kultury station. The attacks killed 40 people and injured more than 100. Russian authorities attributed the bombings to the Caucasus Emirate, an Islamist insurgency group based in the North Caucasus, which claimed responsibility.

04-05.title: Upper Big Branch Mine explosion
04-05.description: A methane and coal dust explosion ripped through the Upper Big Branch Mine, operated by Massey Energy, on April 5, 2010, killing 29 of the 31 miners underground, making it the deadliest U.S. coal mining disaster in 40 years. A U.S. Mine Safety and Health Administration investigation determined the blast was preventable and resulted from systemic violations including inadequate ventilation and failure to control dust accumulations. The disaster led to a federal review of mine safety enforcement and congressional scrutiny of the industry.

04-14.title: Nyanya Bus Station Bombing
04-14.description: On 14 April 2014, a bomb exploded at the Nyanya bus station on the outskirts of Abuja, Nigeria, during the morning rush hour. Around 75 people were killed and more than 100 injured. Boko Haram claimed responsibility for the attack, which occurred on the same day the group abducted more than 270 schoolgirls in Chibok.

04-14.title: Yushu earthquake
04-14.description: A magnitude 6.9-7.1 earthquake struck Yushu Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture in Qinghai Province, China, on April 14, 2010, at an altitude of about 4,300 meters. The quake killed 2,698 people, left 270 missing and 12,135 injured, and destroyed an estimated 85 to 90 percent of buildings, primarily in Jiegu Town, leaving at least 100,000 residents homeless. Rescue and relief operations were hampered by the remote high-altitude terrain, harsh weather, and poor infrastructure.

04-20.title: Lushan earthquake
04-20.description: On April 20, 2013, a magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck Lushan County in Ya'an, Sichuan Province, China, killing at least 193 people (196 in official tallies), with 23 missing and more than 11,000 injured. The shallow quake destroyed or severely damaged hundreds of thousands of rural homes and triggered landslides in the mountainous region, and it was the deadliest earthquake in China since the 2008 Wenchuan disaster.

04-20.title: Deepwater Horizon explosion and oil spill
04-20.description: An explosion aboard the BP-operated drilling rig Deepwater Horizon on April 20, 2010 killed 11 workers and sank the rig two days later, rupturing the Macondo wellhead and releasing an estimated 4.9 million barrels of oil over 87 days in the largest marine oil spill in U.S. history. The spill devastated Gulf of Mexico fisheries, wildlife, and coastal economies along Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and Florida, and triggered billions of dollars in cleanup, compensation, and legal settlements for BP and its contractors.

05-28.title: Lahore Ahmadiyya mosque attacks
05-28.description: Gunmen from the Punjabi Taliban wing of Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan attacked two Ahmadiyya mosques in Lahore during Friday prayers on May 28, 2010, using automatic weapons, grenades, and suicide vests, and holding worshippers hostage for several hours. Human Rights Watch documented 94 people killed, 27 at the Baitul Nur mosque in Model Town and 67 at the Darul Zikr mosque in Garhi Shahu, with more than 100 wounded. The attacks were the deadliest assault on the Ahmadiyya religious minority in Pakistan's history.

06-10.title: Tigray famine
06-10.description: Amid the war between Ethiopian federal forces and the Tigray People's Liberation Front, the United Nations declared a famine in parts of Tigray in June 2021 as an aid blockade prevented food from reaching millions of people. Research from Ghent University estimated that 162,000 to 191,000 people died from violence and starvation-related causes in Tigray between November 2020 and June 2022, most of them during 2021.

06-10.title: Osh ethnic violence in southern Kyrgyzstan
06-10.description: Four days of inter-ethnic violence between Kyrgyz and Uzbek communities erupted in Osh on June 10, 2010 and spread to Jalal-Abad, following the ouster of President Kurmanbek Bakiyev in April and a period of political instability. The Kyrgyz health ministry reported an official toll of about 312 dead and over 2,300 injured, while the International Crisis Group estimated up to 470 killed; interim leader Roza Otunbayeva said the true figure was likely around 2,000 because many victims were buried quickly per local tradition. Hundreds of thousands of ethnic Uzbeks fled across the border into Uzbekistan, and the U.N. reported whole districts of Osh burned to the ground.

07-28.title: Kumamoto earthquake
07-28.description: On 28 July 2026, a magnitude 6.8 earthquake (M7.1 on the Japanese scale) struck Kumamoto Prefecture on the Hinagu Fault, killing 38 people and injuring 129. The second floor of Aeon Mall Kumamoto collapsed and later exploded, a chimney collapse at a paper factory in Yatsushiro killed nine workers, and the Kyushu Shinkansen was damaged at more than 200 locations. The toll rose from 36 to 38 on 2 August, with more than 9,200 residents still in evacuation shelters.

07-28.title: Pakistan floods
07-28.description: Unprecedented monsoon rains in late July and August 2010 caused the Indus River and its tributaries to burst their banks, flooding nearly one-fifth of Pakistan's land area across 78 of its 121 districts. Official figures recorded 1,985 deaths and 2,946 injuries, while more than 20 million people were affected, making it one of the largest humanitarian disasters in modern history. The floods destroyed roughly 1.7 million homes, submerged vast agricultural areas, and forced the U.N. to launch a $2 billion relief appeal for what it called the worst flood disaster in Pakistan's history.

08-07.title: Zhouqu mudslide
08-07.description: A massive debris flow triggered by heavy rain swept through the mountain county town of Zhouqu in Gansu Province, China, on the night of August 7, 2010, burying about 2.4 square kilometers of the town under mud and rock and damming the Bailong River. Final official loss statistics recorded 1,557 confirmed dead and 284 missing, a combined toll of 1,765, with more than 2,300 injured or sick. It was described by Chinese authorities as the most severe debris-flow disaster since the founding of the People's Republic, with surges reported up to five storeys high.

08-07.title: Russo-Georgian War
08-07.description: Fighting between Georgian forces and separatists backed by Russian troops erupted on 7 August 2008 and expanded into a five-day war, with Russian air strikes and ground operations reaching Gori, Tbilisi, and other cities, including attacks that killed civilians and a cluster-munition strike on Tbilisi. Georgian authorities reported 412 dead on the Georgian side (about 228 civilians, 170 military personnel, and 14 police), Russian figures listed 64-67 soldiers and about 162-170 civilians killed, with total estimates around 850 dead and roughly 150,000 displaced. Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International concluded total deaths were in the hundreds, not the thousands initially claimed.

08-07.title: Russian drone strike on Lozova train station kills two
08-07.description: A morning Russian drone attack on the train station in Lozova, Kharkiv region, killed two men aged 52 and 59 and injured 11 other people, according to the Kharkiv Regional Police Directorate.

08-07.title: Thailand school shooting kills nine
08-07.description: A 14-year-old student shot and killed his grandparents at home before opening fire at Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Bang Kruai district, Nonthaburi, killing teachers and students and wounding more than 20 other people before taking his own life. Authorities said the death toll rose to nine, including the shooter, as of August 8.

08-07.title: Firefighting helicopter crash near Utah wildfire kills two
08-07.description: A Sikorsky S-64 heavy-lift helicopter supporting firefighting operations on the Widemouth 2 Fire in central Utah crashed near Richfield on Friday morning, killing a pilot and a crewmember, authorities confirmed.

08-07.title: Wildfire kills bulldozer operator in Oregon
08-07.description: A 47-year-old bulldozer operator, Jason Ensign, died after being trapped when fire rapidly overran his position while he helped forestry crews battle an uncontained wildfire in south-central Oregon on Friday.

07-05.title: 2016 China floods (Yangtze basin)
07-05.description: Torrential monsoon rains produced the worst flooding in China since 1998, hitting the Yangtze and Huai river basins across 26 provinces and affecting an estimated 32 million people, with hundreds of thousands left homeless. More than 350 people died in the floods, and a June 23 EF4 tornado in Jiangsu Province that killed at least 99 people brought the combined toll to more than 440. Rivers breached their banks in multiple provinces, including Hubei and Anhui, and damage was estimated in the tens of billions of dollars.

07-05.title: Russian heatwave and wildfires
07-05.description: A record-breaking heatwave in July and August 2010, the hottest in eastern Europe in 500 years, combined with massive wildfires and dense smog across western Russia, causing an estimated 55,000 excess deaths nationwide, according to the Center for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters and peer-reviewed studies. In Moscow alone, an estimated 10,900 to 11,300 excess deaths occurred during the 44-day heat wave and accompanying smog episode, largely from cardiovascular and respiratory failure. The fires destroyed about one-third of Russia's grain harvest and caused roughly $15 billion in economic losses.
sources: Center for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters (CRED)

10-25.title: Lewiston mass shooting
10-25.description: A 40-year-old Army reservist opened fire at a bowling alley and a bar in Lewiston, Maine, killing 18 people and wounding 13 others before fleeing, prompting a two-day manhunt that ended with his death by suicide. It was the deadliest mass shooting in Maine's history and one of the deadliest in the United States in 2023. The shooter's history of mental health episodes and threats had raised concerns within his unit and family.

10-25.title: Mentawai Islands earthquake and tsunami
10-25.description: A magnitude 7.7-7.8 earthquake struck beneath the Indian Ocean off the Mentawai Islands, west of Sumatra, Indonesia, on October 25, 2010, generating tsunami waves up to 3 meters that devastated low-lying coastal villages. The Indonesian disaster management agency and IFRC recorded 452 people dead and 76 missing, with nearly 15,000 displaced. The disaster struck the same week as the Mount Merapi eruption, and both events combined killed over 700 people, with many of the tsunami victims never recovered from the sea.

10-25.title: Baghdad Justice Ministry Bombings
10-25.description: On October 25, 2009, two suicide car bombs exploded in quick succession near the Iraqi Ministry of Justice and the Baghdad Provincial Council building, killing at least 155 people and wounding more than 500. Victims included about two dozen children riding a bus near the Justice Ministry daycare. The Islamic State of Iraq, an al-Qaeda-linked group, claimed responsibility. It was Iraq's deadliest attack in more than two years.

10-26.title: Hindu Kush earthquake
10-26.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake centered in the Hindu Kush mountains of northeastern Afghanistan shook a wide area of South Asia, killing 399 people, including at least 280 in Pakistan, 115 in Afghanistan and 4 in India, and injuring about 2,500. Hundreds of homes collapsed across northern Pakistan and Afghanistan, and shaking was felt as far away as Delhi.

10-26.title: Mount Merapi eruption
10-26.description: Mount Merapi in central Java began a series of violent eruptions on October 26, 2010, with major eruptions continuing through November 5, including a powerful blast that killed its spiritual guardian Mbah Maridjan and overwhelmed emergency shelters. The final toll recorded 273 deaths, 176 from pyroclastic flows on the spot and 97 from related causes after hospitalization, with 577 people injured and up to 300,000 displaced across Central Java and Yogyakarta. It was the volcano's most powerful eruption in over a century, its eruptive activity peaking in early November.

10-31.title: Tezgam train fire
10-31.description: On 31 October 2019, a fire broke out on the Tezgam express train travelling from Karachi to Rawalpindi near Rahim Yar Khan in Punjab, after a gas canister used by passengers to cook food exploded, igniting fuel carried on board. At least 74 passengers were killed, many of them burned to death or killed jumping from the moving train, and dozens more were injured. Pakistan's railways minister acknowledged that cooking equipment and flammable materials were routinely carried on trains and ordered an inquiry into the deadliest rail accident in Pakistan in years.

10-31.title: Metrojet Flight 9268 bombing
10-31.description: Metrojet Flight 9268, an Airbus A321 carrying 224 people from the Egyptian resort of Sharm el-Sheikh to Saint Petersburg, Russia, broke up in flight over the Sinai Peninsula about 23 minutes after takeoff, killing everyone on board, including 219 Russians. Investigators concluded that an improvised explosive device of about 1 kg of TNT destroyed the aircraft; the Islamic State's Sinai branch claimed responsibility, and Egypt and Russia ultimately acknowledged the cause as a terrorist bombing.

10-31.title: Our Lady of Salvation church siege
10-31.description: Gunmen from the Islamic State of Iraq stormed Our Lady of Salvation, a Syriac Catholic church in Baghdad, during Sunday Mass on October 31, 2010, taking more than 100 worshippers hostage before Iraqi security forces stormed the building. The siege killed 58 people, including 44 worshippers, two priests, seven security personnel, and five attackers, and wounded more than 70. It was the deadliest attack on Iraq's Christian community since the 2003 invasion and prompted an exodus of Iraqi Christians, with many families fleeing the country.

11-19.title: Pike River Mine disaster
11-19.description: A methane explosion at the Pike River coal mine on the South Island of New Zealand on November 19, 2010 trapped 29 miners, all of whom were declared dead after a series of further explosions prevented rescue attempts and a subsequent fire forced the mine to be sealed. The victims' bodies were never recovered. A royal commission of inquiry found the explosion was preventable and identified systemic failures in mine management, gas monitoring, and safety culture, prompting a major overhaul of New Zealand's mining safety legislation.

11-26.title: Mumbai attacks (26/11)
11-26.description: Ten gunmen from the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba group, arriving by sea from Karachi, carried out a coordinated 60-hour attack on multiple Mumbai targets beginning 26 November 2008: the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus railway station, the Taj Mahal Palace and Oberoi-Trident hotels, Nariman House (a Jewish centre), Cama Hospital, and Leopold Cafe. The siege, which ended on 29 November when security forces killed nine of the attackers, left 166 people dead, including six police officers, and over 300 injured; one attacker, Ajmal Kasab, was captured alive.

06-20.title: Typhoon Fengshen (Frank) and MV Princess of the Stars sinking
06-20.description: Typhoon Fengshen swept across the central Philippines from 20-23 June 2008 with winds up to 175 km/h, causing flooding, landslides, and sea surges. Its deadliest impact came when the passenger ferry MV Princess of the Stars, which had sailed from Manila into the storm, capsized off Sibuyan Island on 21 June, killing roughly 800-850 of the estimated 850-920 people aboard. Including the ferry and flood victims, the Philippine government and UN recorded at least 1,371 deaths in the Philippines and China, with hundreds missing, making it the deadliest Philippine typhoon since 2006.

09-20.title: MV Nyerere ferry capsizing
09-20.description: The passenger ferry MV Nyerere capsized minutes after leaving the dock at Ukerewe Island on Lake Victoria, Tanzania, on a journey to Bugolora in the Mwanza region. The vessel, with a listed capacity of about 100 people, was carrying a far larger number of passengers, many returning from the island's market day. At least 228 people drowned in the disaster, with hundreds of others rescued; officials later arrested ferry crew members over safety violations.

09-20.title: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico
09-20.description: Hurricane Maria, a Category 5 storm at peak intensity, made landfall in Puerto Rico on 20 September 2017, devastating the island with winds up to 175 mph and torrential rainfall. The storm destroyed the electric grid, knocked out water systems and communications, and left much of the island without power for months. Official estimates of direct and indirect deaths were later revised from 64 to 2,975 after a George Washington University study commissioned by the governor attributed the higher toll to the disruption of health care, medication and infrastructure, making it among the deadliest US hurricanes on record.

09-20.title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
09-20.description: A dump truck carrying about 1,000 kg of explosives detonated at the security gate of the Marriott Hotel in Islamabad on the evening of 20 September 2008, gutting the building and killing 54 people, including the Czech ambassador to Pakistan, three US citizens, and a Danish intelligence agent, while wounding at least 266. The attack, hours after President Asif Ali Zardari's first address to parliament, was one of the worst terrorist attacks in Pakistan's history; no group claimed responsibility.

03-06.title: Syrian coastal massacres of Alawites
03-06.description: From March 6, 2025, security forces and allied armed groups linked to Syria's caretaker government carried out a crackdown that turned into mass sectarian killings of Alawite civilians in the coastal governorates of Latakia and Tartus, as well as parts of Hama and Homs, in response to an insurgency by Assad loyalists; death toll estimates range from about 1,000 to 2,000, with a Reuters investigation documenting at least 1,479 Alawites killed on March 7-9.

03-06.title: Karrada double bombing in Baghdad
03-06.description: On the evening of 6 March 2008, a roadside bomb exploded in the packed Karrada shopping district of central Baghdad; minutes later, as bystanders and security forces gathered to help the wounded, a suicide bomber detonated a second, larger bomb. Police confirmed 68 people killed and 120 wounded, the deadliest attack in Baghdad in about nine months. Iraqi police and the US military blamed al-Qaeda in Iraq for the double-bombing tactic designed to maximize casualties.

01-10.title: China winter storms (2008 Chinese snowstorms)
01-10.description: Severe snowstorms, freezing rain, and cold struck 20-21 provinces across central and southern China from mid-January to early February 2008, collapsing power pylons, halting trains and highways during the Lunar New Year travel season, and stranding nearly one million people at Guangzhou's railway station. China's Civil Affairs Ministry confirmed 129 people killed and 4 missing, with 1.66 million people relocated, 485,000 houses collapsed, and economic losses of about 151 billion yuan (roughly US$21 billion). It was China's worst winter weather in half a century.

09-17.title: Bamako Attack
09-17.description: On September 17, 2024, jihadist attackers from Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) stormed a military police school and the military airport in Bamako, Mali, in a coordinated assault. The attack killed at least 77 people, including civilians, and wounded more than 250, making it one of the deadliest attacks in Mali in years and prompting heightened security measures in the capital.

09-17.title: Chinese melamine milk scandal
09-17.description: In September 2008 it emerged that infant formula produced by Sanlu Group and other dairies had been adulterated with melamine, an industrial chemical added to watered-down milk to boost apparent protein content, causing kidney stones and acute kidney failure in infants. China's Ministry of Health confirmed at least 6 infant deaths and reported that nearly 300,000 infants had been sickened, over 50,000 hospitalized at the peak. The government withdrew 8,300 tons of tainted products and arrested dozens of executives and officials.

01-18.title: Nigeria fuel tanker explosion in Suleja
01-18.description: On January 18, 2025, a fuel tanker exploded at the Dikko junction near Suleja in Niger State after a crash, engulfing people who had gathered to collect spilled fuel; Nigeria's Federal Road Safety Corps confirmed more than 100 bodies were recovered and buried, with dozens of others badly burned.

01-18.title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead)
01-18.description: Israel's military offensive against Hamas in the Gaza Strip ran from December 27, 2008, to a ceasefire on January 18, 2009. Human rights organizations and UN agencies documented approximately 1,340-1,400 Palestinians killed, including around 750-770 civilians and more than 300 children, with over 5,000 wounded. Thirteen Israelis were killed, including 3 civilians. The offensive included heavy air strikes and ground operations and caused extensive destruction of homes, schools, and infrastructure across Gaza.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
Al Mezan Centre for Human Rights

05-18.title: Cubana de Aviación Flight 972 crash
05-18.description: Cubana de Aviación Flight 972, a Boeing 737-200 leased by the national airline, crashed shortly after takeoff from Havana's José Martí International Airport on a domestic flight to Holguín. The aircraft struck a hillside in a rural area, killing 112 of the 113 people on board; one passenger survived with serious injuries. Cuba's government launched an investigation into the crash, the country's deadliest aviation disaster in decades, and declared two days of national mourning.

05-18.title: Sri Lankan Civil War Final Offensive
05-18.description: Between January and May 2009, the Sri Lankan military's final offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) trapped roughly 330,000 civilians in an ever-shrinking 'no fire zone' in the northeast. A UN Secretary-General-appointed panel of experts estimated in 2011 that as many as 40,000 civilians were killed, most by government shelling, with the LTTE also accused of using civilians as human shields. The government's own figures put the toll at about 7,000-9,000. The war ended on May 18, 2009, with the military declaring victory.

04-06.title: L'Aquila Earthquake
04-06.description: A magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck the Abruzzo region of central Italy at 3:32 a.m. on April 6, 2009, with its epicenter near the city of L'Aquila. The quake killed 308 people, injured about 1,500, and left roughly 65,000 homeless. Many victims, including 55-66 university students, died in collapsed buildings such as the university dormitory and apartment blocks. It was the deadliest earthquake to hit Italy since the 1980 Irpinia earthquake.

10-03.title: Kunduz hospital airstrike
10-03.description: A United States AC-130 gunship repeatedly struck the trauma hospital of Medecins Sans Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders) in Kunduz, Afghanistan, during fighting between Afghan forces and Taliban fighters who had seized the city days earlier. The airstrike killed 42 people, including 14 MSF staff, 24 patients and four caretakers, and wounded more than 30. The US military called the attack a mistake and later disciplined two officers by court-martial.

10-03.title: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng)
10-03.description: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng) made landfall in northern Luzon on October 3, 2009, and lingered over the island for a week, making landfall three times and causing torrential rains. Massive landslides in Benguet province and the Cordillera Administrative Region killed 465 people in the Philippines, with total regional deaths near 500, including in Vietnam and China. Landslide-buried villages in La Trinidad and Baguio City accounted for the heaviest losses.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

09-30.title: Kaaj education centre bombing (Kabul)
09-30.description: On 30 September 2022, a suicide bomber attacked the Kaaj education centre in Dashte Barchi, a Shia Hazara neighbourhood of Kabul, during a university entrance practice exam. The Associated Press reported at least 53 people killed, most of them young women, and about 110 wounded, while Taliban authorities gave a lower figure. Islamic State Khorasan Province claimed responsibility for one of the deadliest attacks in Afghanistan in 2022.

09-30.title: West Sumatra (Padang) Earthquake
09-30.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck off the coast of West Sumatra on September 30, 2009, about 45 km northwest of Padang. The Indonesian government confirmed 1,115 deaths, with more than 1,200 seriously injured and about 450,000 people displaced. Widespread collapse of poorly reinforced buildings in Padang and Padang Pariaman district caused most casualties. USGS called it the deadliest earthquake of 2009.

09-29.title: Samoa Earthquake and Tsunami
09-29.description: A magnitude 8.1 earthquake struck south of the Samoan Islands on September 29, 2009, generating tsunami waves that reached runup heights of up to 17 meters and struck coastal villages with little warning. At least 189 people were killed — 149 in Samoa, 34 in American Samoa, and 9 in Tonga — with many victims children and elderly residents. It was the strongest earthquake of 2009 according to USGS.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

09-04.title: Apalachee High School Shooting
09-04.description: On September 4, 2024, a 14-year-old student opened fire at Apalachee High School in Winder, Georgia, United States, killing four people — two students and two teachers — and injuring nine others before surrendering to officers. It was the deadliest school shooting in the United States in 2024, and the teenage suspect was charged as an adult with murder.

09-04.title: Kunduz Fuel Tanker Airstrike
09-04.description: On September 4, 2009, NATO aircraft, at the request of German forces, bombed two fuel tankers hijacked by Taliban insurgents near Kunduz City. Villagers had gathered around the stranded tankers to siphon fuel. Death toll estimates range from 56 to 179, with a German parliamentary investigation concluding up to 142 people died, including more than 100 civilians. The strike sparked a major political crisis in Germany and led to compensation payments to victims' families.

10-28.title: Peshawar Meena Bazaar Bombing
10-28.description: On October 28, 2009, a car bomb exploded in the Meena Bazaar, a women's market in Peshawar, killing approximately 110-120 people — about 70 of them women and children — and injuring more than 200. The blast, among the deadliest attacks in Peshawar's history, destroyed several buildings and trapped many victims in rubble. Pakistani Taliban-linked militants were suspected. The bombing came amid a surge of militant attacks across Pakistan's northwest.

11-05.title: Sutherland Springs church shooting
11-05.description: On 5 November 2017 a gunman entered the First Baptist Church in Sutherland Springs, Texas, during Sunday service and opened fire with an assault rifle, killing 26 people including an unborn child and injuring more than 20; victims ranged in age from 18 months to 77 years. The attack ended when the shooter was wounded by a neighbor and fled, later dying of a self-inflicted gunshot. It was the deadliest mass shooting at a place of worship in US history, and investigators found the gunman had a history of domestic violence that was not flagged in federal background checks.

11-05.title: Fort Hood Shooting
11-05.description: On November 5, 2009, Army psychiatrist Major Nidal Hasan opened fire at the Soldier Readiness Processing Center at Fort Hood, Texas, killing 13 people — 12 soldiers and one civilian — and wounding more than 30. Hasan, a US Army officer, was shot by responding police and survived. It was the deadliest mass shooting on a US military base; Hasan was convicted in 2013 of 13 counts of premeditated murder.

04-03.title: Binghamton Immigration Center Shooting
04-03.description: On April 3, 2009, gunman Jiverly Wong entered the American Civic Association immigration center in Binghamton, New York, and opened fire on students and staff, killing 13 people and wounding 4 before killing himself. Most victims were immigrants from countries including Vietnam, China, Haiti, and Iraq who had come to the center for English or citizenship classes. It remains the deadliest mass shooting in New York state history.

11-21.title: Xinxing Coal Mine Explosion
11-21.description: A gas explosion ripped through the state-owned Xinxing Coal Mine in Hegang, Heilongjiang Province, at about 2:30 a.m. on November 21, 2009, while 528 miners were underground. The blast destroyed ventilation and communication systems, killing 108 miners and injuring dozens more. It was China's worst coal mine disaster in nearly two years and prompted the dismissal of mine management and renewed scrutiny of safety in the country's state-run mines.

12-05.title: Lame Horse Nightclub Fire
12-05.description: A fire tore through the Lame Horse nightclub in Perm, Russia, early on December 5, 2009, during the club's eighth-anniversary party. Sparks from an indoor fireworks display ignited the low willow-twig ceiling, and the fire spread rapidly with lights failing amid panic and a stampede at the exit. The blaze killed 156 people and injured about 100 more, making it one of Russia's deadliest fires in decades and prompting prosecutions of club owners and officials.

01-16.title: Mustansiriya University bombing
01-16.description: A suicide truck bomb exploded near Mustansiriya University in central Baghdad during the afternoon rush hour on January 16, 2007, killing about 70 people and wounding more than 160. The blast struck a busy commercial street beside the university where students and shoppers had gathered.

02-03.title: Kwara State attacks
02-03.description: On 3–4 February 2026, hundreds of Boko Haram gunmen of the Sadiku faction surrounded the villages of Nuku and Woro in Kaiama, Kwara State, near the Beninese border, killing at least 162 people in door-to-door executions, with the toll later reported to exceed 200. Attackers blocked exits, torched homes, shops and the palace, shot people who answered a mosque call to prayer, and kidnapped 38 others; the dead included the chief imam, a school principal and schoolchildren.

02-03.title: Somalia famine — 2011-2012 crisis
02-03.description: A UN-declared famine that began in July 2011 in southern Somalia was declared over on 3 February 2012. A joint FSNAU/FEWS NET mortality study attributed about 258,000 excess deaths to the famine between October 2010 and April 2012, roughly half of them children under five, driven by drought, conflict, and obstruction of humanitarian access.

02-03.title: al-Shorja market bombing
02-03.description: A suicide truck bomber detonated a vehicle packed with explosives in the al-Shorja market district of central Baghdad on February 3, 2007, killing at least 135 people and injuring more than 300. The blast destroyed shops and vehicles in one of the city's largest markets on a weekend shopping day.

04-02.title: Bucha massacre
04-02.description: After Russian forces withdrew from Bucha in early April 2022, Ukrainian authorities discovered mass graves and the bodies of hundreds of civilians killed during the month-long occupation of the town. Ukrainian officials recovered 458 bodies, most showing signs of shooting, torture, or other violent trauma. OHCHR documented at least 73 unlawful killings in Bucha itself and reported more than 1,300 killings across the wider Bucha district, describing the massacre as a grave violation of international law.

04-02.title: Garissa University College attack
04-02.description: Four gunmen from the Somali militant group al-Shabaab stormed Garissa University College at dawn, taking students hostage and executing many of them. The attack killed 148 people, comprising 142 students, three soldiers and three police officers, and wounded 79. Kenyan special forces ended the siege the same day, killing all four attackers.

04-02.title: Solomon Islands earthquake and tsunami
04-02.description: A magnitude 8.1 earthquake struck near Gizo in the Solomon Islands on April 2, 2007, generating a tsunami that killed 52 people and left dozens missing. Waves several meters high destroyed at least 13 villages across the Western Province.

04-18.title: al-Sadriya market bombing
04-18.description: A suicide car bomb exploded in a crowded market in the al-Sadriya district of central Baghdad on April 18, 2007, killing about 140 people and injuring more than 150. The blast struck during the evening rush hour, devastating the neighborhood market and surrounding shops.

06-26.title: Sousse beach attack
06-26.description: A gunman affiliated with the Islamic State opened fire on tourists at the Imperial Marhaba beach hotel in Sousse, a popular Tunisian coastal resort, killing 38 people, 30 of them British, and wounding 39. Security forces shot the attacker dead. It was Tunisia's deadliest terrorist attack.

06-26.title: Cyclone Yemyin and Pakistan floods
06-26.description: Cyclone Yemyin made landfall on Pakistan's Makran coast on June 26, 2007, bringing torrential rain and flash floods that killed about 730 people in Balochistan, Sindh, and the North-West Frontier Province, with more than 100 killed in Afghanistan. Preceding heavy rain had already caused flooding and hundreds of deaths in Karachi.

08-15.title: Kerala floods
08-15.description: Unprecedented monsoon rainfall, the heaviest in the Indian state in nearly a century, caused catastrophic flooding and landslides across Kerala in August 2018. All 14 districts of the state were affected, with the Periyar and Pamba rivers overflowing and over 100 dams releasing water. The state disaster management authority confirmed 483 deaths, while over 1.5 million people were displaced into relief camps and property damage was estimated at billions of dollars.

08-15.title: Peru earthquake
08-15.description: A magnitude 8.0 earthquake struck off Peru's central coast on August 15, 2007, killing 595 people and injuring more than 2,000. The city of Pisco was hardest hit, with about 85 percent of its buildings destroyed, and the quake also caused tsunami flooding along the coast.

08-15.title: Russian drone strike on Marhanets kills three-month-old baby
08-15.description: Russian forces struck a multi-storey building in Marhanets, Dnipropetrovsk region, with drones during a nighttime attack, killing a three-month-old boy and injuring 11 people, including children, according to regional military administration chief Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue and clearance operations continued at the site.

08-15.title: Flash flood and landslide in Ponferrada area kill two women
08-15.description: A strong afternoon storm caused the Oza river to overflow, producing a flash flood and landslide that struck the localities of Manzanedo de Valdueza and Bouzas in the Ponferrada area, Castilla y Leon. The flood engulfed a wine cellar where six people were sheltering: two women died and two minors were treated for minor injuries, with the fate of others unknown. The flood also damaged local roads.

08-15.title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 11 including women and children
08-15.description: Two Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon on August 15 killed 11 people, including three children and two women, and wounded others. One strike hit a two-story building in Deir Al Zahrani in the Nabatieh District, killing four; another struck a house in Ansar, killing seven, per the Lebanese Health Ministry. The strikes came amid renewed Israeli bombardment and shelling in Nabatieh, prompting hundreds of residents to flee toward Sidon, and were condemned by Lebanese President Joseph Aoun.

11-06.title: Baghlan bombing
11-06.description: A suicide bomber attacked a ceremony at a sugar factory in Baghlan Province, Afghanistan, on November 6, 2007, killing about 79 people, including six members of parliament and a number of children. A crowd of politicians and local officials had gathered for the event.

11-18.title: Zasyadko mine explosion
11-18.description: A methane explosion in the Zasyadko coal mine in Donetsk, Ukraine, on November 18, 2007, killed 101 miners, making it the worst mining accident in the country's history. An estimated 300 miners were underground at the time of the blast.

12-11.title: Algiers bombings
12-11.description: Two car bombs exploded about ten minutes apart in Algiers on December 11, 2007, one near the Supreme Constitutional Court and one beside UN offices, killing 41 people, including 17 UN staff members, and injuring about 170. Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb claimed responsibility.

03-08.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 Disappearance
03-08.description: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370, carrying 227 passengers and 12 crew, vanished from radar on 8 March 2014 shortly after departing Kuala Lumpur for Beijing. An extensive multinational search failed to locate the main wreckage for years, though debris washed ashore confirmed the aircraft crashed in the southern Indian Ocean. All 239 people on board are presumed dead.

03-22.title: South Korea wildfire outbreak
03-22.description: Between March 21 and May 15, 2025, wildfires across central and southern South Korea, the largest starting in Uiseong County, destroyed thousands of buildings and killed at least 32 people, making it the deadliest wildfire outbreak in the country's recorded history.

03-22.title: Crocus City Hall Concert Hall Attack
03-22.description: On March 22, 2024, four armed gunmen opened fire on concertgoers at Crocus City Hall in Krasnogorsk, outside Moscow, and set the venue ablaze. At least 145 people were killed and more than 500 injured; the Islamic State's Khorasan Province (ISIS-K) claimed responsibility, and Russia charged four Tajik nationals with the attack.

03-22.title: Boulder supermarket shooting
03-22.description: A gunman opened fire with a semi-automatic rifle at a King Soopers grocery store in Boulder, killing ten people, including a police officer who was the first responder on the scene. The suspect, who had purchased the weapon six days earlier despite a history of mental health issues, was captured alive.

03-22.title: Brussels airport and metro bombings
03-22.description: Three coordinated suicide bombings struck Brussels on the morning of March 22: two at Zaventem airport's departure hall and one on a Maalbeek metro train near the European Commission headquarters. Islamic State claimed responsibility. Thirty-two civilians were killed and more than 300 wounded, in attacks that came days after the arrest in Brussels of Paris attacks suspect Salah Abdeslam.

03-22.title: Oso Mudslide
03-22.description: On 22 March 2014, a large hillside collapsed in the community of Oso, Washington, sending a debris-filled mudslide across the Stillaguamish River valley and destroying dozens of homes. Forty-three people were killed, making it the deadliest landslide in United States history, and two residents remain unaccounted for.

05-14.title: Buffalo supermarket shooting
05-14.description: On 14 May 2022, a gunman driven by white supremacist ideology opened fire at a Tops supermarket in a predominantly Black neighbourhood of Buffalo, New York, livestreaming the attack. Ten Black people were killed and three injured in what authorities called a racially motivated hate crime. The shooter pleaded guilty and was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

05-14.title: Gaza border protest killings
05-14.description: On May 14, 2018, during the Great March of Return protests marking the 70th anniversary of the Nakba, Israeli forces opened fire on Palestinian demonstrators near the Gaza-Israel border, killing at least 60 people and wounding about 2,700 in a single day. The protests, which began in March 2018, saw roughly 189 Palestinians killed by Israeli gunfire over the course of the year, according to UN figures, making it the deadliest period of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict in years.

05-14.title: Balkan Floods
05-14.description: Record rainfall in mid-May 2014 triggered the worst floods in the Balkans in more than a century, inundating Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and parts of Croatia. At least 80 people died, hundreds of thousands were displaced, and landslides in Bosnia uncovered mass graves from the 1990s war. The floods caused billions of euros in damage across the region.

08-03.title: El Paso Walmart shooting
08-03.description: On 3 August 2019, a gunman opened fire at a Walmart store in El Paso, Texas, near the US-Mexico border, killing 23 people and wounding more than 20 others in an attack targeting Latinos. The suspect, who had posted an anti-immigrant manifesto online, was arrested at the scene and later pleaded guilty to 90 federal counts, receiving a sentence of 90 consecutive life terms. The shooting was the deadliest anti-Latino attack in modern US history and prompted federal charges treated as domestic terrorism.

08-03.title: Ludian Earthquake
08-03.description: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck Ludian County in Yunnan province, southwestern China, on 3 August 2014. The shallow quake triggered landslides that buried villages and destroyed tens of thousands of homes; 617 people were killed, more than 100 went missing and over 3,100 were injured. It was China's deadliest earthquake in several years.

08-03.title: ISIS Genocide of Yazidis in Sinjar
08-03.description: On 3 August 2014, fighters of the Islamic State group overran the Yazidi heartland of Sinjar in northern Iraq, forcing tens of thousands of people onto Mount Sinjar, where hundreds died of thirst and heat. Men and boys were executed, while women and girls were taken as sex slaves; the United Nations later estimated that about 5,000 Yazidis were killed in the 2014-2017 campaign. The UN formally declared the attacks on the Yazidis an act of genocide.

08-03.title: Israeli strike kills two in Gaza City
08-03.description: An Israeli airstrike targeted a vehicle southwest of Gaza City on Monday evening, killing two Palestinians in the Sheikh Ajlin area, in another violation of the ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, medical sources said.

08-03.title: Israeli fire kills 19 Palestinians in Gaza
08-03.description: At least 19 Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire over 24 hours, including 18 killed by Israeli forces and one who died of wounds from an earlier attack, according to the Gaza Health Ministry. The deaths brought the number of Palestinians killed since the ceasefire to more than 1,250.

08-03.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Gelendzhik beach kills seven
08-03.description: During a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Krasnodar Krai on August 3, a drone fell onto a crowded beach at Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik, killing at least seven people, including four children, and injuring more than 50. Ukrainian officials said the deaths were caused by Russian air-defence debris.

08-03.title: Landslide kills 14 at Ethiopian monastery
08-03.description: Heavy rainfall triggered a landslide that buried worshippers gathered at Tsadqane Debre Mitmaq St. Mary Monastery in Amhara's North Shewa Zone, killing 14 people and injuring at least seven, with an unknown number still missing as search and rescue efforts continued.

09-07.title: Super Typhoon Yagi
09-07.description: Super Typhoon Yagi, the most powerful storm of the 2024 season, made landfall in northern Vietnam on September 7, 2024, after causing destruction in the Philippines and southern China, and spawned flooding and landslides across Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, and Myanmar. The storm and its aftermath killed at least 844 people across the region, more than 320 of them in Vietnam, with hundreds more missing in Myanmar.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

09-07.title: Chiapas earthquake, Mexico
09-07.description: A magnitude 8.2 earthquake struck off the Pacific coast of Chiapas state in the early hours of 7 September 2017, making it the strongest quake in Mexico in a century. The tremor killed at least 98 people, most in Oaxaca and Chiapas, and destroyed hundreds of homes, schools and churches across the southern states; damage was worsened by the region's adobe-built housing. It was followed on 19 September by a second major earthquake centered near Puebla that struck central Mexico.

09-07.title: Kashmir Floods
09-07.description: Torrential monsoon rains in the first half of September 2014 caused catastrophic flooding in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir and parts of Pakistan-administered Kashmir. The Jhelum River broke its banks and submerged much of Srinagar, killing around 500 people and stranding hundreds of thousands, with relief operations hampered by the scale of the flooding. It was the region's worst flooding in decades.

09-07.title: Yunnan earthquakes
09-07.description: On 7 September 2012, a doublet of earthquakes (magnitudes 5.6 and 5.3) struck Yiliang County in Zhaotong, Yunnan, China. The quakes killed 81 people and injured 821, damaged more than 20,000 houses, and forced the evacuation of at least 100,000 residents from the mountainous, landslide-prone area.

09-27.title: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
09-27.description: On 27 September 2020, Azerbaijan launched a large-scale military offensive against the Armenian-backed Nagorno-Karabakh (Artsakh) region, starting a 44-day war that ended with a Russian-brokered ceasefire on 10 November 2020. Official figures from both sides listed about 2,900 Azerbaijani and 3,800 Armenian soldiers killed, along with roughly 185 civilians, for a combined death toll of more than 6,900, with tens of thousands displaced. Azerbaijan regained control of territory around and within the region under the ceasefire terms.

09-27.title: Mount Ontake Eruption
09-27.description: Mount Ontake in central Japan erupted without warning on 27 September 2014, sending an ash cloud over hundreds of hikers who had climbed the peak for the autumn colors. Fifty-seven people were killed on the day of the eruption and the toll later rose to 63, mostly from injuries caused by falling rocks. It was Japan's deadliest volcanic eruption in nearly 90 years.

12-28.title: Mogadishu truck bombing
12-28.description: On 28 December 2019, a truck bomb detonated at the Ex-Control Afgoye checkpoint on the outskirts of Mogadishu, followed by another blast at a bus station in the city, killing at least 85 people and injuring more than 140. The attack hit taxis, buses and minibuses collecting passengers at the checkpoint during rush hour, and al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. It was among the deadliest attacks in Mogadishu in years and targeted a route frequented by civilians travelling between the capital and surrounding towns.

12-28.title: Indonesia AirAsia Flight QZ8501 Crash
12-28.description: Indonesia AirAsia Flight QZ8501, an Airbus A320 flying from Surabaya to Singapore, crashed into the Java Sea on 28 December 2014 during stormy weather. All 155 passengers and seven crew members were killed; wreckage and bodies were recovered over the following weeks. Investigators concluded that an electrical fault in the flight-control system led the aircraft to stall after the pilots' responses.

04-01.title: India's second COVID-19 wave
04-01.description: India was overwhelmed by a second wave of COVID-19 driven by the Delta variant from April to June 2021, when hospitals, crematoria, and oxygen supplies ran out in Delhi and other cities. India officially recorded about 400,000 COVID-19 deaths during 2021, the vast majority during this wave, while independent estimates such as the World Health Organization's excess-death analysis placed the true toll far higher.

04-01.title: Mocoa mudslide, Colombia
04-01.description: Heavy overnight rainfall on 31 March-1 April 2017 caused rivers to overflow and triggered massive mudslides that swept through the city of Mocoa in Putumayo department, burying neighborhoods as residents slept. At least 336 people were killed, including many children, and hundreds more were injured or missing; dozens of homes, schools and bridges were destroyed. Search-and-rescue operations continued for weeks, and the Colombian government declared a state of emergency in the affected region.

04-09.title: Palm Sunday church bombings, Egypt
04-09.description: On Palm Sunday, 9 April 2017, suicide bombers attacked two Coptic Orthodox churches during services: St. George's Church in Tanta and St. Mark's Cathedral in Alexandria, where Pope Tawadros II had just left. At least 45 people were killed and scores injured in the coordinated bombings, making it one of the deadliest attacks on Christians in Egypt's modern history. The Islamic State's Sinai branch claimed responsibility for both attacks.

06-14.title: Shooting of Minnesota state legislators
06-14.description: In the early hours of June 14, 2025, a gunman attacked the homes of Minnesota Democratic state legislators in the Minneapolis suburbs, fatally shooting Representative Melissa Hortman and her husband at their Brooklyn Park home and wounding Senator John Hoffman and his wife; the suspect was arrested and later pleaded guilty to murder.

06-14.title: Pakistan floods
06-14.description: From mid-June 2022, record monsoon rains and glacial melt triggered catastrophic flooding across Pakistan that submerged as much as one-third of the country at its peak. The National Disaster Management Authority reported 1,739 deaths and about 12,900 injuries, with 33 million people affected and more than 2 million homes damaged or destroyed. Among the deadliest floods in the country's history, the disaster caused damages estimated in the tens of billions of dollars and was widely linked to climate change.
sources: National Disaster Management Authority of Pakistan

06-14.title: Grenfell Tower fire
06-14.description: A fire broke out in a kitchen on the fourth floor of Grenfell Tower, a 24-storey social housing block in North Kensington, London, on 14 June 2017 and spread rapidly across the building's exterior cladding, engulfing the tower within minutes. Seventy-two people died, including two who later died in hospital, and more than 70 were injured; residents above the initial floors were trapped because the building had a single stairway and lacked a full sprinkler system. The public inquiry later found the deaths were caused by a combination of combustible aluminium composite cladding panels, polyisocyanurate insulation, and the fire-protection failures of the building's refurbishment. It remains the deadliest UK residential fire since the Second World War.

07-10.title: Battle of Mosul ends
07-10.description: The nine-month campaign by Iraqi security forces and the US-led coalition to retake Mosul from the Islamic State concluded with victory declared on 10 July 2017, after the final pockets of resistance fell in the Old City. The battle devastated Iraq's second-largest city, leaving entire districts in ruins. An Associated Press investigation estimated 9,000-11,000 civilians were killed during the campaign, many in coalition airstrikes and IS-held areas where residents were used as human shields; Amnesty International documented thousands of civilians killed by strikes, while UN figures recorded over 2,500 verified civilian deaths, making it one of the deadliest urban battles since World War II.

08-28.title: South Asia floods
08-28.description: Monsoon floods triggered by some of the heaviest rainfall in decades inundated large parts of Bangladesh, northern and northeastern India, and Nepal during August 2017, displacing more than 40 million people. Confirmed fatalities numbered 1,288 by 2 September 2017 (over 1,400 across the three countries per some tallies), with hundreds of thousands of homes destroyed, crops ruined and outbreaks of waterborne disease reported in relief camps. The flooding destroyed infrastructure on a massive scale, leaving millions dependent on emergency food and shelter aid from national governments, the UN and the Red Cross.

09-19.title: Puebla earthquake, Mexico
09-19.description: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck on 19 September 2017, coinciding with the anniversary of the 1985 Mexico City quake, with its epicenter near Puebla state. The shaking collapsed dozens of buildings in Mexico City and nearby states, including schools, apartment blocks and offices; 370 people were killed and more than 6,000 injured. Rescue workers and volunteers dug through rubble for weeks in a national mobilization, and the toll included 19 children and six adults killed when an elementary school collapsed in Mexico City's Roma Norte district.

10-14.title: Mogadishu truck bombing
10-14.description: On 14 October 2017 a truck packed with explosives detonated at a busy intersection near the Safari Hotel in Mogadishu, followed shortly by a car bomb attack in the Madina district. The blasts killed at least 587 people and injured more than 300, according to a parliamentary investigative committee that concluded its count in March 2018, with hundreds of victims burned beyond recognition; a two-story building collapsed onto the truck's blast crater. No group claimed responsibility, though Somali officials attributed the attack to al-Shabaab. It was the deadliest bombing in Somalia's history.

10-17.title: Battle of Raqqa ends
10-17.description: The Syrian Democratic Forces, backed by heavy US-led coalition airstrikes, captured the Islamic State's self-declared capital of Raqqa on 17 October 2017 after a four-month siege. The battle left the city largely destroyed, with most buildings ruined by bombing and street fighting, and tens of thousands of residents displaced. Estimates of civilians killed during the campaign range from about 1,300 to 1,873 (Airwars and Amnesty International: 1,300-1,600 from coalition airstrikes; local monitors: 1,854-1,873), including hundreds who died as IS used residents as human shields or as they fled through minefields; the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights counted 1,540 civilians dead.

11-12.title: Iran-Iraq earthquake
11-12.description: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck near the Iran-Iraq border on 12 November 2017, with its epicenter about 30 km southwest of Halabja in Iraqi Kurdistan. At least 630 people were killed and more than 8,100 injured, the vast majority in Iran's Kermanshah province, where the town of Sarpol-e Zahab was devastated; roughly 12,000 homes collapsed across 14 Iranian provinces, and thousands of people spent weeks in tents through the winter. It was the deadliest earthquake worldwide in 2017, with Iraqi casualties centered on the Halabja area.

11-12.title: Beirut suicide bombings
11-12.description: Two suicide bombers detonated explosives in the crowded Bourj el-Barajneh district of southern Beirut, a predominantly Shia area of the Lebanese capital, killing 43 people and wounding about 240. The Islamic State claimed responsibility for the attack, the deadliest in Beirut in years.

11-24.title: Bir al-Abed mosque attack, Egypt
11-24.description: Gunmen detonated explosives and opened fire with automatic weapons on worshippers attending Friday prayers at the al-Rawda Sufi mosque in Bir al-Abed, North Sinai, on 24 November 2017. The attack killed 311 people, including 27 children, and wounded at least 128; attackers also fired on ambulances and vehicles carrying the wounded. No group formally claimed responsibility, but Egyptian authorities and analysis attributed it to the Islamic State's Sinai branch, targeting the local Sufi community; it remains the deadliest terrorist attack in Egypt's history.

11-24.title: Tazreen Fashion factory fire
11-24.description: On 24 November 2012, a fire broke out in the Tazreen Fashion garment factory in Ashulia on the outskirts of Dhaka, killing at least 117 workers and injuring more than 200. Exit doors were locked, forcing workers to jump from upper floors; the disaster highlighted fire-safety failures in the Bangladeshi garment industry and preceded the larger Rana Plaza collapse in 2013.

01-27.title: M23 capture of Goma
01-27.location: Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
01-27.description: Between January 23 and 30, 2025, Rwandan-backed M23 rebels captured Goma, the capital of North Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, after heavy fighting against the national army, UN and SADC peacekeepers, and allied militias; the UN estimated about 2,900 people were killed and another 2,900 wounded, with hundreds of thousands displaced.

01-27.title: Kabul ambulance bombing
01-27.description: A suicide bomber drove an ambulance packed with explosives through a checkpoint and detonated it in a crowded district of central Kabul near the Ministry of Interior, targeting Afghan security personnel and civilians. The blast killed at least 103 people and injured more than 235, making it one of the deadliest attacks in Afghanistan in recent years. The Taliban claimed responsibility, and the attack underscored the deteriorating security situation in the capital.

01-27.title: Kiss nightclub fire
01-27.description: On January 27, 2013, pyrotechnics set off by the performing band ignited flammable acoustic foam on the ceiling of the Kiss nightclub in Santa Maria, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. The resulting fire, dense smoke, and stampede killed 242 people, mostly university students, and injured at least 630 others; the venue's single functioning exit and the absence of adequate fire safety systems contributed to the deaths, making it the second-deadliest fire in Brazilian history.

02-16.title: Quetta Hazara market bombing
02-16.description: On February 16, 2013, a suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a vegetable market in Hazara Town, Quetta, Pakistan, in an attack targeting the Shia Hazara community. At least 84 people were killed and more than 170 were wounded; the Sunni militant group Lashkar-e-Jhangvi claimed responsibility, and the bombing was the latest in a series of attacks that year against Hazaras in Balochistan.

06-16.title: Mpondwe school massacre
06-16.description: Armed assailants from the Allied Democratic Forces, an armed group linked to the Islamic State, attacked the Lhubiriha Secondary School in the town of Mpondwe near Uganda's border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, killing 42 people, including at least 37 students, and abducting several others. Most victims were killed by machetes, and several students were burned in their dormitory. Uganda launched military operations against the group in response, including strikes inside Congolese territory.

06-16.title: Uttarakhand floods and landslides
06-16.description: In mid-June 2013, exceptionally heavy monsoon rains caused flash floods, cloudbursts, and landslides across the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand, India, with the worst devastation around Kedarnath on June 16-17. More than 5,700 people were presumed dead in the state (over 6,000 including surrounding regions), and tens of thousands of pilgrims and tourists were stranded in the Kedarnath valley before rescue operations ended.

07-06.title: Western Japan floods and landslides
07-06.description: Record-breaking rainfall, in some areas exceeding 180 millimeters per hour, triggered devastating flooding and landslides across western Japan in early July 2018, most severely in Hiroshima, Okayama, and Ehime prefectures. Rivers burst their banks, and landslides destroyed hillside homes. At least 225 people were killed and thousands displaced in Japan's worst weather disaster in decades, prompting the evacuation of millions of residents.

07-06.title: Lac-Mégantic rail disaster
07-06.description: On July 6, 2013, an unattended 73-car freight train carrying crude oil rolled down a slope and derailed in downtown Lac-Mégantic, Quebec, Canada, exploding into fires that destroyed much of the town center and killed 47 people. Investigators found the train had been left with insufficiently secured brakes; the disaster became the deadliest rail accident in Canadian history.

08-21.title: Ghouta chemical weapons attack
08-21.description: On August 21, 2013, rockets carrying the nerve agent sarin struck opposition-held suburbs of Damascus in the Ghouta region of Syria, killing an estimated 1,400 people (estimates range from 281 to 1,729, with the U.S. government assessing about 1,429). United Nations investigators confirmed the use of sarin, and the attack, attributed to Syrian government forces, was the deadliest chemical weapons use since the Iran-Iraq War and led to an international disarmament agreement.

08-21.title: Daraya massacre
08-21.description: Between 20 and 25 August 2012, Syrian government forces and allied militiamen carried out a mass killing in the town of Darayya near Damascus after a siege and an offer of safe passage. SOHR documented about 320 killed and the opposition reported up to 400 bodies found in homes, streets, and a mosque; a later UN Commission of Inquiry found reasonable grounds that the murders constituted war crimes.

09-16.title: Washington Navy Yard shooting
09-16.description: On September 16, 2013, a former Navy reservist with a history of mental health problems opened fire at the Washington Navy Yard in Washington, D.C., killing 12 people and injuring at least 8 before being shot dead by police. The shooting was among the deadliest workplace and gun violence incidents in the United States in 2013.

09-21.title: Tabas Coal Mine Explosion
09-21.description: On September 21, 2024, a methane gas explosion followed by carbon monoxide release in the Madanjoo coal mine near Tabas, Iran, killed at least 52 miners and injured more than 20. The blast occurred in one of Iran's largest coal mines, rescue operations were hampered by underground gas levels, and authorities launched an investigation into safety conditions.

09-21.title: Westgate shopping mall attack
09-21.description: On September 21, 2013, gunmen from the al-Shabaab militant group attacked the upscale Westgate shopping mall in Nairobi, Kenya, firing on shoppers and staff in a four-day siege. At least 71 people were killed, including 62 civilians and 5 Kenyan soldiers, with 4 attackers also dead, and around 200 people were wounded; parts of the mall collapsed during the security operation.

09-22.title: Peshawar church bombing
09-22.description: On September 22, 2013, two suicide bombers attacked All Saints Church in Peshawar, Pakistan, during Sunday services, killing at least 85 people and injuring more than 200 in the deadliest attack on Christians in Pakistan's history. A Taliban-linked group claimed responsibility; the official toll was later revised upward to as many as 127 in some tallies.

09-24.title: Balochistan earthquake
09-24.description: On September 24, 2013, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Awaran District in Balochistan, Pakistan, killing at least 825 people (some tallies cite 840) and injuring about 600, with thousands of mud-brick homes destroyed in the remote region. The quake also thrust up a new island off the coast near Gwadar and was the deadliest earthquake in Pakistan since 2005.

11-08.title: Camp Fire wildfire
11-08.description: The Camp Fire, ignited in Butte County, California, exploded into the state's most destructive and deadliest wildfire on record at the time, destroying the town of Paradise and surrounding communities. Fueled by drought and strong winds, it burned over 150,000 acres and destroyed 18,804 structures. Eighty-five people were killed, the vast majority in Paradise, with over 12,000 homes lost and thousands displaced.

11-08.title: Typhoon Haiyan
11-08.description: On November 8, 2013, Super Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda), one of the most powerful tropical cyclones ever recorded, made landfall in the central Philippines with sustained winds near 315 km/h, killing 6,300 people across the country (more than 6,350 including Vietnam, China, and Taiwan) and injuring tens of thousands. Catastrophic storm surges devastated Tacloban City and neighboring islands, and around 4 million people were displaced.

12-15.title: Outbreak of the South Sudanese Civil War
12-15.description: On December 15, 2013, fighting broke out in Juba, South Sudan, between forces loyal to President Salva Kiir and supporters of former Vice President Riek Machar following an alleged coup attempt, igniting a civil war. At least 1,000 people were killed in the initial outbreak by late December 2013, including civilians massacred along ethnic lines, and tens of thousands were displaced; the conflict subsequently spread nationwide.

02-06.title: Islamabad mosque suicide bombing
02-06.description: On 6 February 2026, a suicide bomber detonated explosives at the Khadija Tul Kubra Mosque, a Shia mosque in the Tarlai Kalan area of Islamabad, Pakistan, during Friday prayers, killing at least 31 worshippers and injuring more than 100. It was the deadliest attack in Islamabad in nearly a decade.

02-06.title: Turkey–Syria earthquake
02-06.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck near the Turkey–Syria border at 4:17 a.m., followed by a magnitude 7.5 aftershock hours later, collapsing thousands of buildings across southeastern Turkey and northern Syria. More than 59,000 people were confirmed dead, including about 50,700 in Turkey and over 5,900 in Syria, with an estimated 1.5 million people left homeless. It was one of the deadliest earthquakes in the region in modern history, compounded in Syria by the country's ongoing civil war.

02-06.title: Meinong (Kaohsiung) earthquake
02-06.description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck southern Taiwan at 3:57 a.m. local time with its epicenter near Meinong, Kaohsiung. The quake toppled several buildings, most notably the 17-story Weiguan Jinlong apartment complex in Tainan, where 115 of the 117 fatalities occurred. Around 550 people were injured, and the quake was the deadliest in Taiwan since the 1999 Jiji earthquake.

02-25.title: Severnaya coal mine explosions, Vorkuta
02-25.description: Two methane gas explosions hit the Severnaya coal mine in Vorkuta, Komi Republic, on February 25 and 28, 2016. The first explosion killed four miners; a second explosion during the rescue effort killed a group of rescuers and trapped miners underground. In total, 31 miners and five rescue workers died, making it Russia's deadliest mine disaster in years; nine survivors were rescued.

06-28.title: European heat waves
06-28.description: Record-breaking heat waves struck western Europe in late June and late July 2019, with France registering its highest-ever temperature of 45.9°C at Gallargues-le-Montueux on 28 June. France's public health agency attributed 1,435 excess deaths to the June heat wave, and a subsequent peer-reviewed study estimated roughly 2,500 deaths across Europe attributable to the summer's heat waves. Schools closed, rail services were suspended and cities opened cooling centres as authorities issued the highest heat alerts for the first time in several countries.

06-28.title: Atatürk Airport attack
06-28.description: Three suicide bombers opened fire with automatic weapons and then detonated explosives in the international arrivals terminal of Istanbul's Atatürk Airport. Forty-five people, including the attackers, were killed and more than 230 wounded. Turkish authorities identified Islamic State as responsible, making it the deadliest terror attack in Turkey in the year to that point.

07-03.title: Karrada shopping district bombing
07-03.description: A suicide truck bomb exploded shortly after midnight in Baghdad's Karrada district, an area crowded with families shopping during Ramadan, setting several buildings ablaze.
