At least 292 people were killed in the immediate aftermath, with the final toll later placed at more than 320 dead and hundreds wounded. Islamic State claimed responsibility for the deadliest single attack in Iraq since 2003.

08-30.title: Typhoon Lionrock floods in North Korea
08-30.description: Typhoon Lionrock crossed Japan's Tohoku region on August 30 and produced torrential rains that caused devastating flash floods in North Korea's North Hamgyong Province along the Tumen River, washing away entire villages and leaving tens of thousands homeless. Initial UN assessments counted 133 dead and 395 missing in North Korea; later analyses put the country's death toll at more than 500, with about 550 total deaths when the 22 killed in Japan and 3 in Russia are included.

10-04.title: Hurricane Matthew in Haiti
10-04.description: Hurricane Matthew, a Category 4 storm with winds near 145 mph, struck southwestern Haiti on October 4, bringing torrential rain that triggered catastrophic flash floods and mudslides in Grand'Anse and Sud departments. The storm killed 674 people in Haiti and 731 across all affected countries, including 47 in the United States; it destroyed more than 200,000 homes and triggered a major surge in cholera cases. It was Haiti's worst humanitarian crisis since the 2010 earthquake.

10-24.title: Quetta police training college attack
10-24.description: Three attackers stormed the Balochistan Police College in Quetta late on October 24, taking unarmed police recruits hostage and battling security forces for several hours before all three were killed. At least 61 people, mostly recruits, were killed and more than 165 wounded. Islamic State's Khorasan branch claimed responsibility for the deadliest attack in Pakistan since the 2014 Peshawar school massacre.

01-20.title: Kano bombings
01-20.description: Boko Haram militants launched coordinated attacks across Kano on 20 January 2012, attacking five police stations, two immigration offices and the State Security Service headquarters with bombs and gunfire, then shooting pedestrians in the streets. The government confirmed 185 killed, including about 150 civilians and at least 32 police officers, making it one of the deadliest single attacks of the insurgency.

07-21.title: Beijing floods
07-21.description: On 21 July 2012, an extreme rainstorm — the heaviest rainfall on record in Beijing — flooded the city over a 20-hour period, killing 79 people, many of whom drowned in flooded road underpasses and basements. More than 1.6 million people were affected and some 8,200 homes were destroyed, with damages estimated at about 10 billion yuan.

08-05.title: Lombok earthquake sequence
08-05.description: A series of major earthquakes struck the island of Lombok between July 29 and August 19, 2018, the strongest being a magnitude 7.0 quake on August 5. The quakes destroyed more than 70,000 homes, triggered landslides on Mount Rinjani, and killed at least 563 people, including tourists in the Gili Islands, with over 1,000 injured and roughly 350,000 displaced.

08-05.title: Wisconsin Sikh temple shooting
08-05.description: On 5 August 2012, a gunman opened fire during a service at the Sikh Temple of Wisconsin in Oak Creek, killing six worshippers and wounding four others before taking his own life. The shooter, Wade Michael Page, a former US Army soldier with ties to white supremacist groups, died by suicide at the scene; a seventh victim later died of his injuries in 2020.

08-05.title: Russian missile strikes on Kyiv kill two
08-05.description: Russia attacked Kyiv with waves of ballistic missiles and drones after midnight, killing at least 21 people - three in the capital and 18 in the surrounding region - and injuring more than 45. The assault used 24 ballistic missiles, four Zircon/Onyx missiles and 115 drones, hitting warehouses, a railway station and other civilian infrastructure; air defences intercepted 98 drones.

08-05.title: Israeli fire kills four in Gaza
08-05.description: Israel killed four more Palestinians in Gaza over 24 hours, bringing the war's death toll to 73,381, the Gaza Health Ministry said. Since the ceasefire took effect in October 2025, Israeli violations have killed 1,254 Palestinians and injured 4,121.

08-05.title: Israeli airstrike on south Lebanon kills one
08-05.description: An Israeli airstrike targeted a prayer hall in the southern Lebanese town of Tebnine in the Bint Jbeil district, killing one Lebanese civilian and wounding 11 to 12 others, Lebanon's National News Agency and the Health Ministry reported. The strike came as a new round of Rome talks on the border was under way.

08-05.title: Sri Lanka floods and mudslides kill seven
08-05.description: Torrential rains triggered floods and mudslides across Sri Lanka's central highlands, killing at least eight people - six in Nuwara Eliya, one in Kandy and one in Puttalam - and affecting more than 16,000 people, with nearly 11,000 evacuated. Authorities closed schools in the affected areas.

08-05.title: India monsoon floods and landslides kill more than 100 since July
08-05.description: An official tally released on August 5 showed that floods and landslides triggered by monsoon rains had killed at least 133 people across India since the beginning of July: 87 in Assam (47 in Sivasagar district alone), 31 in Jammu and Kashmir, and 15 in Kerala, with seven people still missing and more than 10,000 in relief camps.

08-05.title: Russian strike on grain ship in Odesa region kills one
08-05.description: Russian forces attacked a merchant dry cargo ship flying the flag of Guinea-Bissau and loaded with Ukrainian wheat, damaging the hull and starting a fire. One Ukrainian sailor was killed and three crew members were injured; the crew was evacuated to shore.

08-05.title: Hezbollah blast kills two Israeli soldiers in southern Lebanon
08-05.description: Two Israeli soldiers - a company commander and a soldier of the 55th Armored Brigade - were killed and four others seriously wounded when an explosive device blasted in the southern Lebanese village of Majdal Zoun on Wednesday, the Israeli military said Thursday.

08-05.title: Mass shooting in Caswell County, North Carolina kills three
08-05.location: Caswell County, North Carolina, United States
08-05.description: A mass shooting at a rural home in Caswell County, North Carolina, left three family members dead - including the suspected shooter - and a fourth relative hospitalized, according to the Caswell County Sheriff's Office and the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation.

08-05.title: Mudslide buries household in Zhashui County, Shaanxi
08-05.description: A sudden mudslide triggered by days of heavy rainfall buried members of a household in Xingping township, Zhashui County, while they were clearing water near their home on August 5. One person was confirmed dead and two remained missing; continuous rain from July 30 to August 5 reached 321.4 mm in the county.

08-11.title: East Azerbaijan earthquakes
08-11.location: Ahar and Varzaqan, East Azerbaijan, Iran
08-11.description: On 11 August 2012, twin earthquakes of magnitude 6.4 and 6.2 struck 11 minutes apart near the cities of Ahar and Varzaqan in northwestern Iran. At least 306 people were killed and more than 3,000 injured, with thousands of buildings destroyed or damaged in rural villages across the region and at least 80 aftershocks following.

08-11.title: Russian combined strike on Zaporizhzhia kills seven
08-11.description: A combined Russian attack using ballistic missiles — including North Korean-supplied missiles, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky — and guided aerial bombs hit Zaporizhzhia on the night of August 10-11, killing seven people and wounding at least 24, according to regional military administration head Ivan Fedorov. The strike shut the Zaporizhstal steel plant, where seven workers died and 21 were injured, and damaged residential buildings and infrastructure; August 12 was declared a day of mourning in the region. Kyiv was separately targeted by ballistic missiles.

08-11.title: Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk region kill five
08-11.description: Russian forces carried out massive strikes on the Dnipropetrovsk region on the evening of August 10 and during the night of August 11, killing five people — including three minors — and injuring seven others, according to Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office. Regional authorities earlier reported three dead, including a 15-year-old boy, and five injured, with drone and artillery attacks hitting five districts and damaging logistics facilities.

08-11.title: Russian strike on tanker truck in Odesa region kills two
08-11.description: A Russian strike on a tanker truck in the Odesa region on August 11 killed two people and wounded three others, according to Oleh Kiper, head of the regional military administration. Hours later, a Russian drone hit an apartment building in Odesa with no reported casualties.

08-11.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Voronezh region kills one
08-11.description: A Ukrainian drone attack on the Voronezh region killed a 49-year-old man who was struck by falling UAV debris in the Novousmansky district and died in hospital, and wounded two other people, according to Governor Alexander Gusev. The attack was part of an overnight wave in which Russian air defenses reported intercepting 396 Ukrainian drones, and it sparked fires at two warehouse facilities near Voronezh.

08-11.title: Houthi missile strike on cargo ship Tihama in Bab el-Mandeb kills six
08-11.description: A Houthi missile strike on the commercial vessel Tihama in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait killed six people and injured 10 others, Yemen's coast guard said. Officials described a 'double-tap' attack that set the cargo ship ablaze; among the dead were crew members from Pakistan and Indonesia.

08-11.title: Man kills wife and four children in Winfield, Kansas murder-suicide
08-11.description: A 53-year-old man, Ronald H. Williams Sr., shot and killed his wife, 44-year-old Kelly George, and their four children aged 3 to 9 before taking his own life early Tuesday morning, August 11, in Winfield, Kansas. Williams called 911 after the shootings, and police found the six bodies inside the home.

08-11.title: Flash floods in Adré kill three
08-11.description: Heavy rains in the afternoon triggered flash floods in several neighborhoods of Adré, a town in the Assoungha department of Ouaddaï Province in eastern Chad, killing three people; local media reported five people were swept away by the water.

08-11.title: Ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba killing 46
08-11.description: An overloaded passenger ferry capsized on Lake Kariba after being hit by strong waves on Tuesday afternoon. Police confirmed at least 44 people died, including children, and dozens of others were rescued; President Emmerson Mnangagwa declared the incident a state of disaster.

09-05.title: Luding earthquake (Sichuan)
09-05.description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck Luding County in Sichuan Province, China, on 5 September 2022, triggering landslides that blocked rivers and destroyed mountain villages. At least 93 people were killed and 424 injured, with more than 600,000 people affected. Dozens of the dead were road workers and drivers caught by rockslides along the Dadu River valley.
sources: Ministry of Emergency Management of China

09-05.title: Pakistan monsoon floods — 2012
09-05.location: Sindh, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, Pakistan
09-05.description: Heavy monsoon rains from a low-pressure system that lingered over Pakistan from 3 to 12 September 2012 caused severe flooding across southern Punjab, upper Sindh, and parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. The National Disaster Management Authority reported 455 deaths and some five million people affected, with record rainfall in several cities and widespread destruction of homes and crops.

11-14.title: Piatra Neamț hospital fire
11-14.description: On 14 November 2020, a fire broke out in the COVID-19 ward of Piatra Neamț Emergency Hospital in Romania, killing 10 patients who were being treated for COVID-19 and injuring four others, including two doctors. The fire, extinguished in about 25 minutes, was suspected to have been caused by a short circuit in a syringe pump that ignited oxygen supplies. It was one of a series of deadly hospital fires in Romania during the COVID-19 pandemic, prompting calls for better hospital fire safety.

11-14.title: Gaza conflict — Operation Pillar of Defense
11-14.description: On 14 November 2012, Israel launched an eight-day military offensive against Gaza following rocket fire and the killing of Hamas military chief Ahmed Jabari. A UN Human Rights Council report recorded 174 Palestinians killed, 107 of them civilians, and B'Tselem counted 167; six Israelis were killed by Palestinian rockets, and hundreds more were wounded on both sides before a ceasefire took effect on 21 November.

12-04.title: Typhoon Bopha (Pablo)
12-04.description: Typhoon Bopha, the strongest storm ever recorded to strike the Philippines at that time of year, made landfall on Mindanao late on 3 December / early 4 December 2012 as a Category 5-equivalent super typhoon. The NDRRMC's final toll was 1,901 dead, with widespread flash floods and landslides in Davao Oriental and Compostela Valley, where mudslides buried villages, including in New Bataan.

01-03.title: Kerman Bombings (Soleimani Memorial Attack)
01-03.description: On January 3, 2024, two explosions struck a crowd gathered in Kerman, Iran, for a ceremony commemorating the fourth anniversary of the assassination of General Qasem Soleimani. Islamic State (ISIS) claimed responsibility for the attack, which killed at least 95 people and wounded about 280, making it one of the deadliest attacks in Iran's modern history.

01-03.title: Baga massacre by Boko Haram
01-03.description: Boko Haram militants seized the town of Baga in Borno State and attacked Baga and surrounding towns, setting homes and shops ablaze and killing civilians as they fled. Nigerian officials reported a toll of about 150, while Amnesty International estimated, based on witness accounts, that as many as 2,000 people were killed. Tens of thousands of residents fled across Lake Chad into Niger.

01-07.title: Los Angeles wildfires (Palisades and Eaton fires)
01-07.description: From January 7 to 31, 2025, wind-driven wildfires devastated Los Angeles County, most destructively the Palisades Fire in Pacific Palisades and the Eaton Fire in the Altadena-Pasadena area, destroying more than 16,000 structures and killing at least 31 people, one of the deadliest and most destructive wildfire events in California history.

01-07.title: Charlie Hebdo shooting
01-07.description: Two gunmen affiliated with al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula stormed the office of the satirical weekly Charlie Hebdo during its morning editorial meeting, killing 12 people, including eight journalists and two police officers. The attackers, brothers Said and Cherif Kouachi, were killed in a standoff two days later; attacks by a related cell in the Paris region killed four more people in the same week.

05-26.title: Indian heat wave
05-26.description: An extreme heat wave with temperatures exceeding 47 degrees Celsius swept southern and eastern India in May 2015, killing at least 2,500 people. Andhra Pradesh, with about 1,735 deaths, and Telangana, with about 585, were hardest hit. It was India's deadliest heat wave since 1979.

06-17.title: Charleston church shooting
06-17.description: A 21-year-old white supremacist, Dylann Roof, opened fire during a Bible study at Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church, one of the oldest Black churches in the United States, killing nine parishioners and wounding one. Roof fled the scene but was arrested the following morning; he was later convicted on federal hate-crime and murder charges and sentenced to death.

06-24.title: 2026 Venezuela earthquakes
06-24.description: On 24 June 2026, a doublet of earthquakes — an Mw 7.2 foreshock followed roughly 30 seconds later by an Mw 7.5 mainshock — struck the central Venezuelan coast, with epicenters in Yaracuy state and offshore La Guaira state. At least 5,546 people were killed and 16,740 injured, with tens of thousands initially missing; nearly 800 buildings collapsed and about 590,000 were damaged, and the worst-hit communities in La Guaira lost roughly 80% of their buildings. The UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction estimated US$37 billion in direct damage. The death toll rose to 6,125 by August 4, 2026, with nearly 17,000 people injured, as rescue and recovery operations continued.

06-24.title: Surfside condominium collapse
06-24.description: The 12-story Champlain Towers South condominium partially collapsed at night in Surfside, near Miami Beach, killing 98 residents and leaving a pile of rubble that took weeks to fully search. Investigations pointed to long-standing structural deterioration, including corrosion of reinforcing steel, compounded by years of deferred maintenance.

06-24.title: Karachi heat wave
06-24.description: A heat wave with temperatures reaching 44-49 degrees Celsius struck Karachi and southern Pakistan during the Muslim fasting month of Ramadan, killing at least 1,265 people in the city, most of them poor residents without electricity or water, and about 2,000 across the country. Hospitals reported a surge in heat-stroke cases and morgues were overwhelmed as power outages worsened the crisis.

10-10.title: Ankara peace rally bombing
10-10.description: Two suicide bombers, later linked to the Islamic State, detonated bombs among crowds gathered for a peace rally near Ankara's central train station, killing at least 102 people, the figure given by Turkish prosecutors, and injuring more than 500. Some later counts put the death toll as high as 109. It was the deadliest terrorist attack in Turkey's history, surpassing the 2013 Reyhanli bombings.

01-15.title: Yeti Airlines Flight 691 crash
01-15.description: Yeti Airlines flight 691, an ATR 72-500 operating from Kathmandu to Pokhara, crashed while on approach to Pokhara's newly opened international airport, killing all 72 people on board (68 passengers and 4 crew). The aircraft was observed in a stall-like attitude shortly before impact, and Nepal's investigation commission later reported that the pilots had inadvertently put the propellers into feather mode during the approach. The crash was Nepal's deadliest aviation accident since 1992.

01-15.title: Sulawesi earthquake
01-15.description: A magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck near the city of Mamuju on Sulawesi island, killing at least 105 people and injuring hundreds more. The quake toppled homes, hospitals, and hotels, triggering landslides in the mountainous region. Thousands were displaced and months of aftershocks hampered rescue and recovery efforts.

01-15.title: DusitD2 complex attack
01-15.description: Four al-Shabaab gunmen stormed the DusitD2 hotel and office complex in Nairobi's Westlands district on 15 January 2019, detonating explosives and firing on guests and workers. Twenty-one people were killed and dozens wounded before the attackers were killed in a standoff that lasted nearly 20 hours. Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility, saying the attack targeted a US-run hotel and a Kenyan court complex nearby.

02-01.title: Myanmar military coup and crackdown
02-01.description: On February 1, the Myanmar military seized power in a coup, detaining elected leader Aung San Suu Kyi and triggering nationwide civil disobedience and protests. Security forces responded with lethal force, and by the end of 2021 more than 1,400 civilians had been killed and over 10,000 detained, according to monitoring groups such as the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners.

02-07.title: Chamoli glacier disaster
02-07.description: A portion of the Nanda Devi glacier broke off in Chamoli district, sending a massive flash flood of water, ice, and debris down the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga rivers. The flood destroyed two hydroelectric power projects and swept away workers and infrastructure, leaving roughly 200 people dead or missing, most of them power-plant employees.

03-16.title: Kocani nightclub fire
03-16.description: On March 16, 2025, pyrotechnics used during a concert ignited flammable acoustic foam in the unlicensed, overcrowded Pulse nightclub in Kocani, North Macedonia, producing a rapidly spreading fire and toxic smoke; 59 people were killed at the scene and the final death toll reached 63 as injured victims died in hospital, with about 193 injured.

03-16.title: Atlanta spa shootings
03-16.description: A gunman attacked three massage businesses in the Atlanta area, killing eight people, six of whom were women of Asian descent. The shooter was arrested hours later in south Georgia. The killings drew national attention to anti-Asian violence and were investigated as a possible hate crime.

05-03.title: Mexico City metro overpass collapse
05-03.description: An elevated section of the Mexico City Metro's Line 12 collapsed between Olivos and Tezonco stations as a train passed over it, killing 26 people and injuring about 70. The train cars plunged onto a busy road below. Investigations later attributed the collapse to structural design and construction deficiencies.

05-10.title: Baghlan Flash Floods
05-10.description: On May 10, 2024, heavy seasonal rainfall caused flash floods that swept through villages in northern Afghanistan, most severely in Baghlan Province. United Nations agencies reported at least 315 people killed and more than 1,600 injured, with tens of thousands of homes destroyed or damaged and several thousand people displaced.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

05-10.title: Eleven-day Gaza conflict
05-10.description: An 11-day war between Israel and Hamas erupted after weeks of tension in Jerusalem, with Israeli airstrikes and Palestinian rocket fire striking densely populated areas. At least 256 Palestinians, including 66 children, and 13 people in Israel were killed. More than 100,000 Gazans were displaced before a ceasefire took effect on May 21.

06-04.title: BM Container Depot fire and explosions (Sitakunda)
06-04.description: A fire broke out at the BM Container Depot near Sitakunda, Bangladesh, on 4 June 2022, igniting chemicals stored in shipping containers and triggering a series of massive explosions. At least 49 people were killed and more than 450 injured, many of them firefighters and workers who had tried to contain the initial blaze. The explosions hurled containers hundreds of metres, in one of Bangladesh's deadliest industrial accidents.

06-04.title: Solhan village massacre
06-04.description: Armed jihadists, reportedly affiliated with al-Qaeda-linked groups, attacked the village of Solhan in Burkina Faso's Sahel region, killing around 160 people, including many children, and burning homes. It was the deadliest attack in the country's history since the insurgency began in 2015 and forced thousands of residents to flee the area.

06-25.title: Pacific Northwest heat dome
06-25.location: Pacific Northwest, United States and Canada
06-25.description: An exceptional heat dome pushed temperatures to records across the Pacific Northwest, with Lytton, British Columbia, reaching 49.6°C (121.3°F), Canada's hottest temperature ever recorded. The heat is estimated to have caused about 800 deaths or more across Canada and the U.S., mostly among elderly and vulnerable people in homes without air conditioning.

08-26.title: Kabul airport bombing
08-26.description: During the chaotic U.S. troop withdrawal from Afghanistan, an ISIS-K suicide bomber detonated a device amid crowds gathered at Hamid Karzai International Airport's Abbey Gate, followed by a second explosion. At least 183 people were killed, including 13 U.S. service members and roughly 170 Afghan civilians, many of whom were attempting to flee the country.

12-10.title: Mayfield tornado outbreak
12-10.description: A historic tornado outbreak spawned an EF4 tornado that leveled the town of Mayfield, Kentucky, and caused damage across six states from Arkansas to Ohio during the night of December 10-11. At least 89 people were killed, most of them in Kentucky, where it was the deadliest tornado event in the state's history, with deaths also reported in Tennessee and elsewhere.

06-03.title: Khartoum massacre
06-03.description: On 3 June 2019, Sudanese security forces, including the Rapid Support Forces, violently dispersed a civilian sit-in outside the army headquarters in Khartoum that had been demanding a transition to civilian rule. The Sudanese Doctors' Syndicate documented at least 104 deaths, with later tallies exceeding 128 including children, and hundreds of people wounded; an official inquiry reported 87 deaths. The crackdown followed the ouster of President Omar al-Bashir and preceded a power-sharing agreement that established a civilian-led transitional government later that year.

06-03.title: Volcán de Fuego eruption
06-03.description: Guatemala's Volcán de Fuego erupted violently, sending pyroclastic flows and ash that buried the villages of San Miguel Los Lotes and El Rodeo in mud and rock. The eruption killed 425 people according to Guatemala's disaster agency (CONRED), injured hundreds, destroyed thousands of homes, and forced the evacuation of over 12,000 people, while dozens of victims were never recovered from the deposits.

04-07.title: Douma chemical weapons attack
04-07.description: A suspected chemical weapons attack struck the town of Douma in Syria's Eastern Ghouta region during the Syrian civil war, the last rebel-held area near Damascus. Medical and rescue groups reported at least 43 people killed and hundreds suffering respiratory distress from what they described as exposure to chlorine and sarin gas. The Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons later confirmed the use of chlorine, and the attack prompted US-led airstrikes on Syrian facilities.

10-27.title: Pittsburgh synagogue shooting
10-27.description: A gunman entered the Tree of Life synagogue in the Squirrel Hill neighborhood of Pittsburgh during Shabbat morning services and opened fire, killing 11 worshippers and wounding six others, including four police officers. The attacker, who expressed antisemitic views online, was arrested after a shootout with police. It was the deadliest antisemitic attack in US history, and the community later rebuilt and reopened the synagogue.

01-21.title: Monterey Park mass shooting
01-21.description: A 72-year-old gunman opened fire at Star Ballroom Dance Studio during a Lunar New Year celebration in Monterey Park, California, killing 11 people and wounding 9 others. The shooter then drove to a second dance hall in Alhambra, where he was disarmed by a patron, and died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound the next day after being confronted by police. It was one of the deadliest mass shootings in Los Angeles County history.

01-30.title: Peshawar mosque bombing
01-30.description: A suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vest inside a mosque within a police compound in Peshawar, Pakistan, during afternoon prayers, killing at least 83 people, mostly police officers, and wounding more than 220 others. The bombing collapsed part of the mosque roof onto worshippers. The Pakistani Taliban (Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan) claimed responsibility, saying the attack was retaliation for military operations against the group.

05-04.title: South Kivu floods and landslides
05-04.description: Days of torrential rain triggered flash floods and landslides in the Kalehe territory of South Kivu province in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, burying villages such as Bushushu and Nyamukubi under mud. More than 400 people were killed, with local officials later counting 438 bodies, and thousands were left missing or displaced. The flooding was among the deadliest natural disasters recorded in the region.

05-06.title: Allen outlet mall shooting
05-06.description: A gunman opened fire at the Allen Premium Outlets mall in Allen, Texas, killing eight people, including children, and wounding seven others before being fatally shot by a police officer, bringing the total dead to nine. The attacker, a 33-year-old who had posted racist and extremist content online, was armed with a rifle. The shooting was the deadliest mass shooting in Texas since 2019.

05-20.title: Battle of Bakhmut
05-20.description: Russian forces completed their capture of the eastern Ukrainian city of Bakhmut on May 20, 2023, ending one of the bloodiest battles of the Russia–Ukraine war, which had raged for about ten months. U.S. officials estimated that roughly 20,000 Russian soldiers had been killed in the battle, with tens of thousands more wounded, and Ukrainian officials reported thousands of their own soldiers killed; the city was reduced to ruins. Independent verification of exact casualties was not possible due to the secrecy of the warring sides.
sources: Institute for the Study of War

05-20.title: Cyclone Amphan
05-20.description: Cyclone Amphan, the first super cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal since 1999, made landfall near Bakkhali in West Bengal, India on 20 May 2020 with winds up to 260 km/h. The storm killed 133 people in total, including 103 in India (most in West Bengal) and 26 in Bangladesh, and displaced millions. Amphan severely damaged Kolkata and the Sundarbans, and its landfall during the COVID-19 pandemic complicated evacuation and relief efforts.

06-02.title: Odisha train collision
06-02.description: Three trains collided near the Balasore district in Odisha, India, when the Coromandel Express derailed onto an adjacent track and was struck by a passenger train, with a stationary freight train also involved. At least 292 people were killed and more than 1,000 were injured in India's deadliest rail disaster in decades. India's railways minister attributed the crash to a signal alteration error in the electronic interlocking system.

11-03.title: Jajarkot earthquake
11-03.description: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck the Jajarkot district in western Nepal on November 3, toppling thousands of poorly built mud-and-stone homes across remote hill villages in Jajarkot and Rukum West districts. At least 153 people were killed and hundreds injured, with thousands left sleeping outdoors in cold weather. The quake was Nepal's deadliest since the 2015 Gorkha earthquake.

11-03.title: Hurricane Eta
11-03.description: Hurricane Eta made landfall near Puerto Cabezas, Nicaragua on 3 November 2020 as a Category 4 hurricane, then stalled over Central America for two days, triggering catastrophic flash floods and landslides across the region. At least 189 people died, including 74 in Honduras, 60 in Guatemala and 19 in Panama, with more than 100 missing. Eta was followed within two weeks by Hurricane Iota, which compounded the destruction in Honduras and Nicaragua.

12-18.title: Jishishan earthquake
12-18.description: A magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck Jishishan County in Gansu province, China, in the early hours of December 18, triggering landslides and collapsing village homes across Gansu and neighboring Qinghai province during sub-freezing night temperatures. At least 151 people were killed and nearly 1,000 injured, with hundreds of thousands affected. It was China's deadliest earthquake since 2014, and rescue operations were hampered by cold weather.

12-21.title: Prague university shooting
12-21.description: A 24-year-old history student opened fire at Charles University's Faculty of Arts building in central Prague, killing 14 people and wounding 25 others before killing himself as police closed in. The gunman had earlier killed his father, and investigators linked him to the earlier killing of a man and his infant daughter in a nearby forest. It was the deadliest mass shooting in the Czech Republic's history.

02-02.title: Central Chile Wildfires
02-02.location: Viña del Mar, Valparaíso Region, Chile
02-02.description: In early February 2024, wildfires driven by extreme heat, drought, and wind swept through central Chile, most destructively in the Valparaíso Region around Viña del Mar. The fires killed at least 137 people, burned more than 27,000 hectares, and destroyed thousands of homes, making it Chile's deadliest fire disaster on record.

04-26.title: Kenya Floods and Landslides
04-26.description: Torrential rains and flash floods in Kenya from mid-March through May 2024, driven by an unusually heavy long-rains season, caused rivers to overflow, dams to breach, and landslides to bury communities, including in the capital Nairobi. At least 291 people were killed, hundreds were reported missing, and more than 280,000 were displaced, prompting the government to declare the floods a national disaster.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

05-01.title: Rio Grande do Sul Floods
05-01.location: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
05-01.description: Record rainfall from late April 2024 triggered catastrophic flooding in Brazil's southern state of Rio Grande do Sul, overwhelming Porto Alegre and hundreds of municipalities. The floods killed at least 183 people, with dozens more reported missing, displaced more than 580,000, and destroyed or damaged thousands of homes, businesses, and roads.

06-15.title: Hajj Extreme Heat Deaths
06-15.description: Extreme heat during the 2024 Hajj pilgrimage in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, in mid-June killed more than 1,300 pilgrims, with temperatures exceeding 50 degrees Celsius at times. Most deaths occurred among unregistered pilgrims lacking access to official facilities; Egypt, Indonesia, and India reported the largest national casualty counts, and several countries attributed the deaths to heatstroke.

09-23.title: Israel–Hezbollah War in Lebanon
09-23.description: From late September to November 2024, Israel launched a major military campaign against Hezbollah in Lebanon — preceded by the September 17-18 pager and radio sabotage attacks that killed dozens of Hezbollah members — involving heavy airstrikes on Beirut's southern suburbs, the south, and the Bekaa Valley, and a ground incursion. Lebanese authorities reported about 4,000 people killed and more than 16,000 wounded, with roughly 1.2 million people displaced, until a US-brokered ceasefire took effect on November 27.

12-29.title: Jeju Air Flight 2216 Crash
12-29.description: On December 29, 2024, Jeju Air Flight 2216, a Boeing 737-800 arriving from Bangkok, made an emergency belly landing and crashed into a concrete embankment at Muan International Airport, South Korea, exploding after a suspected bird strike and reported landing gear failure. All but two of the 181 people on board — 179 in total — were killed, making it the deadliest aviation disaster in South Korean history.

12-31.title: Israel–Hamas War: 2024 Death Toll in Gaza
12-31.description: During 2024, the Israel–Hamas war in the Gaza Strip continued with intense Israeli military operations and armed resistance, with the Gaza Ministry of Health reporting more than 45,600 Palestinians killed since October 2023 — roughly 25,000 of them during 2024 — while most of the territory's 2.1 million residents were repeatedly displaced and UN agencies warned of famine conditions and disease outbreaks. The conflict also involved continued rocket fire into Israel and expanding regional confrontation with Hezbollah and Iran.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

12-31.title: Russia–Ukraine War: 2024 Casualties
12-31.description: The Russia–Ukraine war entered its third year in 2024, with Russian offensives in eastern Ukraine, a Ukrainian incursion into Russia's Kursk region, and relentless artillery and drone strikes on cities including Kharkiv, Kyiv, and Odesa. Independent media documented more than 78,000 named Russian soldiers killed by December 2024 and estimated total military deaths on both sides at more than 100,000 during the year — making 2024 the war's deadliest — while the UN recorded about 1,300 civilian deaths in Ukraine in 2024 and more than 12,000 civilians killed since the February 2022 invasion.

03-10.title: Gamo Zone floods and landslides
03-10.description: On 10 March 2026, days of heavy rainfall in the Gamo Zone of South Ethiopia triggered widespread flash floods and landslides that killed at least 125 people. The disaster struck farming communities in the southern highlands, destroying homes, roads and farmland across multiple villages.

03-10.title: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crash
03-10.description: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 flying from Addis Ababa to Nairobi, crashed six minutes after takeoff on 10 March 2019, killing all 157 people on board, including 149 passengers and 8 crew from more than 30 countries. The crash bore close similarities to the Lion Air 737 MAX disaster five months earlier, and evidence of problems with the aircraft's automated MCAS flight-control system led authorities worldwide to ground the entire 737 MAX fleet for nearly two years.

03-14.title: Cyclone Idai
03-14.description: Cyclone Idai made landfall near the port city of Beira in central Mozambique on the night of 14-15 March 2019, bringing torrential rains and winds of up to 175 km/h that caused the Buzi and Pungwe rivers to burst their banks. More than 1,500 people died across Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Malawi and Madagascar, with the toll later confirmed at 1,593, and more than 2,000 people were reported missing. Hundreds of thousands were left stranded in floodwater, and the United Nations called it one of the worst weather-related disasters to hit the Southern Hemisphere.

03-23.title: Ogossagou massacre
03-23.description: On 23 March 2019, armed Dogon hunters attacked the Fulani herding village of Ogossagou in central Mali, killing 160 people, many of them women and children, and burning down the village. The massacre was one of the deadliest in Mali's recent history and followed a cycle of intercommunal violence between Dogon and Fulani communities that has been exploited by jihadist groups. Mali's government declared three days of national mourning and dissolved the local militia group accused of involvement.

04-21.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings
04-21.description: On Easter Sunday, 21 April 2019, a series of coordinated suicide bombings struck three churches and three luxury hotels in Colombo, Negombo and Batticaloa, with two further explosions occurring later in the day. A total of 269 people were killed, including dozens of foreign nationals, and more than 500 were injured, making it the deadliest act of violence in Sri Lanka since the end of the civil war. The Islamic State claimed responsibility, and investigations focused on the local group National Thowheeth Jama'ath and its links to international militant networks.

04-30.title: Idlib offensive (Syria)
04-30.description: On 30 April 2019, the Syrian government, backed by Russian air power, launched a ground offensive against opposition-held areas of Idlib Governorate, the last major rebel stronghold. Between April and August, the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights recorded at least 1,043 civilian deaths and roughly 3,000 combatant deaths, while the United Nations reported more than 500 civilians killed in the first months and hundreds of thousands of people displaced, including repeated attacks on schools, hospitals and camps for displaced people.

12-09.title: Whakaari/White Island eruption
12-09.location: Whakaari/White Island, Bay of Plenty, New Zealand
12-09.description: New Zealand's Whakaari/White Island volcano erupted without warning on 9 December 2019 while dozens of tourists and guides were on the island, which had been a popular day-trip destination. Twenty-two people, mostly Australian and American tourists, died from the blast or from injuries sustained in the eruption, including two whose bodies were never recovered, and 25 survivors were treated for severe burns. Criminal charges were later brought against tour operators and the island's owner over safety failures in the management of visits to the active volcano.

01-09.title: Chinagodrar military camp attack
01-09.description: Jihadist fighters, believed to belong to the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara, attacked a Nigerien army camp at Chinagodrar near the Mali border on 9 January 2020. The assault killed 89 soldiers, one of the deadliest attacks on the Nigerien military in its history, according to authorities and the French army, which supported the response. The attack highlighted the expansion of jihadist groups along Niger's western border.

02-08.title: Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) mall shooting
02-08.description: On 8-9 February 2020, Royal Thai Army Sergeant Major Jakrapanth Thomma stole weapons from his base and opened fire at the Terminal 21 Korat shopping mall, killing 29 people and wounding 58 before being shot dead by police, bringing the total death toll to 30 including the perpetrator. The rampage lasted about 17 hours and was the deadliest mass shooting in Thailand's history, with the attacker broadcasting live from the scene.

05-07.title: Visakhapatnam LG Polymers gas leak
05-07.description: In the early hours of 7 May 2020, styrene gas leaked from a sealed storage tank at the LG Polymers chemical plant on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, India. The National Disaster Response Force reported 13 deaths and more than 1,000 people sickened, with about 300 hospitalized, many of them villagers and workers asleep during the nationwide COVID-19 lockdown. The leak was compared to the 1984 Bhopal gas disaster and led to arrests of company officials.

08-27.title: Hurricane Laura
08-27.description: Hurricane Laura made landfall near Cameron, Louisiana on 27 August 2020 as a Category 4 storm with winds of 240 km/h, the strongest hurricane to hit the state since 1856. The storm killed 81 people in total across its path, including at least 41 in the United States (30 in Louisiana), 31 in Haiti and 9 in the Dominican Republic, and caused roughly $19 billion in damage. Storm surge and wind destroyed entire communities along the Gulf Coast of Louisiana and Texas.

11-02.title: Kabul University attack
11-02.description: On 2 November 2020, three gunmen from Islamic State Khorasan Province stormed Kabul University during an Iranian book fair, killing 32 people and wounding more than 50 in a siege that lasted several hours. The attackers, killed by security forces, brought the total death count including themselves to 35. The attack targeted students and academics and was one of the deadliest attacks on a university in Afghanistan's recent history.

11-11.title: Typhoon Vamco (Ulysses)
11-11.description: Typhoon Vamco, known locally as Ulysses, made landfall in Quezon province on 11 November 2020 as the third typhoon to strike the Philippines in two weeks. The storm caused severe flooding in Metro Manila and Cagayan Valley, killing 102 people with 10 more missing, according to the Philippine disaster agency. More than a million people were displaced, and the flooding in Cagayan was described as the worst in decades.
sources: NDRRMC (Philippines National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council)

04-11.title: Jilli market airstrike
04-11.description: On 11 April 2026, a Nigerian military airstrike hit a crowded market in Jilli, Yobe State, killing more than 100 civilians; authorities described the strike as a misfire. It was one of the deadliest airstrike incidents in Nigeria's counterinsurgency campaign in 2026 and drew calls for independent investigations into civilian casualties.

04-11.title: KwaZulu-Natal floods
04-11.description: Torrential rain on 11-13 April 2022 caused catastrophic flash floods and mudslides across KwaZulu-Natal province, South Africa, devastating the city of Durban and surrounding townships. The official death toll was 435, with thousands of homes destroyed, roads and bridges washed out, and critical water and electricity infrastructure severely damaged. It was one of the deadliest natural disasters in South Africa's recorded history.

03-04.title: Peshawar mosque bombing
03-04.description: On 4 March 2022, a suicide bomber detonated explosives during Friday prayers at a Shia mosque in Peshawar's Qissa Khwani Bazaar, Pakistan. At least 63 people were killed, including the attacker and five police officers, and nearly 200 were injured. The Islamic State Khorasan Province claimed responsibility for one of the deadliest attacks in Pakistan in years.

06-08.title: Mindanao earthquake
06-08.description: On 8 June 2026, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck offshore Sarangani province, Mindanao, on the Cotabato Trench, killing at least 106 people (107 per final tallies) and injuring 1,320, with 7 missing. More than 121,000 homes were damaged or destroyed and damage exceeded ₱71 billion (US$1.44 billion). General Santos, Sarangani, South Cotabato and Davao Occidental were hardest hit, and coastal uplift of up to 2 metres damaged marine habitats across Sarangani Bay.

01-28.title: Rubaya coltan mine collapse
01-28.location: Rubaya, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
01-28.description: On 28 January 2026, a landslide at the informal coltan mines in Rubaya, North Kivu, killed more than 400 miners and diggers, with some reports placing the toll higher. The collapse occurred amid a surge of artisanal mining in the conflict-affected region, and a second collapse at the same mines on 3 March 2026 killed at least 200 more people.

01-29.title: Balochistan Liberation Army attacks
01-29.description: Between 29 January and 5 February 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Army launched a coordinated series of attacks across Balochistan province, Pakistan, including raids on a police station and banks in Kharan, a security post in Panjgur and military positions in Harnai. The week-long campaign left at least 225 people dead, including 36 civilians and 2 security personnel, while Pakistani forces reported killing 216 militants in retaliatory raids.

01-29.title: Potomac River mid-air collision (American Airlines Flight 5342)
01-29.description: On January 29, 2025, American Airlines Flight 5342, a PSA Airlines regional jet arriving from Wichita, collided mid-air with a US Army Black Hawk helicopter over the Potomac River while on approach to Reagan Washington National Airport; all 67 people aboard both aircraft died, making it the deadliest US aviation accident since 2001.

01-29.title: Unity oilfield plane crash
01-29.description: On January 29, 2025, a Beechcraft 1900D operated by Eagle Air on behalf of Light Air Services crashed shortly after takeoff from the Unity oilfield airstrip in Unity State, South Sudan, while carrying oil workers to Juba; 20 of the 21 people on board were killed.

02-10.title: Tumbler Ridge school shooting
02-10.description: On 10 February 2026, an 18-year-old former student shot and killed her mother and 11-year-old half-brother at their home in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, then entered Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and shot six people before dying by suicide, for a total of nine dead and 27 injured. It was the deadliest mass shooting in Canada since the 2020 Nova Scotia attacks and the deadliest school shooting in the country since 1989.

01-19.title: Gaza war ceasefire
01-19.description: A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect on January 19, 2025, after 15 months of war in which the Gaza Health Ministry reported more than 47,000 Palestinians killed and most of the territory's population displaced. The first phase of the agreement included releases of hostages and prisoners before hostilities later resumed.

01-22.title: Antioch High School shooting
01-22.description: On January 22, 2025, 17-year-old Solomon Henderson opened fire in the cafeteria of Antioch High School in Nashville, Tennessee, fatally shooting one student and wounding another before killing himself with a self-inflicted gunshot; police said he fired ten rounds in about 17 seconds.

03-07.title: Bahia Blanca flash floods
03-07.description: On March 7-9, 2025, roughly 290 mm of rain fell within hours over Bahia Blanca, Argentina, triggering catastrophic flash flooding that killed at least 17 people and forced mass evacuations; the floods were described as the worst in the city's recorded history.

06-13.title: Israel-Iran war (Twelve-Day War)
06-13.description: On June 13, 2025, Israel launched Operation Rising Lion, striking Iranian military and nuclear facilities and killing commanders and nuclear scientists; Iran responded with more than 550 ballistic missiles and over 1,000 drones fired at Israel over 12 days. Roughly 33 people were killed in Israel and about 1,060 in Iran, according to the respective authorities.

07-29.title: Militant drone-and-ambush attack on police checkpoint in Hangu
07-29.description: Militants, blamed by police on the Pakistani Taliban (TTP), launched a drone strike and ambush on the Khazina Banda police checkpoint in Hangu district on the evening of July 29, 2026, in an assault that also involved an attack on a neighbouring checkpost. Eleven police officers, including a deputy superintendent of police, were killed as the death toll rose through the following morning, with initial reports citing 9 to 10 officers dead and at least 28 injured; authorities said 15 attackers were also killed in the ensuing gunfight. It was the second major assault on security forces in the area within a week amid escalating attacks in the Afghanistan–Pakistan border region.

07-29.title: US–Saudi airstrikes kill 20 Iran-backed militiamen in Iraq as US strikes on Iran resume
07-29.description: As part of the 2026 Iran war, US Central Command and Saudi forces carried out joint strikes on positions of Iran-backed militias in Iraq on July 29, 2026, killing 20 Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) militants, including several Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) members, according to the PMF. The same day, after a six-day pause, the US military resumed heavy waves of strikes against dozens of IRGC targets inside Iran in retaliation for an attempted missile attack on US forces in the Middle East a day earlier, an escalation that prompted Iranian retaliatory strikes on Kuwait days later.
sources: Wikipedia: July 2026 United States strikes against Iran

07-29.title: Wildfires in southern Greece kill three firefighters
07-29.location: Rethymno, Crete and Gytheio, Laconia, Greece
07-29.description: During a late-July heatwave that fuelled wildfires across southern Greece, three firefighters were killed on July 29, 2026 — two while battling a fire near Rethymno on the island of Crete and one near Gytheio in Laconia in the Peloponnese. The fires, part of the broader 2026 European heatwaves, forced the evacuation of thousands of people on Crete and destroyed farmland, olive groves and residential areas before crews brought the blazes under control in early August.

07-29.title: Firefighting helicopter crash in San Juan kills seven
07-29.description: A Bell 412 helicopter leased by Argentina's Federal Emergency Management Agency crashed on July 29, 2026, in the Ischigualasto natural park in San Juan Province while on a training flight before deployment to firefighting operations in the neighbouring La Rioja Province. The aircraft lost contact with ground control at about 10:26 a.m. local time, and all seven people on board — firefighters, police officers and civil protection personnel — were killed in the crash, which was one of Argentina's deadliest aviation accidents in years.

08-02.title: Israeli strikes kill 18 in Gaza
08-02.description: Israeli airstrikes and shelling continued across the Gaza Strip for a second straight day on Sunday, killing at least 18 Palestinians, including children, Gaza medics and civil defence officials said. Strikes hit multiple residential buildings, killed four people in Deir al-Balah and three near Saraya Square in Gaza City, and an Israeli minister said there was no deal to halt the attacks despite President Trump's announcement of a roadmap to implement the ceasefire agreement.

08-02.title: Firefighting helicopters collide in Greece killing two
08-02.description: Two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air on Sunday while battling a wind-driven wildfire west of Athens, and one caught fire and crashed. A Greek and a Danish crew member died; the two survivors — a Greek and a British national — were taken to hospital in Athens.

08-02.title: Suicide bombing at anti-militant rally kills 14 in Swat
08-02.description: A suicide bomber targeted protesters gathered outside a police station in Kabal, Swat, on Sunday, killing at least 14 people — including eight police officers — and wounding more than two dozen others, officials said. The rally was part of an anti-militant peace campaign in northwestern Pakistan.

08-02.title: Ukraine strikes deep inside Russia kill eight
08-02.description: Large-scale Ukrainian drone strikes on targets deep inside Russia on Sunday killed at least eight people, including at logistics warehouses of retailer Wildberries in the Moscow region. Russia said it shot down 635 UAVs overnight, and the acting governor of the border Belgorod region reported four dead in strikes on civilian areas.

08-02.title: Russian glide bombs kill one in Zaporizhzhia
08-02.description: Russian aircraft dropped eight glide bombs on residential districts of Zaporizhzhia within 90 minutes on Sunday evening, killing a 71-year-old woman, wounding 31 people — including a 16-year-old girl — and damaging 22 apartment buildings in four districts of the city.

08-02.title: Sudanese army drone strike on Darfur court kills 35
08-02.description: A drone strike attributed to the Sudanese Armed Forces hit a customary court in Al-Zawiya Gharra, west of Kabkabiya, North Darfur, on Sunday afternoon, killing at least 35 people during a court session. Medical sources and eyewitnesses later revised the death toll to more than 45, with dozens wounded and several missing.

08-16.title: Russian night attack on Kryvyi Rih kills one and injures six
08-16.description: Russian forces attacked Kryvyi Rih at night, killing one person and injuring six others, with two industrial enterprises catching fire and power outages reported across the city. Regional authorities said the attack caused fires and damage to civilian infrastructure.

08-16.title: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old Palestinian in Khan Younis
08-16.description: A 14-year-old Palestinian boy was killed by Israeli forces in Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip, with his body recovered after being shot, according to Palestinian sources. The killing came amid continued Israeli operations in Gaza despite the ceasefire framework agreed earlier in the year.

08-16.title: Historic flooding in Indiana kills seven
08-16.description: Days of severe storms and record-setting rainfall produced historic flooding across Indiana, killing at least seven people by August 16, with the White River cresting at record levels and the National Guard assisting rescues. Dozens of people were rescued from vehicles and homes as rivers overflowed across the state.

08-16.title: Shooting at Lexington, Kentucky park kills one and injures four
08-16.description: A shooting at a park in Lexington, Kentucky, during a live band performance killed one person and injured four others, including children, on August 16, according to authorities. Police said the victims included children and an investigation was under way.

08-16.title: Ukraine launches one of its largest aerial attacks of the war on Russia, killing at least six
08-16.location: Moscow region and other areas, Russia
08-16.description: Ukraine launched one of its largest aerial attacks of the war overnight on August 15-16, with Russia reporting it shot down more than 800 Ukrainian drones, including 187 over the Moscow region, in what TASS called the largest Ukrainian drone attack since the start of the year. At least six people were killed in Russia, and targets included warehouses and industrial plants as well as refineries.

08-16.title: Wildfires on Greek island of Salamina kill two and injure nine
08-16.description: Two bodies were found during firefighting operations on the Greek island of Salamina after a wildfire started around midday in a forested area of Peristeria on August 16; a second fire burned in the Selini area. Greek national broadcaster ERT, citing Fire Service sources, reported two dead and nine injured, with the identities of the victims not yet established.

08-17.title: Landslide hits apartment in Geoje, South Korea, killing one
08-17.location: Okpo-dong, Geoje, South Gyeongsang, South Korea
08-17.description: A landslide triggered by extreme rainfall hit a ground-floor apartment in Okpo-dong, Geoje, South Korea, at about 4:42 a.m. on August 17, killing one person found in cardiac arrest and leaving two others rescued, with a search for more underway. Geoje received more than 700 mm of rain over the three-day Liberation Day holiday, causing streams to overflow and emergency evacuation requests.
